rubrik: Expand tax on chemicals in certain electronics
dok_titel: GDP indexing of taxes on chemicals in certain electronics and waste incineration
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:11 by Linus Lakso and Emma Nohrén (both Green Party).
notis:
The Riksdag said no to the government's proposal to adjust two taxes in relation to the development of gross domestic product (GDP), so-called GDP indexing. The government's proposal concerns tax on chemicals in certain electronics and tax on waste incineration. The change that the government proposes would mean that the taxes are adjusted in view of both changes in the consumer price index (CPI) and the development of gross domestic product (GDP).
The Riksdag believes that the evaluations that have been made of the taxes have shown that they have not been sufficiently effective to achieve the goals that were the purpose of them. The Riksdag also points out that the government has proposed that the tax on waste incineration be abolished in January 2023. In light of this, the Riksdag said no to the government's proposal to recalculate these taxes based on GDP index.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:11 by Linus Lakso and Emma Nohrén (both Green Party).
Reservation 3

dok_titel: Freedom of association and terrorist organizations (dormant constitutional proposal)
forslag_text: The Riksdag finally adopts the dormant proposal in Annex 2 to the Act amending the Instrument of Government.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to a constitutional proposal that means expanded possibilities to through ordinary law restrict freedom of association for associations that engage in or support terrorism.
The proposal is a so-called dormant constitutional proposal, which means that the Riksdag has made a decision on the matter at an earlier time. To amend a constitutional law, it is required that the Riksdag votes in the same way twice on the proposal and there must be an election between the votes. The first decision on the proposal was made on 6 April 2022 and then the Riksdag voted yes.
The amendment to the law shall enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives: The Riksdag finally adopts the dormant proposal in Annex 2 to the Act amending the Instrument of Government.
Reservation 1

rubrik: Changes in the Code of Judicial Procedure
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the government's proposal for a law amending the Code of Judicial Procedure in the parts that concern Chapter 27, Section 2, and adopts the bill otherwise with the change that
a) Chapter 27, Sections 18, 20 d and 33 shall have the wording that the committee proposes in Annex 4, 
b) the preamble shall have the wording that follows from this. 
Thereby the Riksdag partially grants proposition 2021/22:55 point 4.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposals for amendments to law and constitutional amendments. The constitutional amendments are a so-called dormant proposal, which means that the Riksdag has made a decision on that part at an earlier time.
The bills mean, among other things, that foreign espionage, serious foreign espionage and serious unauthorized handling of secret information based on foreign espionage are criminalized and incorporated into the Criminal Code.
The Riksdag also said yes to the dormant proposal for amendments to the two constitutional laws the Press Freedom Ordinance and the Fundamental Law on Freedom of Expression. The amendments mean, among other things, that foreign espionage as well as the forms of unauthorized handling of secret information and negligence with secret information that are based on foreign espionage also become criminalized as press and freedom of expression crimes.
The amendments to the law also involve restrictions on the right to communicate and the right to obtain information, that is the right to communicate and obtain information for publication in constitutionally protected media forms.
Since the proposal in certain parts concerns amendments to constitutional laws, it is required that the Riksdag votes in the same way twice and there must be an election between the votes. The first decision on the constitutional proposal was made on 6 April 2022 and then the Riksdag voted yes. After that there has been a Riksdag election.
The amendments to the law enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the government's proposal for a law amending the Code of Judicial Procedure in the parts that concern Chapter 27, Section 2, and adopts the bill otherwise with the change that
a) Chapter 27, Sections 18, 20 d and 33 shall have the wording that the committee proposes in Annex 4, 
b) the preamble shall have the wording that follows from this. 
Thereby the Riksdag partially grants proposition 2021/22:55 point 4.

lays document 2021/22:247 on the table.
notis:
In a document, the former government accounts for the work on implementing Agenda 2030 and the global goals for sustainable development that the UN General Assembly adopted in 2015.
The document is a consequence of parliament issuing a formal request (tillkännagivande) to the government to submit a report every other year on the implementation and achievement of the Agenda 2030 goals. The document now submitted is the first of its kind.
In the document, the former government assesses that 35 of the 169 sub-targets for achieving Agenda 2030 have been fully achieved, or have been achieved within Sweden.
For 60 of the sub-targets, the former government assesses that further measures are needed. For 21 of the sub-targets, data was lacking to make an assessment.
Parliament welcomes the document and notes that much progress has been made regarding the goals, both in Sweden and globally. Furthermore, Parliament notes that Sweden has a good starting position and better conditions to achieve the global goals than many other countries. Parliament believes, however, that there is a considerable way to go for Sweden before the goals are fulfilled.
Parliament laid the document on the table, that is, closed the matter.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2022/23:29 by Ulrika Westerlund (MP) demands 1-3.
notis:
Parliament has addressed the government's statement on the administration of the General Inheritance Fund and how the Inheritance Fund Delegation has distributed funds from the fund during 2021.
Parliament agrees with the government that funds from the General Inheritance Fund have been distributed in a good way and in line with the fund's purpose and prioritized areas.
Also during the Covid-19 pandemic, the government argues that the Inheritance Fund Delegation mainly succeeded in fulfilling its assignment, even though applications decreased during 2021. With the decrease among other things as background, the government considers it important to continue the work of increasing awareness and knowledge about the inheritance fund. Parliament shares the government's assessment that there is a continued need to increase the number of applications throughout the country and that the positive results that the projects generate are spread nationally.
The capital of the General Inheritance Fund comes mainly from inheritances from people who die without leaving a spouse or closer relatives than cousins and have not willed the property to anyone else.
The Inheritance Fund Delegation is the authority that, among other things, makes decisions on and follows up the projects that receive funds from the General Inheritance Fund.
Parliament said no to one motion in this area and thereby filed the statement with the records, that is, closed the matter.

rubrik: Changes in the new Riksbank Act
dok_titel: A new Riksbank Act (pending constitutional proposals, etc.)
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2021/22:4297 by Mia Sydow Mölleby et al. (V) demands 1-3.
notis:
Parliament said yes to pending proposals for amendments to the Instrument of Government and the Rules of Procedure of the Riksdag concerning the Riksbank and to the government's proposal for a new Riksbank Act. The proposals for amendments to the Instrument of Government and the Rules of Procedure are so-called pending proposals, which means that parliament has made a decision on the matter at an earlier occasion. The amendments to the Instrument of Government include, among other things, a clarification of the Riksbank's tasks. The proposal for amendment to the Rules of Procedure means that it will be clear that parliament's Finance Committee shall follow up and evaluate the Riksbank's activities.
Parliament also said yes to the government's proposal for a new Riksbank Act, but with some minor changes. The new Riksbank Act includes, among other things:

The objectives, tasks and powers of the Riksbank are clarified with regard to monetary policy, the financial system, means of payment, peacetime crisis situations and enhanced preparedness, and international activities
It will become clearer how the Riksbank's areas of responsibility relate to each other and the areas of responsibility of the Financial Supervisory Authority and the National Debt Office
It will become clearer that the Riksbank within the framework of monetary policy shall take real economic considerations, and conditions are created for democratic anchoring of the specification of the price stability target
The basis of the Riksbank's organization is maintained, but the number of members of the Board is reduced from six to five. A more appropriate distribution of responsibilities is introduced between the Riksbank's Full Assembly, the Board and the Governor of the Riksbank
The Riksbank's position as an independent central bank and independent administrative authority is strengthened
The Riksbank's financial independence is strengthened within the framework of, for example, disposing of profits and structuring own capital as well as borrowing for the currency reserve
The conditions for transparency and review of the Riksbank's activities increase
The Riksbank shall contribute to sustainable development on the financial market.

Since the proposals in some respects concern amendments to the Instrument of Government and the Rules of Procedure of the Riksdag, it is required that parliament votes the same way twice and there must be an election between the votes. The first decision on the proposals was made on 1 June 2022 and then parliament voted yes. Subsequently, there has been a parliamentary election.
All law changes will enter into force 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion 

2021/22:4297 by Mia Sydow Mölleby et al. (V) demands 1-3.

rubrik: The future regulation of dispute resolution procedures
dok_titel: An independent dispute resolution procedure for collective rental disputes
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2022/23:13 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (V) demands 1 and 2.
notis:
The previous government has presented a proposal for dispute resolution in certain collective rental negotiations. This includes, among other things, a new independent dispute resolution body for the entire rental market and stricter rules for rental negotiations.
The parties on the rental market conduct regular collective negotiations on the general rent level. Such negotiations are often called annual rental negotiations. When these negotiations drag on, it can pose economic risks for the parties involved.
Within the public housing stock there is currently a dispute resolution body, the Rental Market Committee (HMK). Now a corresponding solution is to be introduced for the entire rental market, even for the private housing stock. If the parties do not agree on the annual rent increase, a special arbitrator can be appointed to hear the dispute. The purpose is to streamline collective negotiations and to enable annual rental negotiations to be resolved faster.
Stricter rules for rental negotiation meetings are also introduced. Among other things, a party can be liable for damages if they do not show up to a negotiation meeting that is to be held within a certain time.
Parliament said yes to the proposal. The new rules enter into force 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion 

2022/23:13 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (V) demands 1 and 2.
Reservation 1

rubrik: Allocation of Coordination Numbers to Asylum Seekers
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:16 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) amendment 2.
notis:
The Riksdag supports the proposal for a new law on coordination numbers and also changes to, among other things, the population registration act and the population registration database act. The purpose is to strengthen the system for coordination numbers by, for example, increasing the requirements for identity checks that are carried out before a coordination number is given to a person.
A coordination number is an identity designation for persons who are not or have not been registered in the Swedish population register, but who still need to have contact with Swedish authorities or other parts of society. Persons registered in the Swedish population register are assigned a national identity number instead.
Coordination numbers are divided into different levels depending on which identity check has been performed. Today there are two levels. Under the new law, a coordination number can be given at three different levels. To obtain the highest level, the person must be able to prove their identity with valid identity documents and also personally present themselves at the time of application. Identity documents can also be requested for verification of biometric data stored in these documents.
The proposal also means that the Swedish Tax Agency takes over responsibility for, among other things, identity checks when a coordination number is to be assigned to a person. Other authorities shall notify the Swedish Tax Agency if it can be assumed that information is incorrect in the population registration database concerning persons with a coordination number.
The proposal also contains a limitation of the exemption from population registration that applies to persons who are locally employed at foreign embassies or consulates in Sweden.
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.
The legislative changes concerning locally employed staff at embassies and consulates shall enter into force on 1 January 2023 and others on 1 September 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:16 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) amendment 2.
Reservation 2

dok_titel: Copyright in the Digital Internal Market
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:27 by Elin Söderberg and Amanda Lind (both MP) amendment 3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for amendments to, among other things, the Copyright Act. The proposals are based on an EU directive and contain new rules concerning adapting copyright to digital development.
As digital technology enables new forms of use of copyright-protected material, Swedish copyright legislation needs to be modernized. The government's proposal includes, among other things, limitations on copyright to facilitate education and research, but also so that cultural heritage can be preserved. In addition, it includes new provisions allowing free reproduction of older works of art.
The proposal also means that news companies can receive compensation when their material is reused on the internet. There are also new provisions regulating liability when users themselves upload material on various digital platforms. Providers of these services and platforms shall enter into agreements with rights holders who wish to do so, but shall also be obligated to take action when material is uploaded against the wishes of the rights holder.
Finally, a number of rules are introduced to strengthen the contractual position of authors when they transfer their rights to publishers, producers, newspapers or other actors on the copyright market.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:27 by Elin Söderberg and Amanda Lind (both MP) amendment 3.
Reservation 4

rubrik: Court Processing Times in Asylum Cases

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2022/23:24 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) amendments 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a statement from the government concerning the National Audit Office's review of processing times in asylum cases at Sweden's migration courts.
The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the handling has efficiency shortcomings and that the migration courts are far from meeting the goal of deciding 90 per cent of asylum cases within four months. The National Audit Office also submitted recommendations to the National Courts Administration and the government regarding measures for shorter processing times.
In its statement, the government concurs with the National Audit Office's findings and at the same time points to measures that have been taken and that the government will follow up.
The Riksdag assumes that the government will follow up the measures and that the National Courts Administration will continue its efficiency work. With this, the Riksdag filed the government's statement, that is to say closed the matter.

The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:16 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) amendment 4.
notis:
The Riksdag supports the proposal for a new law on coordination numbers and also changes to, among other things, the population registration act and the population registration database act. The purpose is to strengthen the system for coordination numbers by, for example, increasing the requirements for identity checks that are carried out before a coordination number is given to a person.
A coordination number is an identity designation for persons who are not or have not been registered in the Swedish population register, but who still need to have contact with Swedish authorities or other parts of society. Persons registered in the Swedish population register are assigned a national identity number instead.
Coordination numbers are divided into different levels depending on which identity check has been performed. Today there are two levels. Under the new law, a coordination number can be given at three different levels. To obtain the highest level, the person must be able to prove their identity with valid identity documents and also personally present themselves at the time of application. Identity documents can also be requested for verification of biometric data stored in these documents.
The proposal also means that the Swedish Tax Agency takes over responsibility for, among other things, identity checks when a coordination number is to be assigned to a person. Other authorities shall notify the Swedish Tax Agency if it can be assumed that information is incorrect in the population registration database concerning persons with a coordination number.
The proposal also contains a limitation of the exemption from population registration that applies to persons who are locally employed at foreign embassies or consulates in Sweden.
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.
The legislative changes concerning locally employed staff at embassies and consulates shall enter into force on 1 January 2023 and others on 1 September 2023.

rubrik: Other matters regarding implementation of the directive
dok_titel: Copyright on the digital internal market
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion

2022/23:20 by Lorena Delgado Varas et al. (V) claims 2-5.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal on amendments to, among others, the copyright act. The proposals are based on an EU directive and contain new rules aimed at adapting copyright to digital development.
As digital technology enables new forms of use of copyright-protected material, Swedish copyright legislation needs to be modernized. The government's proposal includes, among other things, limitations on copyright to facilitate education and research, but also to preserve cultural heritage. Furthermore, it introduces new provisions allowing the free reproduction of older works of art.
The proposal also means that newspaper companies can receive compensation when their material is reused on the internet. There will also be new provisions governing liability when users themselves upload material on various digital platforms. Providers of these services and platforms must enter into agreements with rights holders who wish it, but are also obliged to act when material is uploaded against the rights holder's will.
Finally, a number of rules are introduced to strengthen the contractual position of authors when they transfer their rights to publishers, producers, newspapers or other actors in the copyright market.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 January 2023.

notis:
Parliament has considered a letter from the government. The letter concerns the Swedish National Audit Office's examination of digital doctor's visits and hired doctors in the sickness certification process.
The Swedish National Audit Office's overall conclusion shows that there are deficiencies in certain control functions during the sickness certification process. In the report, the Swedish National Audit Office recommends that the government draw up clear national guidelines for medical certificates issued on the basis of a digital doctor's visit.
The government largely agrees with the Swedish National Audit Office and refers in the letter to the National Board of Health and Welfare's ongoing work on the matter. Parliament placed the letter among the records, that is, closed the matter.

rubrik: Guidelines for economic and fiscal policy
forslag_text:
Parliament approves the guidelines for economic and fiscal policy proposed by the government.
Thus Parliament approves proposition 2022/23:1 financial plan point 1 and rejects the motions

2022/23:1299 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) claim 1,

2022/23:2074 by Magdalena Andersson et al. (S) claim 1,

2022/23:2180 by Annie Lööf et al. (C) claim 1 and

2022/23:2275 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) claim 1.
notis:
The government has proposed expenditure ceilings and revenue estimates for the state budget in the budget proposal for 2023. Expenditures are estimated at 1,195 billion kronor and revenues are estimated at 1,279 billion kronor. This means a surplus in the state budget of 84 billion kronor for 2023. The expenditure ceiling for the state is 1,665 billion kronor for 2023, 1,745 billion for 2024 and 1,825 billion for 2025.
The budget proposal also contains proposals on tax and fee rules that include

enhanced earned income tax credit for persons over 65 years
increased tax on alcohol and tobacco
enhanced tax reduction for installation of solar cells
temporary reduction in tax on fuel
reduced tax on fuels in certain heat production
maintained travel deduction with certain enhancements for work trips, business trips and return trips.

Some of these proposals have been presented in separate propositions, but are announced in the budget proposal and are included in the calculations of revenues in the budget.
Parliament approved the government's proposal on the frameworks for the state budget for 2023. Parliament's decision on the frameworks for the state budget is then governing when Parliament in the next step decides on appropriations for the 27 expenditure areas in the budget.
All legislative changes enter into force on 1 January 2023 except the decisions concerning abolished tax reduction for server halls and a clearer chemical tax, which enter into force on 1 July 2023. As regards increased tax on alcohol and tobacco, the legislative changes enter into force on 1 January 2023 and 1 January 2024 respectively.
Parliament also approved the government's direction for economic and fiscal policy.
GDP developed relatively strongly during the first half of 2022, but development is expected to weaken in the future. Growth is expected to be negative next year and the Swedish economy is expected to be in a low-growth period in 2023. Fiscal policy should be mildly contractionary in order not to counteract monetary policy in a situation where high inflation could take hold.
Policy should in the near term be focused on measures that support companies and households that are pressured by rising prices. This includes, among other things, a temporary high-cost protection for electricity costs and an extension of the temporary additional allowance for families with children receiving housing assistance. Temporary tax reductions on fuel are to alleviate the consequences for those dependent on cars in rural areas and for companies in agriculture and forestry. General government grants to municipalities and regions are strengthened.
Parliament made a decision in the matter despite the fact that it was available for less than two working days before the day it was dealt with, which is the usual procedure.

notis:
In total, approximately 94 billion kronor from the state budget for 2023 goes to the expenditure area for defense and society's crisis preparedness. Parliament said yes to the government's proposal in the budget proposition concerning defense and crisis preparedness. Parliament shares the government's view that the deteriorated security situation requires accelerating the rearmament of total defense.
Parliament approved the government's so-called procurement authorizations (bemyndiganden) within the defense appropriation covering the period 2024–2031. Through these authorizations, parliament gives the government the opportunity to instruct the authorities to carry out various long-term public investments, for example to acquire defense materiel. The authorization the government receives is a total of 173 billion kronor.
Parliament decides the state budget in two steps. First, the framework for the 27 expenditure areas in the budget is decided. Parliament decided this on 13 December 2022. Subsequently, parliament in a second step determines how the money shall be allocated within each expenditure area. This decision concerns step two in the decision process.

2022/23:1228 by Ida Gabrielsson et al. (V) demand 3.
notis:
In total, 106.4 billion kronor from the state budget for 2023 goes to the expenditure area Economic Security in Illness and Disability. Parliament said yes to the government's proposal.
Most money, 45.6 billion kronor, goes to sick leave and rehabilitation and 45.4 billion kronor goes to activity and sickness benefits. Försäkringskassan (Swedish Social Insurance Agency) receives just over 9 billion kronor.
Parliament said yes to the government's proposal to extend the temporary exemption from certain assessments of sick leave benefits in case of deferred care or rehabilitation until the end of 2023.
Parliament also said yes to the government's proposal on authorizations (bemyndiganden), powers, and economic commitments. At the same time, parliament said no to motions with alternative budget proposals.
Parliament decides the state budget in two steps. First, the framework for the 27 expenditure areas in the budget is decided. Parliament decided this on 13 December 2022. Subsequently, parliament in a second step determines how the money shall be allocated within each expenditure area. This decision concerns step two in the decision process.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the motion

2022/23:1228 by Ida Gabrielsson et al. (V) demand 3.

forslag_text:

In total, it concerns approximately 6.1 billion kronor from the state budget for 2023. Most money, just over 4.3 billion, goes to investment support for arranging rental housing and housing for students. This money shall be used to pay out support to everyone who has been granted support before 31 December 2022. The investment support is being phased out since the 2021/22 year end, and after 31 December this year no applications will be approved. Approximately 721 million goes to Lantmäteriet (National Land Survey of Sweden), 350 million goes to energy efficiency improvements of multi-family housing. The support for energy efficiency improvements is also being phased out since the 2021/22 year end. Approximately 288 million goes to Boverket (National Board of Housing, Building and Planning) and approximately 171 million goes to Konsumentverket (Swedish Consumer Agency).
Parliament also said yes to the government's proposal on certain authorizations (bemyndiganden) on economic commitments. At the same time, parliament said no to alternative budget proposals in motions and other proposals in motions from the general motion period 2022.
Parliament decides the state budget in two steps. First, the framework for the 27 expenditure areas in the budget is decided. Parliament decided this on 13 December 2022. Subsequently, parliament in a second step determines how the money shall be allocated within each expenditure area. This decision concerns step two in the decision process.

rubrik: Subsidiarity Assessment of the Commission's Proposal for a Regulation Establishing a Crisis Instrument for the Internal Market
dok_titel: Subsidiarity Assessment of the Commission's Proposal for a Regulation Establishing a Crisis Instrument for the Internal Market
forslag_text: Parliament decides to submit a reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande) to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council, and the Commission with the wording that appears in the committee's proposal in Appendix 2.
notis:
Parliament has examined a legislative proposal from the EU Commission concerning the introduction of an instrument aimed at ensuring that the internal market within the EU, that is the free movement of persons, goods and services, functions well even in crisis situations. The proposal also contains provisions to secure access to goods and services that are of strategic importance, which according to the proposal is defined as goods and services that are absolutely necessary for the internal market and that cannot be replaced or diversified.
The proposal has been examined according to the so-called subsidiarity principle (subsidiaritetsprincipen), which states that the EU shall only legislate on a matter if the objectives of the planned action cannot be better or equally well achieved by the member states themselves.
Parliament believes that the proposal is not in all respects compatible with the subsidiarity principle. According to parliament, there is a need to clarify how the provisions concerning goods and services of strategic importance relate to the legal basis that is stated. Parliament therefore decided to submit objections to the European Parliament, the Council, and the EU Commission in what is called a reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande).
alternatives: Parliament decides to submit a reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande) to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council, and the Commission with the wording that appears in the committee's proposal in Appendix 2.

rubrik: The purpose of the temporary tax
dok_titel: A temporary tax on extraordinary profits for certain companies during 2023
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion

2022/23:2297 by Helena Lindahl et al. (C).
notis:
To handle the rapidly rising energy prices, the EU has decided on a so-called solidarity contribution. The idea is that companies within the union that deal with fossil fuels and make large profits shall pay a solidarity contribution.
The money shall be used by the member states to be able to pay out financial support to individuals and companies that have been severely affected by high energy prices. In Sweden, the government proposes a temporary tax on extraordinary profits for certain companies in the fossil fuel sector. The temporary tax shall correspond to the EU's solidarity contribution and shall be levied during 2023.
Parliament approved the government's proposal on a temporary tax that shall alleviate the consequences of high energy prices. The temporary law comes into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion

2022/23:2297 by Helena Lindahl et al. (C).

rubrik: Conditions when regions enter into agreements with private healthcare providers
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the government's proposal for a law on amendments to the Health and Medical Care Act (2017:30) in the parts concerning Chapter 15, Section 2 and point 2 of the entry-into-force and transitional provisions.
Thereby Parliament approves the motions

2022/23:5 by Camilla Waltersson Grönvall et al. (M, SD, KD, L) and

2022/23:8 by Anders W Jonsson (C) and

rejects Bill 2021/22:260 point 2 in this respect.
notis:
Parliament rejected the government's proposal on changed conditions when regions enter into agreements with private healthcare providers that also have insurance companies as clients. The government's proposal concerns amendments to the Health and Medical Care Act and means that it shall be stated in the agreement how it is ensured that the private healthcare provider's other assignments do not have a negative impact on the care provided on behalf of the region.
Parliament approved the proposal in the Health and Medical Care Act that rehabilitation shall be included in primary care's core assignment.
Parliament approved the proposal to amend the Patient Safety Act, which means that the Inspectorate for Care Services (Ivo) shall be able to issue a föreläggande (binding order), that is, instruct, a healthcare provider that has not registered itself with Ivo's healthcare register to do so. Such a föreläggande may be accompanied by a vite (penalty fee), that is, a fine.
The amendments to the Patient Safety Act come into force on 1 July 2023. The amendment to the Health and Medical Care Act comes into force on 1 January 2024.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the government's proposal for a law on amendments to the Health and Medical Care Act (2017:30) in the parts concerning Chapter 15, Section 2 and point 2 of the entry-into-force and transitional provisions.

rubrik: Secrecy at the Swedish Social Insurance Agency for information used to identify electrical facilities in matters on support for electricity users
dok_titel: Secrecy in the Swedish Social Insurance Agency's handling of matters on electricity support and abolished reporting obligation
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for a law on amendments to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (2009:400) in the parts concerning Chapter 28, Section 4 b.
Thereby Parliament approves Bill 2022/23:48 point 1 in this respect and rejects the motions

2022/23:2304 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) in this respect,

2022/23:2305 by Malin Björk et al. (C) in this respect and

2022/23:2306 by Per Bolund et al. (MP) in this respect.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal that secrecy shall apply when the Swedish Social Insurance Agency handles matters on electricity support for electricity users. Secrecy shall apply to electricity users' personal circumstances and to information used to identify electrical facilities. If it is clear that the information can be disclosed without leading to an individual suffering harm, secrecy shall not apply.
Parliament also approved the proposal to remove the Swedish Social Insurance Agency's obligation to provide information reports to the Tax Agency in matters on electricity support for electricity users.
The amendments to the law come into force on 1 February 2023.

The government also notes that a number of government agencies, including the county administrative boards, according to their appropriation directions for 2022 are to report how they have contributed to the implementation of regional development policy and the coordinated rural policy.
The Riksdag has also taken a position on a number of motion proposals that address, among other things, commercial services in rural areas, location of government agencies and return of funds and production values from natural resources.
The Riksdag rejected all motion proposals with reference to ongoing work and filed the government's letter, that is, closed the case.

rubrik: The Swedish National Audit Office's report on the annual reallocation of agency appropriations
dok_titel: The Swedish National Audit Office's report on the annual reallocation of agency appropriations
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2022/23:10 by Janine Alm Ericson (MP) and

2022/23:1299 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) clause 9 and

files memorandum 2021/22:241 in the records.
notis:
The Riksdag notes that the legitimacy of the annual reallocation of agency appropriations rests on it being transparent and predictable and therefore views positively that the government continuously works to increase transparency both in the model itself and in information about price and wage reallocation.
Every year, agencies receive appropriations from the state budget to, among other things, finance wages and premises. Before each new budget year, the Ministry of Finance reallocates the appropriations so that agencies are not affected by price and wage increases in the outside world.
The model for price and wage reallocation (also called PLO) was introduced approximately 30 years ago and the calculation is done automatically so that the state's role as employer is kept separate from the government's political priorities. For agencies to achieve productivity development at the level of the private service sector, a so-called productivity reduction is made.
It is due to the National Audit Office's review of the PLO and productivity reduction that the government has submitted a memorandum. The review shows, among other things, that the built-in requirement for productivity has functioned as a steering signal for efficiency and that it has not prevented agencies from carrying out their tasks.
The Riksdag filed the government's memorandum, that is, concluded the matter.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2022/23:10 by Janine Alm Ericson (MP) and

2022/23:1299 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) clause 9 and

files memorandum 2021/22:241 in the records.

notis:
The National Audit Office has examined the government's organization, governance and monitoring of regional development policy. An overarching finding is that the government's handling has created weak conditions for effective coordinated government action to achieve the policy's goals.
Following the examination, the government submitted a letter stating that it partially agrees with the National Audit Office's findings and will consider the agency's recommendations in continued work. The government also emphasizes that several government agencies, including the county administrative boards, according to their appropriation directions for 2022 should report how they have contributed to the implementation of regional development policy and the integrated rural policy.
Parliament has also taken positions on a number of motion proposals dealing with, for example, commercial services in rural areas, location of government agencies and return of funds and production values from natural resources.
Parliament voted no to all motion proposals, citing ongoing work, and placed the government's letter on file—that is, concluded the matter.

dok_titel: National Audit Office report on the state's supervision of pharmacies and wholesale trade in medicines
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2022/23:2287 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V) and

2022/23:2292 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) amendment points 1 and 2.
notis:
Parliament has considered a letter from the government concerning the National Audit Office's examination of the Medical Products Agency's supervision of outpatient pharmacies and wholesale trade in medicines. The report covers supervision by the Medical Products Agency, the Inspectorate for Healthcare and Care Services (Ivo) and the Dental and Pharmaceutical Benefits Agency (TLV).
The National Audit Office's conclusion is that the supervision that the state conducts over the pharmacy sector and trade in medicines is not effective. This can lead to both pharmacies and those who buy and sell medicines risking operating businesses that do not meet legal requirements. The consequence can then be that patient safety suffers and costs to the state and regions become unnecessarily large.
In the letter, the government welcomes the examination and is positive to several of the proposals for measures that the National Audit Office provides. Among other things, the government believes there is reason to consider whether regulations should be introduced that prevent pharmacies from charging excessive prices on medicines that are not included in the pharmaceutical benefits but are subsidized by the state or regions and on special food for children.
Parliament largely agrees with the government's assessments and believes that it is central that supervision can be conducted effectively. With this, parliament placed the letter on file—that is, concluded the matter.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the motions

2022/23:2287 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V) and

2022/23:2292 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) amendment points 1 and 2.

The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for a law amending the Value Added Tax Act (1994:200).
Thereby, the Riksdag grants proposition 2022/23:35 and rejects the motions 

2022/23:2308 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) and 

2022/23:2312 by Marielle Lahti et al. (MP).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal for increased VAT on repairs of bicycles, shoes, leather goods, clothing and household linen from 6 percent to 12 percent. The purpose is to increase uniformity in the tax system. 
Through the proposed tax increase, the difference in tax collection becomes smaller between these repair services and other repair services covered by the standard tax rate of 25 percent. The Government considers VAT to be an effective tax that should be protected as a revenue source for the state and that therefore the starting point should be uniform VAT and application of the standard tax rate.
The new rules come into force on April 1, 2023.

dok_titel: Supplementary Budget for 2023 - Temporary Tax on Certain Electricity Producers' Excess Income
forslag_text:
Changes to the state budget for 2023
The Riksdag approves changed calculation of revenues in the state budget for 2023 according to the Government's proposal.
Thereby, the Riksdag grants proposition 2022/23:58 point 3.

Legislation forming the basis for changes to the state budget
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for
1. law on tax on excess income from electricity,
2. law amending the Tax Administration Act (2011:1244).
Thereby, the Riksdag grants proposition 2022/23:58 points 1 and 2.

Future additions to the Government's legislation proposal

The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:2332 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) claims 1-3, 

2022/23:2334 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S) claims 1 and 2, 

2022/23:2335 by Martin Ådahl and Rickard Nordin (both C) and 

2022/23:2336 by Marielle Lahti and Annika Hirvonen (both MP).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal for a new law, which enables a temporary tax on excess income from certain electricity production. The proposal means that revenues over 1,957 kronor per megawatt-hour will be taxed at 90 percent, during the period March-June 2023. The proposal was submitted in the form of a supplementary budget for 2023.
The proposal is based on an EU regulation, which contains several measures to address high energy prices in Europe. One of the measures is a so-called temporary ceiling for excess income from electricity production. Member states may decide on the exact level of the ceiling, within a certain range.
The temporary tax applies to electricity producers with an installed capacity over 1 megawatt. Primarily, wind power and nuclear power will be affected. The tax is estimated to increase the state's revenues by 362 million kronor during 2023. The law comes into force on March 1, 2023.

rubrik: Future regulation of agricultural land acquisition legislation
dok_titel: Changes to agricultural land acquisition law to prevent circumvention of acquisition permit requirements
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion

2022/23:985 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) request 43.
notis:
Parliament agreed with the government's proposal for changes to agricultural land acquisition law. The law changes mean that the definition of agricultural property is expanded to include not only real property that is assessed as an agricultural unit but also real property that has been converted or newly established for the purpose of agriculture or forestry but has not yet been subject to property taxation.
One of the purposes of agricultural land acquisition law is to maintain balance in land ownership between individuals and legal entities with regard to agricultural properties. Therefore, a so-called förvärvstillstånd (acquisition permit) is required when legal entities such as a company wish to acquire an agricultural property.
The narrow definition of what constitutes agricultural property has in some noted cases allowed legal entities to acquire property from individuals without the provisions on acquisition permits becoming applicable. This is why the government believes the rules should be changed.
The new rules are proposed to come into force on 15 April 2023.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion

2022/23:985 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) request 43.

2022/23:1 by Lotta Johnsson Fornarve et al. (V) proposals 3, 4, 6 and 7 and

notis:
Every other year, the government submits a memorandum with a consolidated report of development cooperation and humanitarian aid through multilateral organisations. That is, support to international organisations, such as various UN bodies.
In the memorandum focusing on the years 2019 and 2020, it appears that aid channelled through multilateral organisations increased significantly during that period. From approximately 59 per cent of the Swedish aid budget in 2019 to approximately 67 per cent in 2020.
The Riksdag filed the memorandum with the documents, that is, closed the case.
At the same time, the Riksdag said no to follow-up motions and eight proposals in motions from the general motion period 2022 concerning multilateral aid. This with reference to ongoing work.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag
a) approves
1. Sweden's accession to the North Atlantic Treaty,
2. the agreement on the status of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, national representatives and the organisation's international personnel,
b) adopts the Government's proposal for an amendment to the Act (1976:661) on immunity and privileges in certain cases.
Thereby the Riksdag grants proposition 2022/23:74 points 1-3 and rejects the motions

2022/23:2348 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V) demands 1 in this part and 2 and

2022/23:2349 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) demands 1 in this part and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag approved Sweden's accession to the North Atlantic Treaty and the agreement on the status of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, NATO. The status agreement regulates immunity and privileges for NATO and certain personnel categories. The Riksdag also approved the Government's proposal for legislative amendments.
In connection with the application to NATO, changes are required in two laws. The Act on operational military support and the Act on immunity and privileges in certain cases. The amendments to the laws aim partly to facilitate Sweden's ability to request support from NATO in the form of military forces, and partly to provide NATO, the national representatives and the international personnel with the immunity and privileges required under the agreement.
With regard to the decision on the Act on operational military support, the decision must be made with at least a three-fourths majority and more than half of the Riksdag members must vote in favour of the proposal. This is according to the Government of Sweden Act as the decision concerns the transfer of authority to another state.
The amendments to the laws shall enter into force on the day determined by the Government.

dok_titel: National Audit Office's report School Money – efficiency and consequences
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions 

2022/23:610 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) demand 5, 

2022/23:884 by Muharrem Demirok et al. (C) demand 32, 

2022/23:2128 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S) demand 4, 

2022/23:2313 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S) demands 1-4 and 

2022/23:2318 by Muharrem Demirok et al. (C) demands 1-4.
notis:
The National Audit Office's examination of school money for independent schools shows that the rules on compensation to private providers in some respects counteract an equitable school and therefore need to be changed. In a letter, the government states that it essentially agrees with the conclusions of the examination and that the issues should be investigated. Parliament places the government's letter in the files, that is, closes the matter.
School money is the sum of money that a student generates to the provider who is responsible for the student's education. The National Audit Office believes that the current rules make it difficult for providers to plan their activities and achieve effective resource distribution. Therefore, it recommends the government to ensure that a government-determined formula model for compensation to private providers is introduced.
Furthermore, the National Audit Office recommends the government to review the regulations on substantial negative consequences when establishing independent schools, so that it becomes clear what is meant.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the motions 

2022/23:610 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) demand 5, 

2022/23:884 by Muharrem Demirok et al. (C) demand 32,

dok_titel: Enhanced Opportunities for the Swedish Tax Agency to Conduct Data Analyses and Selections in Population Register Activities
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:123 by Anna Vikström (S), 

2022/23:292 by Jan Ericson (M), 

2022/23:961 by Magnus Persson et al. (SD) proposal 10 and 

2022/23:1022 by Per Söderlund et al. (SD) proposal 27.
notis:
The Swedish Tax Agency should be given better opportunities to reduce the amount of errors and fraud in the population register. This is to counteract crime directed at, among other things, the welfare systems. The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal.
Through the legislative changes, the Swedish Tax Agency will be able to process personal data to conduct data analyses and selections in order to prevent, avoid, and detect incorrect information in the population register. The Agency should focus on areas with high risk of error and fraud and where the best possible effect can be achieved.
For the information collected for analysis and selection, new regulations are introduced, which, among other things, aim to reduce the intrusion into personal privacy that the proposals may entail. For example, special rules are introduced for the maximum period for processing personal data and strong confidentiality protection.
The legislative changes concerning data analyses and selection and the change in the law on risk taxation for credit institutions enter into force on May 1, 2023. Other legislative changes enter into force on September 1, 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:123 by Anna Vikström (S),

dok_titel: Better opportunities for the Swedish Tax Agency to conduct data analysis and selection in population registration operations
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2022/23:881 by Martina Johansson et al. (C) amendment 24 and

2022/23:1673 by Annie Lööf et al. (C) amendment 94.
notis:
The Swedish Tax Agency shall have better opportunities to reduce the amount of errors and fraud in population registration. This is to be able to counter crime directed against, among other things, the welfare systems. The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal.
Through the legislative changes, the Swedish Tax Agency may process personal data to conduct data analysis and selection in order to prevent, avert and detect incorrect information in population registration. The agency shall focus on areas with high risk for errors and fraud and where the best possible effect can be achieved.
For the information collected for analysis and selection, new regulations are introduced, which, among other things, aim to reduce the interference with personal integrity that the proposals may entail. For example, special rules are introduced regarding the maximum time for processing personal data as well as strong confidentiality protection.
The legislative changes concerning data analysis and selection and the amendment to the law on risk tax for credit institutions enter into force on 1 May 2023. Other legislative changes enter into force on 1 September 2023.

rubrik: Follow-up of the effects of the legislative proposal
dok_titel: Certain questions on healthcare supply preparedness
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:2327 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) and 

2022/23:2329 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S) demand 3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's legislative proposal to clarify requirements for healthcare providers conducting healthcare activities. It concerns that they must provide healthcare products needed to provide good care. Healthcare products include medicines, medical devices, personal protective equipment, food for special medical purposes and raw materials for manufacturing.
The proposals also mean that outpatient pharmacies have an obligation to stock medicines and wholesale distributors have a delivery obligation to hospital pharmacies. A penalty charge is introduced for companies that do not inform the Medical Products Agency if the sale of a medicine ceases temporarily or permanently. Information about any shortage in the supply of medicines or medical devices is proposed to be able to be protected by confidentiality when the information is transferred from the Medical Products Agency to regions or municipalities in connection with investigation.
The legislative changes shall enter into force on 1 July 2023.
The Riksdag also approved the government's proposal that the state-owned company Apotek Produktion & Laboratorier AB receives an expanded public mandate. This means that the company must maintain its operations even during peacetime crises, heightened preparedness and ultimately war. For example, it could be ensuring the supply of active substances, excipients and packaging materials for products needed for care that cannot wait.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:2327 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) and 

2022/23:2329 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S) demand 3.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2022/23:2325 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V) proposal 1 and

2022/23:2329 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S) proposal 1.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's bill to clarify requirements for healthcare providers conducting healthcare activities. This concerns that they must supply healthcare products needed to provide good care. Healthcare products are understood to mean medicines, medical devices, personal protective equipment, food for special medical purposes, and manufacturing materials.
The proposals also mean that outpatient pharmacies have an obligation to stock medicines and wholesale dealers have a supply obligation to hospital pharmacies. A penalty fee is introduced for companies that do not notify the Medical Products Agency about the cessation, temporary or permanent, of sales of a medicine. Information about any shortage in the availability of medicines or medical devices is proposed to be subject to confidentiality when the information is transferred from the Medical Products Agency to regions or municipalities in connection with investigation.
The legislative changes will enter into force on 1 July 2023.
Parliament also approved the government's proposal for the state-owned company Apotek Produktion & Laboratorier AB to receive an expanded public assignment. This means that the company shall maintain its operations even during peacetime crises, elevated preparedness, and ultimately war. This could for example be to ensure the availability of active substances, excipients, and packaging materials for products needed for care that cannot wait.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the motions

2022/23:2325 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V) proposal 1 and

notis:
The Riksdag directed a formal request, a so-called formal directive (tillkännagivande), to the government to take measures for a better-functioning, more efficient and legally secure process for property division. For the party in the worse economic position, the completion of property division usually has very significant economic importance. Often, however, one party benefits from the property division process being prolonged, as has been established in an investigation.
The Riksdag notes that the government is to begin mapping the extent of the problem with prolonged property division processes. The Riksdag views this positively and considers it high time for the government to proceed with this matter. Among other things, the government should review the possibility of introducing a reasonable outer time limit for when a property division should be completed.
This directive is based on several proposals in motions submitted during the general 2022 motion period. In total, the Riksdag has addressed approximately 130 proposals in various family law matters, which also concern, inter alia, the legal regulation of parenthood, consideration periods for divorce, and various custody matters. The Riksdag rejected the other motions, citing inter alia that the government is already working on these issues.

rubrik: The exemption for services within independent groups
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2022/23:1470 by Amanda Lind et al. (MP) request 4,

2022/23:2321 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V),

2022/23:2322 by Helena Vilhelmsson et al. (C) and

2022/23:2323 by Marielle Lahti et al. (MP).
notis:
Parliament said yes to the government's proposal for a new law on value-added tax, so-called VAT. The law entails an adaptation to the EU's value-added tax directive. The law should also, among other things, clarify what applies when non-profit associations sell services internally.
Parliament has previously, in a formal request (tillkännagivande), pointed out that there have been uncertainties regarding what applies when non-profit associations sell services internally. Today, non-profit associations, such as the sports movement, study associations and registered religious communities, are exempt from the requirement to pay VAT. This may also apply when an independent group within an association sells a service internally. For example, it may be a large organization where several associations are part of, which has a joint department that sells IT support to the associations.
If the service instead could have been purchased on the market, it can however be assessed that the exemption from VAT leads to a distortion of competition. In such cases, the exemption from VAT may not be applied. The internal sales are then assessed as VAT-liable. Parliament urged in its formal request the government to investigate how the matter can be solved without causing a distortion of competition, and without increasing the risk for fraud with the value-added tax system.
The new law entails an adaptation to the EU's value-added tax directive, and should therefore not be applied more narrowly than the directive. According to EU Court of Justice practice, consideration should be given to the purpose of the exemption from VAT liability, namely to support civil society. The exemption may not be interpreted so restrictively that it loses its effect. In certain cases, the new law may mean that the exemption from VAT liability is applied differently.
Parliament welcomes the new law, and notes that the government has thereby fulfilled the formal request.
The new law and amendments enter into force on 1 July 2023.

dok_titel: Implementation of the electricity market directive concerning electricity supply and aggregation services
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2022/23:998 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) point of order 7 and

2022/23:1235 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) points of order 1-3.
notis:
Parliament approved the Government's proposal on how the EU's electricity market directive concerning electricity supply and so-called aggregation services should be incorporated into Swedish legislation.
The directive aims to adapt the electricity market to new conditions resulting from more decentralized electricity production from renewable sources and the phase-out of fossil fuels.
The Government's proposal provides greater opportunity for electricity users to adjust their electricity consumption when electricity prices are low or when the electricity grid is heavily stressed. The proposal also includes changes to certain requirements for electricity suppliers and changes to the rules governing switching of electricity suppliers for small businesses. Under the proposal, the Government, or an authority designated by the Government, may also establish rules regarding the information that electricity suppliers must provide to electricity users.
During 2022, Parliament decided to incorporate the parts of the electricity market directive concerning network operations into Swedish legislation. The electricity market directive should have been fully incorporated into Swedish legislation by December 31, 2020. The European Commission has initiated an infringement proceeding against Sweden for late implementation of the electricity market directive.
Parliament also approved an addition to the Government's proposal concerning a so-called rule-making mandate. Such a mandate is needed for the Government to be able to establish rules for various administrative processes. For example, that network operators must send notifications to electricity suppliers when commencing or taking over the supply of electricity.
Finally, Parliament rejected 80 proposals in motions from the general motion period of 2022.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the motions

2022/23:998 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) point of order 7 and

2022/23:1235 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) points of order 1-3.

dok_titel: Implementation of the electricity market directive concerning electricity supply and aggregation services
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:2337 by Rickard Nordin (C) items 2 and 3.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal on how the EU's electricity market directive concerning electricity supply and so-called aggregation services shall be implemented in Swedish legislation.
The directive aims to adapt the electricity market to new conditions such as more decentralized production of electricity from renewable sources and the phase-out of fossil fuels.
The government's proposal provides greater opportunity for electricity users to adjust electricity consumption when the electricity price is low or when the electricity grid is heavily stressed. The proposal also includes changes to certain requirements on electricity suppliers and changes to the rules on switching electricity suppliers for small businesses. The government, or the authority that the government determines, also has the power through the proposal to determine rules on the information that electricity suppliers shall provide to electricity users.
The Riksdag decided in 2022 to implement the parts of the electricity market directive concerning network operations in Swedish legislation. The electricity market directive was to have been implemented in full in Swedish legislation by 31 December 2020. The European Commission has opened an infringement proceeding against Sweden for late implementation of the electricity market directive.
The Riksdag also approved an addition to the government's proposal on a so-called normative mandate. Such a mandate is necessary for the government to be able to determine rules about various administrative processes. For example, that network companies shall send notifications to electricity suppliers when commencing or taking over electricity supply.
Finally, the Riksdag said no to 80 proposals in motions from the general motion period 2022.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:2337 by Rickard Nordin (C) items 2 and 3.

dok_titel: Implementation of the Electricity Market Directive regarding electricity supply and aggregation services
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:2062 by Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S) demand 3.
notis: The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on how the EU's electricity market directive regarding electricity supply and so-called aggregation services shall be incorporated into Swedish legislation. The directive aims to adapt the electricity market to new conditions that more decentralized production of electricity from renewable sources and phase-out of fossil fuels entail. The government's proposal provides greater opportunity for electricity users to adjust electricity consumption when electricity prices are low or when the electricity grid is heavily loaded. The proposal also includes changes to certain requirements for electricity suppliers and changes to the rules on changing electricity suppliers for small businesses. The government, or an authority determined by the government, shall also be able to determine rules on the information that electricity suppliers shall provide to electricity users. The Riksdag decided in 2022 to implement the parts of the electricity market directive concerning network operations in Swedish legislation. The electricity market directive should have been implemented in Swedish legislation by December 31, 2020. The European Commission has initiated an infringement proceeding against Sweden for late implementation of the electricity market directive. The Riksdag also approved an addition to the government's proposal regarding a so-called rule-making authorization. Such an authorization is needed for the government to be able to determine rules on various administrative processes. For example, that network operators shall send notices to electricity suppliers when beginning or taking over the supply of electricity. Finally, the Riksdag rejected 80 proposals in motions from the general motion period in 2022.
alternatives:

2022/23:2062 by Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S) demand 3.

dok_titel: A Special Criminal Provision for Participation in a Terrorist Organization
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:2353 by Ardalan Shekarabi et al. (S).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal to introduce a new crime in the terrorism crime law, participation in a terrorist organization. The new crime creates a special criminal liability for a person who participates in a terrorist organization in a way designed to promote, strengthen or support the organization.
The penalty scale shall be imprisonment for a maximum of four years. If the crime is serious, the penalty scale shall be imprisonment for a minimum of two and a maximum of eight years. If the perpetrator has led the terrorist organization, the penalty scale shall be imprisonment for a fixed term, a minimum of two and a maximum of eighteen years, or for life.
It shall also be punishable to finance participation in a terrorist organization, to publicly incite and recruit for the crime, as well as to travel abroad with the intent to commit the crime.
The law amendments come into force on June 1, 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:2353 by Ardalan Shekarabi et al. (S).

dok_titel: Increased penalties for crimes in criminal networks
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for
1. act amending the Code of Judicial Procedure with the amendment that 27 chap. 18 § shall have the wording that the Committee proposes in Appendix 3,
2. act amending the Penal Code,
3. act amending the Narcotics Penalty Act (1968:64),
4. act amending the Act (2000:1225) on penalties for smuggling,
5. act amending the Act (2007:979) on measures to prevent certain particularly serious crimes with the amendment that 1 § shall have the wording that the Committee proposes in Appendix 3,
6. act amending the Act (2008:322) on the Customs Agency's and Coast Guard's authority to take action against drink-driving offences,
7. act amending the Terrorist Crimes Act (2022:666).
Thereby Parliament approves Government Bill 2022/23:53 points 1-7 and rejects motion

2022/23:2333 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) motion 1.
notis:
Parliament said yes to the government's proposal to increase the penalties for crimes in criminal networks and in criminal settlements. The purpose of the legislative changes is to mark the seriousness of this type of crime and to give the judicial system expanded opportunities to combat gang crime.
Penalties are increased for, among other things, serious illegal coercion, illegal threats, robbery and extortion. The penalty for narcotics crimes aimed at sale is also increased, and ordering narcotics for personal use is criminalized as an attempted crime.
It also becomes a criminal offence to involve persons under 18 years of age in crime or criminal activity. Furthermore, a new type of penalty increase provision is introduced that targets violent settlements among criminals.
The presumption, or assumption, for detention shall apply when there is suspicion of a crime with a minimum sentence of imprisonment of one year and six months or more, compared to previously a minimum sentence of imprisonment of two years or more.
The legislative changes come into effect on 1 July 2023.

2022/23:1811 by Christian Carlsson (KD) motion 6,

2022/23:2356 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) motion 1 and

2022/23:2357 by Bassem Nasr et al. (MP) motion 1.
notis:
Parliament said yes to the government's proposal to introduce a new crime in the Terrorist Crimes Act, participation in a terrorist organization. The new crime means a special criminal liability for the person who participates in a terrorist organization in a way that is designed to promote, strengthen or support the organization.
The scale of punishment shall be imprisonment of at most four years. If the crime is serious, the scale of punishment shall be imprisonment of at least two and at most eight years. If the perpetrator has led the terrorist organization, the scale of punishment shall be imprisonment for a fixed period, at least two and at most eighteen years, or for life.
It shall also be a criminal offence to finance participation in a terrorist organization, to publicly incite and recruit to the crime and to travel abroad with the intention of committing the crime.
The legislative changes come into effect on 1 June 2023.
alternatives:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for
1. act amending the Terrorist Crimes Act (2022:666),
2. act amending the Code of Judicial Procedure,
3. act amending the Act (2007:979) on measures to prevent certain particularly serious crimes.
Thereby Parliament approves Government Bill 2022/23:73 points 1-3 and rejects the motions

rubrik: Changes to the law on collective transport passengers' rights
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the law (2015:953) on collective transport passengers' rights.
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposal 2022/23:72 point 2 and rejects the motion 

2022/23:2354 by Katarina Luhr et al. (MP) point 1.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal on changed rules for collective transport passengers and rail traffic.
The EU has introduced a new train passenger regulation containing basic rules on the transport contract, information, and tickets. In view of the new train passenger regulation, the government proposes, in part, an exception from the passenger's right to a price reduction if a delay is due to an extraordinary event. For example, extreme weather conditions or a major public health crisis. In part, it is proposed that rail traffic conducted for historical purposes or tourism be exempted from the train passenger regulation.
The new rules come into effect on June 7, 2023.

dok_titel: The National Board of Forensic Medicine's handling of human biological material
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts sections 8 and 9 of the Government's proposal for a law on the National Board of Forensic Medicine's handling of human biological material.
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2022/23:82 point 1 in this part and rejects the motion

2022/23:2366 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) demand 1.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's bill on the National Board of Forensic Medicine's handling of human biological material, that is, material from the human body. The new law aims to create clear legal conditions for the handling and thereby strengthen the protection of people's integrity.
The Riksdag also approved the Government's proposed amendments concerning forensic psychiatric examinations. It concerns, among other things, what information may be disclosed if a suspect is to undergo a forensic psychiatric examination, or in connection with so-called section 7 certificates. The need for information from the Social Insurance Agency, the Employment Agency, the Swedish Prison and Probation Service, the Migration Agency and the Swedish Defence Preparedness Agency is considered to outweigh the intrusion into personal integrity that disclosure could entail.
Finally, the Riksdag approved the Government's proposal on confidentiality rules to maintain order and prevent escapes in the forensic psychiatric activities.
The new law and amendments come into force on July 1, 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag adopts sections 8 and 9 of the Government's proposal for a law on the National Board of Forensic Medicine's handling of human biological material.
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2022/23:82 point 1 in this part and rejects the motion

2022/23:2366 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) demand 1.

2022/23:2054 by Lawen Redar et al. (S) point 38 and

2022/23:2309 by Vasiliki Tsouplaki et al. (V) point 1.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for measures to ensure a healthy and safe gambling market. The measures proposed by the government include:

the possibility to involve payment service providers to block bets and payment of winnings to and from unlicensed gambling operators
the possibility for the Gambling Authority to purchase gambling services under assumed identity as part of supervision of gambling operators
the possibility to store and forward personal data to prevent so-called match-fixing, that is when a sporting event has been manipulated in connection with betting
the requirement for gambling operators to, upon request, provide information to the Police Authority needed to investigate crimes related to gambling.

The measures mean changes to the Gambling Act that come into force July 1, 2023. At the same time, the Riksdag rejected approximately 50 proposals in motions on gambling issues from the general motion period of 2022. In particular, the Riksdag refers to previous positions and to the government proposal described above.

notis:
The Riksdag directed a notification to the government to clarify the law on investment savings accounts. An investment savings account is a savings form that is taxed on a standardized basis, which means that the tax is not based on the actual return but on an annual tax calculated on the value of the assets in the account.
The Riksdag considers that there are currently limited opportunities for savers to deposit shares subscribed in connection with an initial public offering or a new share issue directly into an investment savings account. According to current regulations, one must have one's investment savings account with the issuing institution that handles the initial public offering in order to deposit one's shares directly. If one has one's investment savings account with another party, the shares must go through a securities account into the investment savings account. With such a transfer, the shares are thus considered sold for tax purposes, meaning that any capital gains must be reported and capital losses deducted. The clarification means that holders of investment savings accounts are to be treated equally and thus be able to participate in more share issues.
The notification came in connection with the Riksdag's treatment of motions submitted during the general motion period 2022.
The Riksdag said no to other motions regarding enterprise, capital and property. The Riksdag considers that work is already underway in the areas covered by the motions.

Parliament directed a formal request, a so-called tillkännagivande (formal request), to the government to clarify the law on investment savings accounts. If one has one's investment savings account elsewhere, the shares must go through a custody account or securities account to reach the investment savings account. In such a transfer, the shares are thereby considered to be disposed of for tax purposes—that is, sold—and any capital gain must be reported and any capital loss deducted. The clarification means that holders of investment savings accounts shall be treated equally and thereby be able to participate in more new share issues.
The formal request came in connection with Parliament's treatment of motions submitted during the general motion period of 2022.

notis:
Parliament directed a request, a so-called announcement (tillkännagivande), to the Government to clarify the law on investment savings accounts. An investment savings account is a savings form subject to imputed taxation, which means that the tax is not based on the actual return but on an annual tax calculated on the value of the assets in the account.
Parliament considers that today there are limited opportunities for savers to transfer shares acquired in connection with a stock exchange listing or a new share issue directly into an investment savings account. According to current regulations, one must have one's investment savings account with the issuing institution that handles the stock exchange listing to receive one's shares directly. If one has one's investment savings account with another party, the shares must go via a securities account into the investment savings account. In such a transfer, the shares are thus considered to be sold for tax purposes, meaning any capital gains must be reported and capital losses deducted. The clarification means that holders of investment savings accounts shall be treated equally and thus be able to participate in more new share issues.
The announcement came in connection with Parliament handling motions submitted during the general motion period 2022.

forslag_text:
