2022/23:2345 by Jonny Cato and Martina Johansson (both C) claims 1 and 2.
notis:
Parliament has dealt with a letter from the Government. It concerns the Audit Office report on track change in the migration process. The Audit Office has examined whether the system of track change from asylum to labour-based immigration functions effectively.
The overall conclusion is that the system appears to have reached the right target group. However, the Audit Office assesses that there are deficiencies in the Migration Agency's procedures and controls that could lead to track changes being used to circumvent the legislation for asylum and labour-based immigration. The Government agrees with this assessment.
The Government has been recommended to ensure that the Migration Agency can exchange necessary information with cooperating authorities. The Government should also ensure that the Migration Agency can compile information about employers in order to investigate and monitor track change cases.
An investigator has been tasked by the Government to assess how the track change system can be abolished.
Parliament filed the Government letter as received.

rubrik: Drug tests of children under 15 years in more cases
dok_titel: Improved measures when children are suspected of crime
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the law (1964:167) with special provisions for young offenders in the parts it concerns section 36 b.
Thereby Parliament approves government bill 2022/23:78 point 2 in this part and rejects motion 

2022/23:2359 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V).
notis:
Parliament said yes to the government's proposal which aims to improve the regulatory framework for investigations against children suspected of crime. The proposal shall ensure that these investigations maintain a high degree of legal certainty and are effective.
The law amendments deal with the following:

More investigations shall be able to be conducted when children under 15 years of age are suspected of crime.
A complainant's counsel or a special representative for children shall be able to be appointed for the complainant when the person suspected of having committed the crime is under 15 years of age.
A trial, that is a court proceeding, shall be able to be brought in more cases.
It shall become possible to grant review of or set aside a judgment from a trial that has become final.
More drug tests of children under 15 years of age shall be able to be conducted.
It shall become possible for prosecutors to decide on youth service through a summary penalty order.

The law amendments shall enter into force on 1 July 2023.
alternatives:

rubrik: Confidentiality exception in disclosure for technical processing or technical storage of data
dok_titel: Confidentiality exception in disclosure for technical processing or technical storage of data
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the Government's proposal for a law amending the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (2009:400).
Parliament thus approves proposition 2022/23:97 and rejects motion 

2022/23:2376 by Jessica Wetterling et al. (V).
notis:
Parliament approved the Government's proposal for new rules for situations where an authority discloses information for the purpose of technical processing or technical storage of the information with another party.
According to the Government's proposal, authorities should be able to disclose information covered by confidentiality to an individual or to an authority that has the task of technically processing or technically storing the information. The proposal also includes a restriction on the freedom to disclose for those subject to confidentiality obligations under the law on confidentiality obligations in outsourcing of technical processing or storage of information.
The Government's proposal aims to create better conditions for authorities to outsource or coordinate their IT operations. It also aims to strengthen protection for information disclosed to an individual when outsourcing IT operations.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 July 2023.

rubrik: Reduction of employer contributions for persons working with research or development
dok_titel: Reduction of employer contributions for persons working with research or development – increased ceiling for the deduction
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the Government's proposal for a law amending the Social Contributions Act (2000:980).
Parliament thus approves proposition 2022/23:79 and rejects motion 

2022/23:2365 by Ida Gabrielsson et al. (V).
notis:
The possibility of making deductions from employer contributions for persons working with research or development is to be strengthened. Already today, employers can make deductions for this group, but according to a proposal from the Government, the maximum aggregate deduction shall be increased from 600,000 kronor to 1.5 million kronor per month.
This results in the ceiling for the reduction of the general payroll tax also being increased by the corresponding amount.
The new ceiling amount applies in total for all employees working with research or development at the same employer. This means that an employer with a wage base of at least 15 million kronor – for this group of employees – gets their employer contributions and general payroll tax reduced by 3 million kronor per calendar month.
Parliament approved the proposal. The legislative changes shall enter into force on 1 July 2023.
alternatives:

Parliament thus approves proposition 2022/23:79 and rejects motion 

2022/23:2365 by Ida Gabrielsson et al. (V).

dok_titel: Extension of the temporary expanded tax reduction for certain diesel use in agriculture, forestry, and aquaculture
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposals for
1. an act on amendment to the Act (2022:1047) on amendment to the Act (1994:1776) on energy tax,
2. an act on amendment to the Act (1994:1776) on energy tax,
3. an act on amendment to the Act (1994:1776) on energy tax.
Thereby the Riksdag approves Government Bill 2022/23:69 items 1–3 and rejects the motions

2022/23:2358 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) and

2022/23:2361 by Marielle Lahti et al. (MP).
notis: The temporary expanded tax reduction on certain diesel use in agriculture, forestry, and aquaculture shall apply throughout 2023. The Riksdag has previously decided on a temporary tax reduction, and the Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal to extend the period for so-called agricultural diesel. According to the decision, a reduction of the carbon dioxide tax shall be granted at 2,491 kronor per cubic meter for diesel consumed from July 1 to December 31, 2023. For such diesel consumption during the period, a reduction of the energy tax shall be granted at 1,582 kronor per cubic meter. The background for the decision is to support Swedish businesses that have experienced significantly increased costs.

notis:
The Riksdag has considered a communication from the government concerning the National Audit Office's report on government subsidies to study associations. The National Audit Office has audited whether the control, monitoring, and management of subsidies to study associations is effective. The subjects of the audit are the government and the National Board for Adult Education (Folkbildningsrådet), the agency that distributes subsidies to, for example, study associations.
The National Audit Office's assessment is that the monitoring and control of the subsidies needs to be significantly strengthened, and that there are significant challenges with the current management model which is based on stakeholders auditing themselves. A government investigation is underway, a so-called committee directive (kommittédirektiv), of among other things the current management model, which shall be submitted by February 19, 2024 at the latest. The National Audit Office assesses that the direction and scope of the investigation is necessary, but considers that measures to strengthen control are already needed now. Among other things, the National Audit Office recommends to the government to ensure that the National Board for Adult Education's administrative role in the control and monitoring of subsidies is clarified and strengthened.
The Riksdag filed the communication with the records, that is, concluded the matter.
The Riksdag also said no to 17 proposals in motions on further education issues that were submitted during the general motion period 2022.
alternatives:

dok_titel: Implementation of amendments to the firearms directive
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2022/23:2379 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C).
notis:
Parliament accepted the government's proposal for changes to Swedish firearms legislation. The changes are assessed as necessary to implement the so-called amendments directive to the EU firearms directive into Swedish law.
The legislative changes take effect on 1 July 2023 and include, among other things, that marking requirements are expanded while an option is introduced to make exceptions to the marking requirements for historically valuable firearms; firearm magazines holding many cartridges and capable of being combined with certain semi-automatic firearms are regulated; firearms brokers, i.e., business activities that connect buyers and sellers of firearms, are regulated in the same way as firearms dealers; firearms dealers and firearms brokers shall report if a purchase or attempted purchase of ammunition has raised suspicions, for example due to the amount; the requirements for registration are expanded.
alternatives:

forslag_text:

2022/23:2368 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) demand 1 and 

2022/23:2375 by Bassem Nasr et al. (MP) demand 5.
notis:
Parliament accepted the government's proposal for a new law on security guards. The law is intended to create conditions for more flexible and increased use of security guards and to give them expanded powers.
According to the new legislation, security guards are to be permitted to help maintain public order and security or contribute to safety. They are also to be given additional powers, for example, to transport certain detained persons and destroy seized alcohol if the value is negligible.
The new rules take effect on 1 January 2024.

dok_titel: A New Law on Security Guards
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for
1. a law amending the Act (1976:511) on the detention of intoxicated persons etc.,
2. a law amending the Police Act (1984:387).
Thereby the Riksdag approves Government Bill 2022/23:91 points 3 and 4 and rejects the motions

2022/23:2368 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) points 2 and 3 and

2022/23:2375 by Bassem Nasr et al. (MP) points 2 and 3.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal for a new law on security guards. The law is to create conditions for more flexible and increased use of security guards and give them expanded powers.
According to the new legislation, security guards are to be permitted to help maintain public order and security or contribute to public safety. They are also to be given additional powers, for example to transport certain detained persons and destroy confiscated alcohol if the value is minor.
The new rules enter into force on 1 January 2024.
alternatives:

dok_titel: Swedish National Audit Office's report on government initiatives for equivalent grading
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:884 by Muharrem Demirok et al. (C) motion 24, 

2022/23:2341 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S) motions 1-4, and 

2022/23:2347 by Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C).
notis: The government has addressed the Swedish National Audit Office's report on government initiatives for equivalent grading in a communication. The audit office's examination shows that significant differences still exist between grades and results on national tests, and that government measures for more equivalent grading have not achieved the desired results. The Audit Office recommends that the government investigate how grading can become more equivalent, and that the School Inspectorate should improve monitoring of assessment and grading in quality audits. In the communication, the government agrees with the Audit Office's recommendation and announces that it will establish an inquiry on the matter. The government also considers it important that the School Inspectorate regularly reviews whether the monitoring of completed inspections can be improved and streamlined. The Riksdag referred the government's communication to the archives, that is, closed the matter.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:884 by Muharrem Demirok et al. (C) motion 24,

dok_titel: Extended police powers in border areas
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motion

2022/23:2394 by Rasmus Ling et al. (MP) demand 3.
notis:
Parliament said yes to the government's proposal for a new law with special provisions concerning police powers in border areas.
The new law shall give the police extended powers, that is, increased authority to take action, at among other things certain airports, ports and railway stations, at bridges for road traffic to or from abroad and at border crossing points on public roads, to prevent crime.
The powers shall also give the police extended possibilities to intervene in border areas to conduct identity checks of a foreign national to determine whether the person has the right to stay in the country, so-called internal alien control. Furthermore, the powers entail better possibilities for camera surveillance in border areas.
The new regulations shall enter into force on August 1st.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the motion

Parliament approves the guidelines for economic and budgetary policy that the government proposes.
Thereby Parliament adopts government bill 2022/23:100 point 1 and rejects the motions

2022/23:615 by Markus Kallifatides (S) items 1-3,

2022/23:1121 by Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al. (C) items 3 and 4,

2022/23:2388 by Magdalena Andersson et al. (S), and

2022/23:2389 by Martin Ådahl et al. (C).
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for guidelines for economic policy in the spring government bill.
The economic downturn and reduced economic activity are expected to weaken the public sector's finances during 2024, but with gradual strengthening during 2025 and 2026. The Committee welcomes that the government aims for the so-called surplus target, which is a goal for the public sector's financial savings, in formulating the direction of fiscal policy. A neutral fiscal policy in line with the surplus target makes it possible for monetary policy to work so that inflation decreases over time.
Parliament agrees with the government that economic policy should be directed at combating inflation and supporting vulnerable households. The economic downturn should be met with structural reforms for, among other things, a competitive and innovative business sector. The so-called work line should be reintroduced and a benefits reform should increase incentives to enter the labour market.
Other reforms include combating organised crime, increasing the number of qualified teachers, shortening waiting times in healthcare and increasing healthcare places, strengthening defence and crisis preparedness, and improving energy supply and reducing emissions.
alternatives:

2022/23:2393 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) and 

2022/23:2394 by Rasmus Ling et al. (MP) claim 1.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for a new law with special provisions on police powers in border areas.
The new law will give the police extended powers, that is, increased authority to take measures, at, among other things, certain airports, ports and railway stations, at bridges for road traffic to or from abroad and at border crossing points on public roads, to prevent crime.
The powers will also give the police enhanced opportunities to intervene in border areas to carry out personal inspections of a foreign national to determine whether the person has the right to stay in the country, so-called internal alien control. In addition, the powers entail better opportunities for camera surveillance in border areas.
The new rules come into force on 1 August.

notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for amendments to the Local Government Act, the Act on municipal accounting and reporting and the Act on financial coordination of rehabilitation measures.
The legislative amendments mean that the result equalization reserves regulated in the Local Government Act shall be replaced with result reserves. The introduction of result reserves means that municipalities and regions are given greater opportunities to plan their savings in order to achieve good financial management. The purpose of the legislative amendments is to promote efficient financial management in municipalities and regions.

2022/23:2399 by Maj Karlsson et al. (V) demand 1 and

notis:
It becomes the state's responsibility to provide guide dogs to people with visual impairment. Responsibility for guide dog activities is transferred from Synskadades Riksförbund (the Swedish Association of the Visually Impaired) to the government agency determined by the government. 
The new rules aim to transfer the exercise of authority regarding the right to use a guide dog from Synskadades Riksförbund to a government agency. It is also an advantage that the same agency that processes applications and assigns guide dogs is responsible for information, procurement of guide dog equipment, training, and veterinary care. 
A person who has been granted a guide dog shall be assigned a guide dog within a reasonable time, shall undergo continuous training together with the dog, and shall be responsible for ensuring that the dog receives the care it needs during the time the dog is at their disposal.  
Parliament approved the government's proposal. The new rules enter into force on 1 April 2024.

notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's bill on asset freezing to prevent and counteract the financing of terrorist acts. The new law means that assets can be frozen for a person who can reasonably be suspected of a crime under the Terrorist Offences Act, or who has been convicted of a crime under the Terrorist Offences Act.
Also, a person who, based on the content of a foreign criminal investigation, or who can reasonably be suspected of having committed an act in another state that corresponds to a crime under the Terrorist Offences Act, shall be covered by the law.
It will also be possible to decide to temporarily freeze assets for someone listed by the UN Security Council or sanctions committee.
The new provisions aim to ensure that Sweden fulfills its international obligations in the sanctions area and come into effect on January 1, 2024.

notis:

rubrik: Proposal for a Regulation on Combating Late Payment in Commercial Transactions
dok_titel: Subsidiarity Assessment of the Commission's Proposal for a Regulation on Combating Late Payment in Commercial Transactions
forslag_text: The Riksdag decides to submit a reasoned opinion to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission with the wording set out in Annex 2.
notis:
The EU Commission has proposed a new regulation on combating late payment in commercial transactions, that is, transactions between companies or between companies and public authorities.
The Riksdag has assessed the proposal based on the so-called principle of subsidiarity, that is, the principle that decisions on new EU laws are taken as close to citizens as possible. The EU should therefore only take action if it is more effective than if individual countries act on their own. The principle protects member states' right to make their own decisions at the national level.
The Riksdag does not in itself question the need for regulation at EU level to promote faster payment in commercial transactions but considers that the EU Commission's proposal in certain respects goes too far and therefore violates the principle of subsidiarity. This applies, for example, to the proposals for a mandatory payment period of 30 days and a fixed interest rate for default interest that would limit the contractual freedom of companies.
Against this background, the Riksdag decided to submit its views in a so-called reasoned opinion to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council and the EU Commission.
alternatives: The Riksdag decides to submit a reasoned opinion to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission with the wording set out in Annex 2.

rubrik: Group's Standing in Actions for Remedies
dok_titel: Class Action to Protect Collective Consumer Interests
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:106 by Nadja Awad et al. (V),

2023/24:162 by Jennie Nilsson et al. (S) and

2023/24:220 by Katarina Luhr and Daniel Helldén (both MP).
notis:
The Riksdag has voted yes to the government's proposal on, among other things, a new law on class action to protect collective consumer interests.
The bill is based on an EU directive aimed at achieving a high level of consumer protection and improving consumers' access to legal remedies when consumer protection provisions are violated.
Through the new law, rules are introduced for approval of entities that may bring actions for remedies on behalf of a group of consumers. A consumer organization shall be approved as such an entity if, among other things, it conducts activities aimed at the public for the purpose of protecting consumer interests. An entity may bring actions for injunctions and for remedies, such as damages.
The scope of the new law covers, among other things, marketing, contract terms, financial services, transport, medicines, data protection and energy.
The new law is to enter into force on 1 January 2024.

notis:
The Parliament approved expenditure limits and revenue calculations in the government's budget proposition for 2024. Expenses are calculated to amount to SEK 1,331 billion and revenues are estimated at SEK 1,324 billion. This means a deficit in the state budget of SEK 7 billion for 2024. The proposals are based on a political agreement between SD, M, KD and L.
The Parliament also approved the expenditure ceiling for the state and approved proposals on tax and fee rules including

strengthened ordinary earned income tax credit
introducing indexing in the calculation of the earned income tax credit for the elderly and increased age limit
extended expert tax
abolished tax on plastic carrier bags
removed reduction of employer contributions for 15-18 year-olds.

Some of these proposals have been submitted in separate propositions but are announced in the budget proposition and are included in the calculations of revenues in the budget.
All legislative changes come into force on January 1, 2024 except those concerning abolished tax on plastic carrier bags which come into force on November 1, 2024, changed taxation of redemption shares in certain cases which comes into force on January 1, 2025 and increased age limit from 66 to 67 years for the right to deduction in the calculation of own contributions and the general payroll tax which comes into force on January 1, 2026.
The Parliament also approved the government's direction for economic policy and budget policy.
Swedish economy is assessed to be in a low-growth period in 2024. Inflation has started to fall but is still higher than the Riksbank's target of 2 percent. The labour market has so far been resilient but is expected to gradually worsen due to the reduced activity in the economy.
According to the government, policy should be directed according to a long-term plan in three parts to take Sweden through the difficult situation: to combat inflation and support households and welfare, to restore the work line and to implement structural reforms for higher growth. The Parliament is of the same opinion. Through the well-balanced, restrained fiscal policy, responsibility is taken to not add to inflation while contributing to improving the conditions for the Swedish economy. By directing fiscal policy towards the surplus target, fiscal policy does not counteract monetary policy.
The Parliament's decision on expenditure limits will be guiding when the Parliament in the next step decides on appropriations for the 27 expenditure areas in the budget.
The Parliament has also dealt with the government's letter on the National Audit Office's report on the application of the fiscal policy framework 2022. The Parliament decided to file the letter, that is, to close the matter.

notis:
The Parliament approved the government's bill on new nuclear power in Sweden. The legislative changes mean that it becomes permissible to have new reactors at other locations than at the nuclear power plants in Forsmark, Ringhals and Oskarshamn. Furthermore, more than ten reactors are allowed to be in operation simultaneously.
The Parliament shares the government's assessment that fossil-free nuclear power electricity shall play a central role in the Swedish energy mix going forward. The main reasons for this are an expected greater demand for electricity in combination with the fact that fossil fuels must be phased out, not least for climate reasons. Nuclear power also contributes to the Swedish electricity system being able to function in a stable and predictable manner.
The legislative changes come into force on January 1, 2024.

rubrik: Guidelines for economic and budget policy
forslag_text:
Parliament approves the guidelines for economic and budget policy as proposed by the government.
Thereby Parliament adopts proposition 2023/24:1 financing plan point 1 and rejects the motions

2023/24:2385 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) proposal 1,

2023/24:2654 by Magdalena Andersson et al. (S) proposal 1,

2023/24:2689 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) proposal 1 and

2023/24:2733 by Muharrem Demirok et al. (C) proposal 1.
notis:
Parliament approved spending limits and revenue forecasts in the government's budget proposition for 2024. Expenditures are estimated at 1,331 billion kronor and revenues at 1,324 billion kronor. This means a deficit in the state budget of 7 billion kronor for 2024. The proposals are based on a political agreement between SD, M, KD and L.
Parliament also approved the spending ceiling for the state and approved proposals on tax and fee rules that include, among others,

strengthened ordinary earned income tax credit
introduction of indexing in the calculation of the earned income tax credit for older persons and raised age limit
expanded expert tax
abolished tax on plastic carrier bags
abolished reduction in employer contributions for 15–18-year-olds.

Some of these proposals have been presented in separate propositions, but are announced in the budget proposition and are included in the calculations of revenues in the budget.
All legislative changes enter into force on 1 January 2024 except those concerning abolished tax on plastic carrier bags which enter into force on 1 November 2024, changed taxation of redemption shares in certain cases which enter into force on 1 January 2025 and raised age limit from 66 to 67 years for the right to deduction in calculating own contributions and the general wage tax which enter into force on 1 January 2026.
Parliament also approved the government's direction for economic and budget policy.
The Swedish economy is assessed to be in a recession in 2024. Inflation has begun to fall, but is still higher than the Riksbank's target of 2 percent. The labour market has so far been resilient, but is expected to gradually worsen due to reduced activity in the economy.
According to the government, policy should be directed in accordance with a long-term three-part plan to take Sweden through the difficult situation: to combat inflation and support households and welfare, to re-establish the work line and to implement structural reforms for higher growth. Parliament is of the same opinion. Through the well-balanced, restrained fiscal policy, responsibility is taken not to fuel inflation while also contributing to improving the conditions for the Swedish economy. By directing fiscal policy towards the surplus target, fiscal policy does not counteract monetary policy.
Parliament's decision on spending limits will be steering when Parliament in the next step decides on allocations for the 27 spending areas in the budget.
Parliament has also considered the government's report on the Swedish National Audit Office's report on the application of the fiscal policy framework in 2022. Parliament decided to file the report, that is, to conclude the matter.

forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the Act (2017:1201) on reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from certain fossil fuels.
Thereby Parliament adopts proposition 2023/24:28 and rejects the motions

2023/24:2763 by Rickard Nordin et al. (C) proposal 1.
notis:
Parliament voted yes to the government's proposal for an amendment to the Act on reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from certain fossil fuels.
The amendment means that the reduction obligation's requirement for reduced emissions for petrol and diesel is lowered to six percent for 2024–2026 and that the reduction levels for 2027–2030 are eliminated. Currently, the reduction levels are at 7.8 percent for petrol and 30.5 percent for diesel.
The purpose of the amendment is, among other things, to reduce fuel prices.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 January 2024.

dok_titel: Firearms and explosive goods – increased penalties for more serious crimes
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2023/24:2771 by Ardalan Shekarabi et al. (S).
notis:
The Riksdag voted yes to the government's proposal for increased sentences for more serious forms of firearms crimes, crimes against the licensing requirement for explosive goods, firearms smuggling and smuggling of explosive goods.
The proposals mean that the laws are strengthened in the following way:

The sentence scales for aggravated crime are changed from imprisonment of at least two years and at most five years to imprisonment of at least four years and at most seven years.
The sentence scales for particularly grave crime are changed from imprisonment of at least four years and at most seven years to imprisonment of at least six years and at most ten years.
The maximum sentences for ordinary crimes are increased from imprisonment for three years to imprisonment for five years.

The purpose is to mark the seriousness of these crimes which are often committed by criminal networks.
The legislative changes shall take effect on 1 January 2024.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions 

2023/24:2770 by Niklas Karlsson et al. (S) demand 1 and 

2023/24:2775 by Helena Lindahl et al. (C) demand 2.
notis:
The government has proposed a new additional tax for companies in large groups. Parliament approved the proposal, but with a modification regarding accounting standards. The government's proposal means that groups with annual revenues of at least 750 million euros shall pay an effective tax of at least 15 percent on a specially defined tax base. Exceptions are government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and pension funds.
The purpose of the legislative change is for companies in multinational and national groups to pay a fair share of tax regardless of where they operate. The proposal is based on an EU directive that shall be implemented in Swedish legislation.
The legislative change takes effect on January 1, 2024.

dok_titel: The National Audit Office's report on the government's governance of society's information and cybersecurity
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:415 by Jimmy Ståhl et al. (SD) amendment 6 and

2023/24:461 by Hanna Gunnarsson et al. (V) amendments 2 and 3.
notis:
The Riksdag has reviewed a letter from the government concerning the National Audit Office's examination of the government's governance of society's information and cybersecurity.
The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the government's work in this area is not effectively designed. According to the National Audit Office, strategic trade-offs and priorities for information and cybersecurity work are lacking. The National Audit Office therefore provided recommendations to the government on how the new national information and cybersecurity strategy should be designed to address the shortcomings.
In its letter, the government agrees with the National Audit Office's findings. It has taken a long time to build up the National Cybersecurity Centre (NCSC). The distribution of responsibilities within the centre also makes the operations themselves difficult to manage and monitor. The Ministry of Defence has instructed a researcher to both propose how the Swedish Defence Radio Establishment (FRA) should be given main responsibility for the NCSC and to review the centre's organization and governance.
The Riksdag views positively the measures announced by the government in the letter. With this, the Riksdag filed the government's letter with the records, that is, closed the matter.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:415 by Jimmy Ståhl et al. (SD) amendment 6 and

2023/24:461 by Hanna Gunnarsson et al. (V) amendments 2 and 3.

notis:
Parliament has deliberated a letter from the government concerning the National Audit Office's review of the government's management of society's information and cyber security.
The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the government's work in this area is not effectively designed. According to the National Audit Office, strategic considerations and priorities for information and cyber security work are lacking. The National Audit Office therefore provided recommendations to the government on how the new national information and cyber security strategy should be designed to address the shortcomings.
In its letter, the government agrees with the National Audit Office's observations. It has taken a long time to establish the National Cyber Security Center (NCSC). The division of responsibility within the center also makes the operations difficult to manage and monitor. The Ministry of Defence has commissioned a person to both provide proposals on how the Swedish Defence Radio Institute (FRA) should be assigned primary responsibility for the NCSC and to review the center's organization and management.
Parliament views positively the measures that the government announces in the letter. With this, Parliament placed the government's letter with the records, that is, concluded the matter.

rubrik: Fee for examination of a dispute at the General Complaints Board
dok_titel: Fee for examination of a dispute at the General Complaints Board
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for an act amending the act (2015:671) on alternative dispute resolution in consumer disputes.
Thus Parliament approves proposition 2023/24:5 and rejects motions

2023/24:228 by Nadja Awad et al. (V),

2023/24:1341 by Jennie Nilsson et al. (S) and

2023/24:1871 by Katarina Luhr et al. (MP).
notis:
The government is given the opportunity to introduce a fee for examination of a dispute at the General Complaints Board. Parliament approved the government's proposal, which involves an amendment to the act on alternative dispute resolution in consumer disputes.
The influx of cases to the General Complaints Board has increased steadily in recent years. Moreover, the cases have become more complicated and extensive. Today, approximately one-third of cases are dismissed, usually because the complainant has not submitted the required supplementary information. In these cases, the authority uses resources on cases that will not be examined on the merits. According to the government, there is likely a connection between the large number of cases that are dismissed due to missing supplementary information and the fact that today it is free to file a complaint. A fee would therefore likely reduce the number of complaints that will not be examined on the merits.
The legislative change enters into force on 1 July 2024.

The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the government's localization of agencies in locations outside Stockholm during the period has partially lived up to the Riksdag's intentions. The National Audit Office assesses that the localization decisions have resulted in a small but positive contribution to regional development, while the government's localization decisions have not jeopardized the agencies' ability to conduct their operations efficiently in the long term.

An important starting point for the government is that agencies can conduct their operations efficiently regardless of where they are located. This is something the government monitors within the framework of ongoing agency management.
The Riksdag views positively the government's continuous work with the question of state presence throughout the country. With this, the Riksdag laid the government's statement to the records, that is, concluded the matter, and rejected the motions.

dok_titel: The Swedish National Audit Office's report on establishment of agencies outside Stockholm
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:29 by Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S) point 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has addressed a letter from the government concerning the Swedish National Audit Office's report on the establishment of agencies outside Stockholm.
The Swedish National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the government's localization of agencies in areas outside Stockholm during the period has partly lived up to the Riksdag's intentions. The Swedish National Audit Office assesses that the localization decisions have contributed a small but positive impact to regional development while the government's localization decisions have not jeopardized the agencies' ability to conduct their operations effectively in the long term.
In its letter, the government largely concurs with the Swedish National Audit Office's observations. The government works continuously with the question of state presence throughout the country. An important starting point for the government is that agencies can conduct their operations effectively regardless of where they are located. This is something the government monitors within the framework of ongoing agency management.
The Riksdag views positively that the government continuously works with the question of state presence throughout the country. With this, the Riksdag filed the government's letter with the records, that is, concluded the matter, and rejected the motions.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:29 by Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S) point 2.

rubrik: Temporary Ban on Transporting Persons without Valid Identity Documents to Sweden
dok_titel: Temporary Ban on Transporting Persons without Valid Identity Documents to Sweden
forslag_text:
The Riksdag approves the government's proposal for a law on a temporary ban on transporting persons without valid identity documents to Sweden.
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2023/24:62 and rejects the motions 

2023/24:2796 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V), 

2023/24:2806 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) and 

2023/24:2813 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C).
notis:
The government shall be able to introduce rules on a temporary ban on transporting persons without valid identity documents to Sweden from other states. The government shall also be able to introduce penalty fees for transport companies that violate the ban. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.  
A ban may only be introduced if – due to events in the migration field – a serious threat to public order or internal security of the country has arisen, and if the rules are needed for important public functions to more easily be able to perform their tasks.
The new law comes into force on 1 March 2024.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2023/24:2450 by Emma Berginger et al. (MP) demands 44 and 45.
notis: The Riksdag has considered a communication from the government concerning privacy protection in signal intelligence in defense intelligence activities. Signal intelligence is part of Sweden's defense and protection against terrorism and is regulated by law. The State Inspection for Defense Intelligence Activities, Siun, is responsible for ensuring that defense intelligence activities are conducted in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. dok_titel: Report on the use of coercive measures in secret during 2022
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2804 by Rasmus Ling et al. (MP).
notis:
Every year, the government reports to the Riksdag in a document how the crime-fighting authorities use secret wiretapping and other coercive measures in secret. Now the Riksdag has dealt with the document on use during 2022. It addresses how the Public Prosecution Authority, the Economic Crimes Authority, the Police Authority, the Customs Agency, and the Security Police have used secret wiretapping of electronic communications, monitoring of electronic communications, camera surveillance, and room wiretapping.
During 2022, 4,108 permits were issued for secret wiretapping of electronic communications, 13,146 permits for secret monitoring of electronic communications, 239 permits for secret camera surveillance, and 79 permits for secret room wiretapping. The coercive measures in secret were used in 2022 primarily under suspicion of drug-related crime and violent crime.
The Riksdag considers, like the government, that the coercive measures in secret fulfill an important function for investigating crime and that the report shows that the coercive measures in secret have been useful. The Riksdag filed the document, that is, closed the matter.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2801 by Ciczie Weidby et al. (V) demands 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a letter from the government on the Swedish National Audit Office's review of Samhall AB.
The Swedish National Audit Office assesses that both the government's and Samhall's governance have prioritized commercial development too much at the expense of developing the employees' work capacity. The authority's overarching conclusion is that Samhall does not fulfil its entire societal mission.
The Riksdag welcomes both the review and the government's recent decision to appoint an inquiry tasked with conducting a broad review of Samhall's mission, activities and conditions. With this decision, the Riksdag decided to conclude the matter by filing the letter.

rubrik: Proposal for a regulation on strengthened police cooperation regarding migrant smuggling and strengthening Europol's support for preventing and combating such criminal activity
dok_titel: Subsidiarity assessment of the Commission's proposal for a regulation on strengthened police cooperation regarding migrant smuggling and strengthening Europol's support for preventing and combating such criminal activity
forslag_text: The Riksdag decides to submit a reasoned opinion to the presidents of the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission with the wording specified in Annex 2.
notis:
The European Commission has proposed a new regulation on strengthening police cooperation to prevent, detect and investigate migrant smuggling and human trafficking and on strengthening Europol's support for preventing and combating such crimes and amending Regulation (EU) 2016/794.
The Riksdag has assessed the proposal based on the so-called subsidiarity principle. The principle means that the EU may only act if the objectives of a planned action cannot be achieved by the Member States or if the objectives can be better achieved by taking action at the EU level. The principle protects the Member States' right to make their own decisions at the national level.
The Riksdag takes a positive view of the proposal's approach and believes there is a great need for regulation at the EU level to combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking more effectively than today. However, the Committee considers that the European Commission's proposal is too far-reaching in certain respects and therefore violates the subsidiarity principle. This applies to certain parts of the proposals on expanding Europol's operational powers and the proposal that requires Member States to establish specialized units within their national law enforcement authorities.
Against this background, the Riksdag decided to submit its views in a so-called reasoned opinion to the presidents of the European Parliament, the Council and the European Commission.
alternatives: The Riksdag decides to submit a reasoned opinion to the presidents of the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission with the wording specified in Annex 2.

dok_titel: Swedish National Audit Office report on state grants to civil society
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2759 by Lawen Redar et al. (S).
notis:
The Riksdag has addressed a communication from the government concerning the Swedish National Audit Office's report on state grants to civil society.
The National Audit Office has examined whether the state's grants to civil society have been effective. The overall conclusion is that the examined agencies' grant provision is not sufficiently effective and that enhanced control is necessary to maintain and to some extent rebuild confidence in the state grant systems. The National Audit Office submits in the report a number of recommendations to the government. Among other things, to task grant-providing agencies with developing and strengthening their control, for example by increasing the number of risk-based operational visits. Another proposal is to task grant-providing agencies with improving grant recipients' opportunities to meet the grant requirements, for example by providing basic training on what requirements apply to grant-receiving organizations.
The government welcomes the examination and essentially agrees with the National Audit Office's observations. In the communication, the government reports measures taken and planned that are in line with the National Audit Office's observations and recommendations. 
The Riksdag filed the communication for the record, that is, concluded the matter. The Riksdag also rejected motion demands.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2759 by Lawen Redar et al. (S).

dok_titel: Implementation of new requirements for heated tobacco products
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2809 by Carina Ståhl Herrstedt et al. (SD) amendment 1.
notis:
Heated tobacco products with characteristic flavour will be prohibited. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal. Heated tobacco products are something that is heated to produce a release that contains nicotine and other chemicals which is then inhaled by users. Depending on its properties, it can be a smokeless tobacco product or one that is smoked. Furthermore, the government or the authority determined by the government shall be entitled to issue regulations concerning which heated tobacco products shall be considered to have a characteristic flavour.
The legislative amendment is based on an EU directive and is proposed to come into force on 1 May 2024.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2809 by Carina Ståhl Herrstedt et al. (SD) amendment 1.

dok_titel: Implementation of new requirements for heated tobacco products
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion

2023/24:2808 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) request 2.
notis:
It will be prohibited to market heated tobacco products with a characteristic flavor. The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal. Heated tobacco products are products that are heated to produce an emission containing nicotine and other chemicals that is then inhaled by users. Depending on its properties, it can be a smoke-free tobacco product or a product that you smoke. Furthermore, the government or the authority that the government designates shall be authorized to issue regulations on which heated tobacco products should be considered to have a characteristic flavor.
The legislative amendment is based on an EU directive and is proposed to enter into force on May 1, 2024.

2023/24:2628 by Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al. (S) demand 36.
notis:
The Government should investigate how the regulations for local small-scale slaughterhouses can be simplified. The Riksdag holds this view and therefore decided to direct a tillkännagivande (formal request), an appeal, to the Government about this. The Government should also investigate what additional measures are needed to increase the number of small-scale slaughterhouses and mobile slaughterhouses, that is, mobile facilities that are transported to the farm, where slaughter is carried out.
The Riksdag believes that this would counteract long transports of animals to slaughter, as well as contribute to supporting local and small-scale agriculture. Furthermore, the Riksdag sees that it would enable animal husbandry in more parts of the country and increase the supply of locally produced food.
The tillkännagivande was made when the Riksdag considered approximately 160 proposals in motions about animal welfare from the general motion period of 2023. The Riksdag said no to the other motions.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:964 by Per Bolund et al. (MP) request 22, 

2023/24:989 by Lorena Delgado Varas et al. (V) requests 4-6 and 15, 

2023/24:2466 by Kerstin Lundgren et al. (C) request 25, 

2023/24:2669 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) request 112 and 

2023/24:2699 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) request 20.
notis:
The EU ban on trade in seal products should be lifted. In a so-called formal request, Parliament directs an appeal to the government that it shall work for an exemption or to completely lift the ban on trade in seal products. Seal hunting is today permitted, but it is prohibited to sell seal products. Parliament believes that the EU ban complicates sound management of Sweden's growing seal population.
The appeal to the government is based on proposals submitted during the general motion period of 2023. Approximately 100 proposals in trade matters have been submitted. The motions deal, among other things, with international trade, the EU's internal market, and sustainable enterprise. Apart from the formal request on seal products, Parliament rejected the other proposals.

Parliament rejects the motions 

2023/24:1094 by Markus Wiechel and Victoria Tiblom (both SD) requests 1, 2 and 4 and 

2023/24:1525 by Rebecka Le Moine et al. (MP) requests 1-4.
notis:
The government should investigate how the rules for local smaller slaughterhouses can be simplified. This is what Parliament means and therefore decided to direct a formal request, an appeal, to the government about it. The government should also investigate what additional measures are needed to increase the number of small-scale slaughterhouses and mobile slaughterhouses, that is, movable facilities that are transported to the farm, where the slaughter is carried out.
Parliament means that this would counteract long transports of animals to slaughter, as well as contribute to supporting local and small-scale agriculture. Furthermore, Parliament sees that it would enable animal husbandry in more parts of the country and increase the supply of locally produced food.
The formal request was made when Parliament dealt with approximately 160 proposals in motions about animal welfare from the general motion period of 2023. Parliament said no to the other motions.

forslag_text:

2023/24:2810 by Alireza Akhondi and Rickard Nordin (both C).
notis:
According to a new law, car dealers must inform consumers about fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions for the new passenger cars they have for sale or long-term rental. The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal.
Information on fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions shall be available at the point of sale and in advertising for new passenger cars.
The new law is being introduced to clarify the implementation of an EU directive that has previously been implemented through the Consumer Agency's general guidance. The law comes into force on 1 July 2024.

The Riksdag
a) adopts the committee's proposal in Annex 1 to
1. Act on certain surgical procedures in sex organs,
2. Act on determination of sex in certain cases,
3. Act on repeal of the Act (1972:119) on determination of sex in certain cases,
4. Act on amendment to the Sterilization Act (1975:580),
5. Act on amendment to the Patient Data Act (2008:355),
6. Act on amendment to the Discrimination Act (2008:567),
7. Act on amendment to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (2009:400),
8. Act on amendment to the Prisons Act (2010:610),
9. Act on amendment to the Detention Act (2010:611),
10. Act on amendment to the Act (2022:913) on integrated health and care documentation,
b) aligns itself with what the committee states about
1. the need for regulations and notifies this to the Government,
2. national knowledge support and notifies this to the Government.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the Social Committee's proposals for a new Act on certain surgical procedures in sex organs and a new Act on determination of sex in certain cases, as well as a proposal for an Act on repeal of the Act on determination of sex in certain cases.
The proposals mean that the process for changing the sex shown in the population register is separated from the process for surgical procedures in sex organs. No permission from the National Board of Health and Welfare shall be required to undergo such surgical procedures in sex organs aimed at making the person's body correspond to their gender identity. It shall become easier to change sex in the population register.
A person who has reached the age of 16 shall be able to have the sex shown in the population register changed after a simplified review of their gender identity.
The proposal which forms the basis for the decision is what is called a committee initiative. It means that it is a committee which has taken the initiative for it and that it does not come from a Government proposition or motions from members, which otherwise is the usual.
The laws begin to apply on 1 July 2025.
The Riksdag directs four formal requests (tillkännagivanden) to the Government on the need for regulations, national knowledge support, prevention of criminal conduct and monitoring of the application.
Vote on referral
The decision was preceded by a vote on whether the matter should be referred back to the Social Committee, that is sent back to the committee for further consideration.
At the vote on referral, 94 members voted yes, 234 members voted no and 0 members abstained. 21 members were absent.

notis:

rubrik: More concrete measures against violent extremism and terrorism
dok_titel: National strategy against violent extremism and terrorism – prevent, hinder, protect and manage
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion

2023/24:2818 by Rasmus Ling et al. (MP) motions 2-4.
notis:
Parliament has considered a statement from the government on a new comprehensive national strategy against violent extremism and terrorism. The purpose of the strategy is to provide long-term direction for work in Sweden – locally, regionally, nationally and internationally.
The strategy is divided into four areas:

prevent – for example, reduce the growth of violent extremism by preventing the risk of radicalization.
hinder – for example, prevent opportunities for financing and access to weapons
protect – for example, work on protecting the democratic society and
continue identifying risks and vulnerabilities
manage – for example, work on how terrorist attacks or ongoing lethal violence should be handled, as well as focus on the importance of accountability and measures for crime victims.

The new strategy replaces the earlier strategies against violent extremism and terrorism from 2015.
Parliament considers that the strategy creates conditions for broad and long-term work in the area and proposes that Parliament should file the government's statement as a closed matter, i.e., conclude the case.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion

2023/24:2818 by Rasmus Ling et al. (MP) motions 2-4.

dok_titel: The National Audit Office's report on the government's work on waiting times in healthcare
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:2797 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S),

2023/24:2802 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V), and

2023/24:2807 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) amendment 1.
notis:
The Riksdag has reviewed a communication from the government concerning the National Audit Office's report on the government's work on waiting times in healthcare.
The National Audit Office has examined whether several of the policy instruments used by the government to reduce healthcare queues have been effective. The policy instruments are:

The care guarantee, which aims to provide care within certain time limits.
The queue billion 2009–2014, which meant that the state paid out one billion kronor annually between 2009–2014. The money was distributed to regions based on how well they met requirements linked to the care guarantee's time limits within specialist healthcare.
Standardized care pathways in cancer treatment (SVF), which describes, among other things, what investigations and initial treatments should be performed for certain cancer diagnoses.

The examination also concerns whether these policy instruments have affected the goal of equitable healthcare according to need.
The government welcomes the examination and shares the National Audit Office's view that there is a need to review the effectiveness in order to strengthen the patient's position and the importance of the care guarantee as a state policy instrument.
In the communication, the government reports measures taken and planned that are in line with the National Audit Office's findings and recommendations. The Riksdag filed the communication for the record—that is, concluded the matter. The Riksdag also rejected the motion proposals.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:2797 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S),

2023/24:2802 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V), and

2023/24:2807 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) amendment 1.

notis: The Riksdag approved a more comprehensive travel ban for children and young people. Under current legislation, a travel ban is to be issued if there is a significant risk that a person under 18 years is taken abroad to enter into marriage or to undergo female genital mutilation. The government's legislative proposal means that a decision on a travel ban can also be made if there is a significant risk that a child is taken abroad and the child's health or development is harmed during the stay abroad due to circumstances that may lead to care according to the law with special provisions for care of young people (LVU). This can, for example, involve so-called educational trips, conversion attempts, or children who want to leave Sweden to join terrorist organizations and other criminal organizations. The proposal also means that information about children with a travel ban is to be covered by confidentiality at the Police Authority, because it can involve sensitive information about children's personal circumstances. According to the proposal, criminal liability for unauthorized treatment of children is also to be extended to apply when a child under 15 years is taken away or withheld to prevent care according to LVU from being initiated. The legislative changes come into force on 1 June 2024.

2023/24:2825 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) demands 2 and 3.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts
1. 15 p § second paragraph the Government's proposal for a law amending the Act (1990:52) with special provisions on care of young persons,
2. 16 h § second paragraph the Government's proposal for a law amending the Act (1998:603) on the enforcement of closed youth care.
Thereby the Riksdag grants Parliament proposition 2023/24:81 points 1 and 2, both in this respect, and rejects motion 

2023/24:2830 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S) claims 1 and 2.
notis:
Security and safety at special youth homes shall be enhanced. The Riksdag approved the Government's proposals for measures.
Among other things, it is proposed that the State Board of Institutions (Sis) special youth homes shall be divided into security levels.
Those who are cared for under the Act with special provisions on care of young persons at a special youth home with elevated security level and those who serve closed youth care under the Act on the enforcement of closed youth care shall only be permitted to use electronic communications services such as, for example, mobile telephony and the internet, to communicate with another person if the equipment has been offered by Sis, approved by Sis and if it is deemed appropriate.
Sis is also proposed to gain expanded opportunities to decide on restrictions and control of visits. A visit shall, for example, be able to be conditional upon the visitor undergoing body search on grounds of security if necessary. Sis shall also be able to investigate whether the person the child or young person wishes to communicate with or receive visits from has been convicted of or is suspected of committing a crime.
The amendments to the law come into force on 15 May 2024.
alternatives:
The Riksdag adopts
1. 15 p § second paragraph the Government's proposal for a law amending the Act (1990:52) with special provisions on care of young persons,
2. 16 h § second paragraph the Government's proposal for a law amending the Act (1998:603) on the enforcement of closed youth care.
Thereby the Riksdag grants Parliament proposition 2023/24:81 points 1 and 2, both in this respect, and rejects motion

forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts 31 a § the Government's proposal for a law amending the Act (1990:52) with special provisions on care of young persons.
Thereby the Riksdag grants Parliament proposition 2023/24:72 point 2 in this respect and rejects motion 

2023/24:2823 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S).
notis:
The Riksdag approved a more extensive exit ban for children and young persons.
Under current legislation, an exit ban shall be issued if there is a substantial risk that a person under 18 years of age is taken abroad to marry or to undergo female genital mutilation. The Government's legislative proposal means that decisions on exit bans may also be taken if there is a substantial risk that a child is taken abroad and the child's health or development is damaged during the stay abroad due to circumstances that may lead to care under the Act with special provisions on care of young persons, LVU.
This may, for example, involve so-called upbringing trips, conversion attempts or children who wish to leave Sweden to join terrorist organisations and other criminal organisations.
The proposal also means that information about children with exit bans shall be subject to confidentiality at the Police Authority, since it may involve sensitive information about children's personal circumstances.
Under the proposal, criminal liability for kidnapping of a child shall also be expanded to apply when a child under 15 years of age is removed or withheld in order to prevent care under LVU from commencing.
The amendments to the law come into force on 1 June 2024.

dok_titel: Resilience and capability – a national strategy against organized crime
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2821 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) demands 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has addressed a dispatch from the government on a national strategy against organized crime. The aim of the strategy is to clarify the direction of work against organized crime and reduce the vulnerabilities that crime exploits. The government identifies five goals to guide the work:

Stop criminal careers, for example counteracting the recruitment of young people into crime.
Reduce access to illegal weapons and explosives, for example by improving efforts against smuggling.
Dismantle the criminal economy, for example preventing the misuse of public funds.
Build resilience against unauthorized and improper influence, for example by developing a new action plan against corruption.
Ensure reliable identities and effective information provision, for example by improving opportunities to exchange information.

The Riksdag placed the dispatch on record, that is, concluded the case. The Riksdag also rejected proposals in motions, of which eight are from the general motion period 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2821 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) demands 1 and 2.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for
1. an act amending the Land Code,
2. an act amending the Act (1973:188) on lease disputes and rent disputes committees,
3. an act amending the Rent Negotiation Act (1978:304),
4. an act amending the Legal Aid Act (1996:1619).
Thereby the Riksdag passes government bill 2023/24:112 points 1-4 and rejects the motions

2023/24:2861 by Jennie Nilsson et al. (S) proposal 8,

2023/24:2862 by Alireza Akhondi et al. (C) proposals 1 and 6,

2023/24:2863 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (V) proposal 1, and

2023/24:2864 by Katarina Luhr et al. (MP) proposal 5.
notis:
To create safer residential areas throughout the country, the Government has proposed that property owners should get expanded opportunities to terminate rental agreements with tenants who commit crimes. A rental agreement may be terminated if the tenant commits a crime that typically worsens the immediate environment for those living in the building's surroundings. The responsibility that the tenant has for children and other persons living or present in the apartment should also apply to ensuring that these persons do not commit crimes that create insecurity for other residents. A rental agreement may further be terminated in more cases if the apartment is used to commit crimes, namely in cases of serious or extensive criminality. Additionally, the tenant's obligation to maintain security within the property is clarified and strengthened.
To counteract misuse of the rules on subletting, the tenant's right to admit outside persons into the apartment will be tightened. The property owner will also get better opportunities to control how an apartment is used.
The proposals also provide improved conditions for a tenant who has been subjected to violence by a close relative to retain the apartment when a termination is made. Furthermore, the opportunities are strengthened for a co-tenant or cohabiting spouse or partner who has been subjected to violence by a close relative to take over a rental agreement.
The Riksdag said yes to the proposals and the legislative changes begin to apply on 1 July 2024.
alternatives:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for
1. an act amending the Land Code,
2. an act amending the Act (1973:188) on lease disputes and rent disputes committees,
3. an act amending the Rent Negotiation Act (1978:304),
4. an act amending the Legal Aid Act (1996:1619).
Thereby the Riksdag passes government bill 2023/24:112 points 1-4 and rejects the motions

dok_titel: Making it easier to study at a faster pace and at a higher level
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts
a) the Government's proposal for an act amending the Education Act (2010:800), bill 2.1, in the parts concerning chapter 10, sections 6 and 23 h and chapter 23, section 12 b,
b) the Government's proposal for an act amending the Education Act (2010:800), bill 2.2, in the parts concerning chapter 10, sections 6 and 23 h and chapter 23, section 12 b,
c) chapter 10, section 23 i of the Government's proposal for an act amending the Education Act (2010:800), bill 2.1,
d) chapter 10, section 23 i of the Government's proposal for an act amending the Education Act (2010:800), bill 2.2.
Thereby the Riksdag passes government bill 2023/24:79 points 1 and 2, both in this part, and rejects the motion

2023/24:2826 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S) proposal 2.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal which provides better opportunities for students in primary school, special school and Sami school to study at a higher level and for students in upper secondary school to progress at a faster study pace.
Certain primary school students with particular talent or who are high-performing may need an education in a specially adapted study environment where there are opportunities for daily exchange of experience and shared learning with other students with the same aptitude and interest. The Riksdag considers the Government's proposal to introduce elite education permanently to be valuable and will be significant for students who today do not receive sufficient challenges at school.
The new regulations begin to apply on 2 July 2024. Certain regulations begin to apply on 1 July 2025.

dok_titel: A clearer provision on hate speech targeting ethnic groups
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2859 by Matheus Enholm et al. (SD).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal for amendment to the Penal Code and adopted as standing the government's proposals for amendments to the Freedom of the Press Ordinance.
The amendments mean that the provisions on hate speech targeting ethnic groups are clarified. The clarifications mean, among other things, that denial of the Holocaust and certain other international crimes are explicitly criminalized.
The proposals also mean that individual persons in protected groups shall be given protection, victim status and the right to compensation.
The changes to the Penal Code begin to apply on 1 July 2024. The changes to the Freedom of the Press Ordinance the Riksdag said yes to as standing and they shall begin to apply on 1 January 2027. Since parts of the proposals concern an amendment to the Freedom of the Press Ordinance, a basic law, the Riksdag must vote equally twice on the proposal and there must be an election between the votes.

notis:
To create safer residential areas throughout the country, the Government has proposed that property owners be given expanded opportunities to terminate leases of tenants who commit crimes. A lease agreement can be terminated if the tenant commits a crime that typically worsens the immediate surroundings for those living in the vicinity of the apartment. The responsibility that the tenant has for children and other persons who live or stay in the apartment shall also apply to ensuring that these persons do not commit crimes that create insecurity for other residents. A lease agreement can further be terminated in more cases if the apartment is used to commit a crime, namely in cases of serious or extensive criminal activity. Furthermore, the tenant's obligation to maintain safety within the property is clarified and strengthened.
To prevent misuse of the rules on lodgers, the tenant's right to accommodate third parties in the apartment is restricted. The landlord shall also have better opportunities to control how an apartment is used.
The proposals also provide improved conditions for a tenant who has been subjected to violence by a close relative to retain the apartment in the event of a termination. Furthermore, the possibilities for a co-tenant or co-resident spouse or partner who has been subjected to violence by a close relative to take over a lease agreement are strengthened.
Parliament approved the proposals and the legislative amendments come into force on 1 July 2024.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag approves the delivery security target that the government proposes shall apply to the electricity system.

2023/24:2845 by Birger Lahti et al. (V) in this respect,

2023/24:2853 by Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S, C) demands 2 and 4 and

notis:
The government proposes two new goals for Sweden's electricity system: a planning goal and a delivery security goal. The Riksdag proposes that the Riksdag shall say yes to the proposal.
The planning goal means that the electricity system shall provide conditions for delivering the electricity that is needed for increased electrification and to make the green transition possible. The goal shall facilitate planning to be able to meet an electricity demand of at least 300 TWh in 2045.
The delivery security goal means that the Swedish electricity system shall have the ability to deliver electricity where demand exists, at the right time and in sufficient quantity, to the extent that it is economically efficient for society. The authority Swedish National Grid shall be responsible for regular follow-ups of the goal.
The Riksdag said no to proposals in motions in the energy policy area, including approximately 130 proposals in motions from the general motion period 2023.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:2822 by Mats Berglund et al. (MP) demands 1 and 2, and

2023/24:2835 by Mats Berglund et al. (MP) demands 2 and 3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal that reimbursement for high sick leave costs should cease. The reimbursement scheme, which has existed for just under ten years, means that employers in certain cases have the right to reimbursement from the state for their sick leave costs. The Riksdag agrees with the government's description of the current economic situation and the need for public funds to be used efficiently. Like the government, the Riksdag also emphasizes that control possibilities are limited and increase the risk of erroneous payments.
The provisions regarding the reimbursement shall, according to the proposal, cease to apply at the end of June 2024, but reimbursement shall still be able to be paid out for certain costs relating to the time before that.
In addition to the bill, the Riksdag also considered a communication from the government regarding the Swedish National Audit Office's report on the system for reimbursement for high sick leave costs. In the communication, the government assesses that there is no reason to take any action based on the Swedish National Audit Office's findings since the reimbursement scheme, according to the government's proposal, shall be abolished.
Against this background, the Riksdag filed the communication as handled, that is, concluded the matter.

rubrik: Tightened requirements for acquiring Swedish citizenship by declaration
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for
a) a law amending the Citizenship Act (2001:82) in the parts concerning sections 6–10, 18, 19 and 27, as well as point 4 of the transitional provisions of the Instrument of Government, 
b) a law amending the Act (2014:481) amending the Citizenship Act (2001:82).
Thereby the Riksdag approves Government bill 2023/24:107, points 1 in this part and 2, and rejects the motions 

2023/24:2847 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) amendments 1-8, and 

2023/24:2857 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) amendments 1, 2, 4 and 5.
notis:
The Riksdag approved changes to the citizenship law.
A person can acquire Swedish citizenship at birth, by adoption, by declaration, or by application. The Government proposes that the requirements for acquiring Swedish citizenship by declaration should be tightened.
The proposed provisions mean that a person who is reasonably suspected of or convicted of certain criminal offences, constitutes a threat to Sweden's security or public safety, or has connections to certain groups and organizations, shall not be able to acquire Swedish citizenship by declaration. The provisions shall, with certain exceptions, apply to everyone who has reached 15 years of age. According to the Government, the significance of Swedish citizenship needs to be strengthened both legally and symbolically.
The Government also proposes that the possibilities to reject an application for exemption from Swedish citizenship should be expanded. The aim is to strengthen the protection of children and adults in vulnerable situations.
The legislative changes shall come into force on 1 October 2024.
alternatives:

forslag_text:
The Riksdag
a) adopts the government's proposal for
1. act amending the Act (1991:1047) on sick leave,
2. act repealing the Act (2014:1475) on crediting to tax account for compensation for sick leave costs,
b) approves what the committee states regarding the government's proposal for an act amending the Act (2001:181) on processing of data in the Tax Agency's tax assessment activities.

2023/24:2835 by Mats Berglund et al. (MP) proposal 1,

2023/24:2839 by Isabell Mixter et al. (V) and

2023/24:2841 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal to cease compensation for high sick leave costs.
The compensation scheme, which has existed for nearly ten years, means that employers in certain cases have the right to compensation from the state for their sick leave costs. The Riksdag agrees with the government's description of the current economic situation and the need for public funds to be used in an efficient manner. Like the government, the Riksdag emphasizes among other things that control possibilities are limited and increase the risk of incorrect payments.
The provisions on the compensation are according to the proposal to cease to apply at the end of June 2024, but compensation shall still be able to be paid for certain costs relating to time before that.
Beyond the proposition, the Riksdag has also considered a written communication from the government concerning the National Audit Office's report on the system for compensation for high sick leave costs. In the communication, the government assesses that there is no reason to take any measures based on the National Audit Office's observations as the compensation scheme is according to the government's proposal to be abolished.
In light of this, the Riksdag laid the written communication to the records, that is, closed the matter.

notis:
The Riksdag voted yes to the Government's proposal to temporarily raise the ceiling for the home repair deduction. This means that the ceiling for the home repair deduction will be temporarily raised and that separate ceilings for home repair and home services deductions will be temporarily introduced.
During the tax year 2024, the ceiling for the home repair deduction shall be 75,000 kronor per person and 75,000 kronor per person for the home services deduction. Until June 30, 2024, however, a maximum of 50,000 kronor can be used for the home repair deduction and a maximum of 75,000 kronor in total for home repair and home services deductions.
The temporarily raised ceiling aims to temporarily promote employment in the construction sector during the economic downturn in the Swedish economy. The provisions may be applied to household work that has been paid for, benefits of household work that has been provided, and household work that has been reported in a simplified employer declaration during the tax year 2024.
The new rules enter into force on July 1, 2024 and expire at the end of the year.
