rubrik: Overarching measures for a circular and non-toxic economy
dok_titel: Circular and non-toxic economy and the Swedish National Audit Office's report on the management of spent solar cell panels and wind turbine blades
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:438 by Andrea Andersson Tay et al. (V) point 2 and

2023/24:996 by Per Bolund et al. (MP) points 9, 10 and 13.
notis:
The Riksdag has dealt with a letter from the government concerning the Swedish National Audit Office's report on the management of spent solar cell panels and wind turbine blades. The Swedish National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the government, the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency and the Swedish Energy Agency have not ensured that spent solar cell panels and wind turbine blades can be managed in a non-toxic and circular manner. The Swedish National Audit Office's recommendations to the government include, among other things, reviewing the need for policy instruments to promote such management.
In its letter, the government agrees with the Swedish National Audit Office's findings and at the same time points to measures that have been taken, including that the government has tasked the Swedish Energy Agency with investigating how solar cell panels and wind turbine blades for wind power plants to a greater extent can be managed in accordance with the so-called waste hierarchy.
The Riksdag believes that the measures the government presents partly correspond to what the Swedish National Audit Office is requesting. At the same time, the Riksdag emphasizes that the work needs to be intensified to achieve sustainable management of these products. With this, the committee proposes that the Riksdag places the government's letter on file, that is, closes the matter.
The Riksdag also said no to approximately 180 proposals on circular and non-toxic economy in motions from the general motion period in 2023, partly with reference to ongoing work. The motions concern, among other things, sustainable design, consumption and production, reuse and recycling, waste, circular food issues, plastic issues and chemical issues.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2023/24:438 by Andrea Andersson Tay et al. (V) point 2 and

2023/24:996 by Per Bolund et al. (MP) points 9, 10 and 13.

forslag_text:

2023/24:462 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V) items 12, 22 and 23,

2023/24:2873 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V) item 8 and

2023/24:2880 by Yasmine Eriksson et al. (SD) item 1.
notis:
Parliament decided to file the government's document on strategic export control, which meant that the matter was concluded.
Since 1985, the government has reported on its policy regarding Swedish exports of military equipment and dual-use products. The document contains an account of the military equipment exports that occurred during 2023. Furthermore, the government describes cooperation within the EU and in other international forums regarding strategic export control of military equipment and dual-use products. The government also reports on Sweden's donations of military material to Ukraine and on the consequences for export control of Sweden's application for NATO membership.
Parliament also rejected seven proposals in motions concerning export control of military equipment and dual-use products from the general motion period of 2023. The motions deal, for example, with reviewing current legislation and with the application of legislation becoming more restrictive or in certain cases more generous.
Parliament refers, among other things, to ongoing investigative work and current regulations.

forslag_text:

2023/24:2629 by Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al. (S) item 34.
notis:
Parliament has dealt with a document from the government concerning the National Audit Office's report on the management of discarded solar panels and wind turbine blades. The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the government, the Environmental Protection Agency and the Energy Agency have not ensured that discarded solar panels and wind turbine blades can be managed in a non-toxic and circular manner. The National Audit Office's recommendations to the government include, among other things, reviewing the need for policy instruments to promote such management.
In its document, the government agrees with the National Audit Office's findings and at the same time points to measures that have been taken, including that the government has tasked the Energy Agency with investigating how solar panels and wind turbine blades can be managed to a greater extent in accordance with the so-called waste hierarchy.
Parliament considers that the measures presented by the government partly correspond to what the National Audit Office calls for. At the same time, Parliament emphasizes that the work needs to be intensified to achieve sustainable management of these products. On this basis, the committee proposes that Parliament files the government's document, that is, concludes the matter.
Parliament also rejected approximately 180 proposals concerning circular and non-toxic economy in motions from the general motion period of 2023, partly with reference to ongoing work. The motions deal, among other things, with sustainable design, consumption and production, reuse and recycling, waste, circular food issues, plastic issues and chemical issues.

Parliament approves the guidelines for economic policy that the government proposes.
Thereby parliament grants proposition 2023/24:100 points 1 and 2 and rejects the motions 

2023/24:790 by Markus Kallifatides (S), 

2023/24:1519 by Elin Söderberg et al. (MP) request 14,

2023/24:2893 by Daniel Helldén et al. (MP) and 

2023/24:2894 by Magdalena Andersson et al. (S).
notis:
Parliament said yes to the government's proposal for guidelines for economic policy in the spring economic bill.
Economic policy should be directed towards laying the foundation for recovery, higher growth and better welfare, as inflation falls while the effects of the economic downturn become increasingly apparent. Parliament shares the government's assessment that although there are large uncertainties, there is now room for directing policy towards more normal cyclical policy and investing in Sweden. A low government debt and strong public finances provide room for further investments for higher growth. Through a well-balanced fiscal policy, inflation should continue to be combated. The work line should be restored and structural reforms should be implemented to increase productivity and improve long-term growth. Sweden should be built stronger and richer through investments in infrastructure, climate transition, research, energy production, regulatory simplifications and skills supply, and by continuing the work to reduce crime. Tax policy is a central part of economic policy and should encourage entrepreneurship, enterprise, hard work and higher education.

dok_titel: Agreement on defense cooperation with the United States
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motion 

2023/24:2902 by Emma Berginger et al. (MP) demand 3.
notis:
Parliament approved the agreement on defense cooperation between Sweden and the United States. The agreement is a so-called defense cooperation agreement (DCA agreement) and regulates the specific conditions for American military presence in Sweden.
It concerns, among other things, the legal status of American military personnel, contractors and family members. The agreement also regulates the United States' right of access to Swedish territory and the right to use certain installations here.
Parliament also voted yes to the government's proposals for legislative changes, which are required for Sweden to fulfill its commitments under the DCA agreement. The legislative changes take effect on the day the government decides.

rubrik: The Future Design of Unemployment Insurance
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2023/24:2881 by Ciczie Weidby et al. (V) demand 2, 

2023/24:2884 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) demands 1 and 4, 

2023/24:2886 by Jonny Cato et al. (C) and 

2023/24:2888 by Leila Ali Elmi et al. (MP) demands 1-12.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal that the right to unemployment benefits should be based on income and that those applying for unemployment benefits must meet an income requirement. The same income that formed the basis for the applicant's right to unemployment benefits shall be used in calculating the amount of the benefit. The benefit level shall be based on how long the applicant has been a member of an unemployment insurance fund. Unemployment benefits shall be gradually reduced while the applicant is unemployed. The length of the benefit period shall vary depending on how established the applicant is in the labor market.
The legal changes enter into force on 1 October 2025.

rubrik: Preventive Coercive Measures to Prevent and Hinder Serious Crimes
dok_titel: Preventive Coercive Measures to Prevent and Hinder Serious Crimes
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for 
1. Act amending the Act (2007:979) on measures to prevent certain particularly serious crimes,
2. Act amending the Act (2023:538) on amendment of the Act (2007:979) on measures to prevent certain particularly serious crimes,
3. Act amending the Act (2007:979) on measures to prevent certain particularly serious crimes,
4. Act amending the Act (2007:980) on supervision of certain crime prevention activities, amended to delete the word "that" in the preamble in the expression "shall have the following wording",
5. Act amending the Act (2012:278) on obtaining information about electronic communications in the crime prevention authorities' intelligence activities,
6. Act amending the Act (2012:278) on obtaining information about electronic communications in the crime prevention authorities' intelligence activities, 
7. Act amending the Act (2020:62) on secret data inspection,
8. Act amending the Act (2022:700) on special control of certain aliens.
Thereby the Riksdag grants proposition 2023/24:117 items 1-8 and rejects the motions 

2023/24:2876 by Rasmus Ling et al. (MP) demands 2, 3 and 7 and 

2023/24:2879 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) demand 5.
notis:
Law enforcement authorities receive expanded opportunities to use preventive coercive measures. The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal on legislative amendments aimed at strengthening the conditions for preventing and hindering serious crime.
The legal amendments concern, among other things:

information about certain electronic communications can be obtained for more types of crime
more coercive measures and enforcement measures, for example, secret room eavesdropping and house searches, shall be able to be used
remote searches, for example, searches of external servers, shall be able to be used in alien matters with qualified security aspects
the legal protection of the individual shall be strengthened, among other things through expanded prohibitions on eavesdropping and surveillance.

The legal amendments enter into force on 1 September 2024. Several of the legal amendments are time-limited until the end of September 2028.
alternatives:

7. Act amending the Act (2020:62) on secret data inspection,
8. Act amending the Act (2022:700) on special control of certain aliens.

forslag_text:

notis:
Parliament has dealt with a statement from the government regarding the National Audit Office's examination of subsidised employment. That is, employment where the state, following a decision by the Public Employment Service, pays part of the wage costs, but in other respects has the same conditions as ordinary employment, and whether this is effective or not.
The results of the examination are presented in the report Subsidised Employment – Countering Errors in a System with Serious Risks. Among other things, the assessment is made that the checks which the Public Employment Service performs when a subsidised employment is granted are ineffective, often due to neglected IT systems and cumbersome administration. The National Audit Office also assesses that the government has designed the subsidised employment in a way that entails risks of abuse, and this applies especially to start-up jobs. The report contains three recommendations to the government and three recommendations to the Public Employment Service.
The Labour Market Committee welcomes the National Audit Office's examination, not least because abuse of subsidised employment in certain cases involves systematic and organised economic crime. The Committee notes that the government has taken a number of measures in response to the National Audit Office's findings.
With this, Parliament laid the government's statement on the table and rejected the motions.

dok_titel: Improved living conditions for foreign nationals with temporary protection
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2917 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) demand 2.
notis:
The Government has proposed legislative changes concerning persons who have been granted a residence permit in Sweden with temporary protection. The Riksdag agreed to the changes.
The legislative changes mean, among other things, that a person who has been granted a residence permit with temporary protection shall be able to be registered earlier than current rules allow. This in turn means, for example, that the person can be offered the same healthcare and dental care as other residents. It also means opportunities to receive work-based parental benefits at certain levels and temporary parental benefits.
Persons covered by the new regulation shall, according to the proposal, not be entitled to residence-based benefits and shall not be entitled to services under the Act on Support and Service for Certain Disabled Persons (LSS).
A residence permit with temporary protection is a form of residence permit enabled by the EU's so-called mass flight directive. The directive was activated for the first time in connection with Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 November 2024.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2023/24:2917 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) demand 2.

Among other things, the National Audit Office points out the difficulties in the state's attempts to govern health and medical care so that the entire population has access to equitable care, while municipal self-governance requires coordination to reduce regional cost differences in pharmaceutical use.

Regarding the National Audit Office's other recommendations, the Government intends to return with proposals for measures in the area.

rubrik: The Role of Kammarkollegiet (Supreme Administrative Court of Appeal) as a Party to Administrative Proceedings
dok_titel: Steps Towards More Efficient Environmental Review
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the Environmental Code in those sections concerning chapter 22, section 4, first paragraph and section 6, chapter 24, sections 11, 12, and 18, and chapter 25, section 3.
Thereby, the Riksdag approves proposition 2023/24:152 point 1 in this respect and rejects motion

2023/24:2916 by Emma Nohrén et al. (MP) point 3.
notis:
The Riksdag voted in favor of the government's proposal for steps towards more efficient environmental review. The purpose of the law changes is to create a more modern and efficient environmental review and to simplify the regulatory framework through greater uniformity and clearer requirement levels.
Among other things, so-called modification permits (ändringstillstånd) shall be able to be used to a greater extent than today, in order that the willingness to invest is not hindered and that the implementation of new technology is not delayed. Furthermore, the validity period of time-limited permits shall be able to be extended by three years.
The law changes also mean that the county administrative board's (länsstyrelsen's) tasks under the scoping consultation (avgränsningssamrådet) shall be developed to increase the possibility of obtaining good background material. The number of party authorities is also reduced as Kammarkollegiet (Supreme Administrative Court of Appeal) shall no longer be such an authority.
Further, changes are made so that more oral proceedings are held and the use of schedules increases. Furthermore, more cases shall be decided without main hearings and the scope for digital processing shall increase.
The new provisions shall enter into force on 1 January 2025.
alternatives:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the Environmental Code in those sections concerning chapter 22, section 4, first paragraph and section 6, chapter 24, sections 11, 12, and 18, and chapter 25, section 3.
Thereby, the Riksdag approves proposition 2023/24:152 point 1 in this respect and rejects motion

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2024/25:552 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) point 3.
notis:
Unemployed people without education face greater difficulties in finding employment. Furthermore, a report from the Swedish National Audit Office shows that the group to a lesser extent trains for available jobs. The Riksdag has considered a letter from the government based on the Swedish National Audit Office's examination of how effectively the Swedish Public Employment Service works to increase the transition of low-educated job seekers to regular education.
The Swedish National Audit Office points to deficiencies in the Swedish Public Employment Service's work and in the government's steering of the Swedish Public Employment Service. In the letter, the government accounts for the measures it has taken to enable more people to find employment.
The Riksdag welcomes the government's initiatives concerning how an educated workforce can better meet labor market demand and thereby uphold the employment-focused approach. The Riksdag laid the government's letter on the table, which meant that the matter was concluded.

dok_titel: A living sea – increased protection, reduced eutrophication and sustainable fishing

2024/25:142 by Emma Nohrén et al. (MP) motions 22-25, 66 and 69, and

2024/25:3037 by Daniel Helldén et al. (MP) motions 28, 29, 31, 32, 35.1 and 48.
notis:
Parliament voted yes to the government's proposal on the direction of marine environmental policy.
The proposal contains overarching principles that shall apply to all marine environmental work.
The government wants to strengthen the use of the so-called ecosystem approach, a working method for conservation and sustainable long-term use of natural resources, biological diversity and ecosystem services. Among other things, work on sustainable management of fish resources should be more clearly coordinated with other marine environmental work.
Other starting points are that eutrophication should decrease and that Sweden should expand and strengthen protection of marine areas.
The proposal also emphasizes the need for Sweden to continue to work internationally to reduce the supply of hazardous substances to the marine environment, and to actively work for the EU's chemical strategy for sustainability to be implemented.
Parliament also voted no to proposals in motions, of which 70 motions come from the general motion period 2024.

forslag_text:

1. Act amending the Dental Care Act (1985:125),
2. Act amending the Act (2008:145) on state dental care support.
Thereby the Riksdag adopts proposition 2023/24:158 points 1 and 2 and rejects the motions

notis: The Riksdag approved lowering the age limit for free children's and young people's dental care from 23 to 19 years. The government assesses that lowering the age limit for free dental care creates resources and capacity for a reform of dental care's high-cost protection, where older people with the poorest oral health will be prioritized. Young adults between 20 and 23 years old will be able to receive state dental care support instead of free dental care. State dental care support is financial support consisting of general dental care grants, special dental care grants, and protection against high costs. The new law comes into force on January 1, 2025.

According to the proposal, witnesses shall be able to provide their information under anonymity if there is a substantial risk that they or their relatives are exposed to serious criminal activity.
To provide information anonymously, the penalty for the crime in question must correspond to at least two years' imprisonment. The reasons for anonymity must also outweigh the difficulties it entails for the suspected or accused person's ability to prepare and carry out their defence.
The purpose of the new rules is to strengthen protection for witnesses and break the silence culture in and around criminal gangs. In this way, the ability to investigate and solve crimes shall be improved.
The amendments to the law come into force on 1 January 2025.

notis:
The Riksdag approved expenditure frames and revenue calculation in the government's budget proposition for 2025. Expenditure is calculated to amount to 1,428 billion kronor and revenues are calculated to amount to 1,374 billion kronor. This means a deficit in the state budget of 55 billion kronor for 2025.
The Riksdag approved the expenditure ceiling for the state and approved proposals for tax and fee rules that include, among other things:

strengthening of the ordinary work tax deduction and the increased basic deduction
removal of the phasing-out at higher income levels within the framework of the work tax deduction, work tax deduction for the elderly and the increased basic deduction
reduced replacement rate in the cap rule for expert tax
reduced tax on petrol and diesel
abrogation of air travel tax
expansion of the so-called grow-support
a tax-free level for savings in investment savings accounts and capital insurance
phased interest deduction for unsecured loans
changed bonus malus for motorhomes and alternative fuel vehicles.

Some of these proposals have been presented in separate propositions, but are announced in the budget proposition and are included in the calculation of revenues in the budget.
All amendments to the law shall come into force on 1 January 2025 except those relating to the abolition of air travel tax which come into force on 1 July 2025 and changed malus for motorhomes and alternative fuel vehicles which come into force on 1 February 2025.
The Riksdag also approved the government's direction for economic policy and fiscal policy.
Lower inflation and stable long-term inflation expectations mean that the focus of economic policy can now shift from fighting inflation to investing in making Sweden richer and safer again. According to the government, policy should be aimed at continuing to strengthen household purchasing power, restore the work line and increase growth. The Riksdag shares this view. The somewhat expansionary fiscal policy provides support for the economic downturn that Sweden is estimated to be in even in 2025. Lower inflation, higher real wages and lower interest rates contribute to household consumption and investments being expected to increase. The labour market recovers gradually during 2025, but unemployment is expected to remain high in 2025.
The Riksdag's decision on the expenditure frames for the state budget is binding when the Riksdag in the next step decides on appropriations for the 27 expenditure areas in the budget.

The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for
1. act on anonymous witnesses in criminal proceedings,
2. act on amendment to the Code of Judicial Procedure with the amendment that Section 5, Chapter 1 shall have the wording that the Committee proposes in Annex 3,
3. act on amendment to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (2009:400) with the amendment that Section 35, Chapter 7 shall have the wording that the Committee proposes in Annex 3.
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2024/25:20 points 1-3 and rejects the motions

2024/25:2703 by Ann-Sofie Lifvenhage (M),

2024/25:3227 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V),

2024/25:3229 by Rasmus Ling et al. (MP) demand 1 and

2024/25:3230 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C).
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to make it possible to testify anonymously during preliminary investigation and criminal proceedings in court. According to the proposal, witnesses shall be able to provide their information under anonymity if there is a substantial risk that they or their relatives are exposed to serious criminal activity.
To provide information anonymously, the penalty for the crime in question must correspond to at least two years' imprisonment. The reasons for anonymity must also outweigh the difficulties it entails for the suspected or accused person's ability to prepare and carry out their defence.
The purpose of the new rules is to strengthen protection for witnesses and break the silence culture in and around criminal gangs. In this way, the ability to investigate and solve crimes shall be improved.
The amendments to the law come into force on 1 January 2025.

notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to strengthen child protection against violence in the home and to strengthen the security and stability of children placed in foster care.
The proposals mean that special consideration shall be given to the risk that a child may be harmed when assessing what is in the best interest of the child in matters of custody, residence and contact.
This shall be achieved through the following changes.

Improve the district courts' decision basis when assessing whether a child risks being harmed. In difficult cases or matters concerning custody, residence and contact, the court shall request an expert opinion from a licensed psychologist.
A child's right to contact with a parent the child does not live with shall only apply when the contact is consistent with the child's best interest.
It shall be clarified which circumstances shall be taken into special consideration for it to become relevant to transfer custody from the child's parents to specially appointed guardians. When such assessment is conducted by the social committee and in court, a public representative shall as a rule be appointed for the child and its guardians.

The amendments to the law come into force on 1 January 2025.

According to the government, policy should be aimed at continuing to strengthen household purchasing power, restore the work line and increase growth. The Riksdag agrees. The somewhat expansionary fiscal policy provides support to the economic downturn that Sweden is assessed to be in even in 2025. Lower inflation, higher real wages and lower interest rates contribute to household consumption and investments being expected to increase. The labour market recovers gradually during 2025, but unemployment is expected to remain high in 2025.
The Riksdag's decision on the expenditure framework for the state budget is binding when the Riksdag in the next step decides on appropriations for the 27 spending areas in the budget.

dok_titel: Seclusion in connection with rest period – for increased safety and security at special youth homes
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the Government's proposal for
1. amendment to the Act (1990:52) containing special provisions on the care of young people,
2. amendment to the Act (1998:603) on the implementation of closed youth care.
Thereby Parliament approves proposition 2024/25:41 items 1 and 2 and rejects the motions

2024/25:3260 by Maj Karlsson et al. (V) demand 1,

2024/25:3261 by Martina Johansson et al. (C) demand 1 and

2024/25:3262 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) demand 1.
notis:
According to a government proposal, the State Institutions Board (Statens institutionsstyrelse), SiS, should be given the opportunity in certain cases to keep children and young people in seclusion in connection with rest periods at special youth homes. Parliament voted in favour of the government's proposal.
Seclusion in connection with rest periods can take place if it is necessary with regard to order or safety at the special youth home. Another reason may be to prevent the child or young person from absconding from the home. The purpose of the proposal is to increase safety and security.
The proposal applies to children and young people who are cared for in a lockable unit at a special youth home with enhanced security or who are serving a closed youth sentence.
The legislative changes come into force on 15 December 2024.

Sweden's support to Ukraine shall be sustainable and long-term

rubrik: Information to be provided in connection with the employer declaration
dok_titel: Information to be provided in connection with the employer declaration
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for
1. an act on information requirements regarding absence due to care of children,
2. an act amending the Act (2001:181) on the treatment of data in the Swedish Tax Agency's tax assessment activities,
3. an act amending the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (2009:400).
Thus the Riksdag approves proposition 2024/25:36 points 1-3 and rejects motion

2024/25:3249 by Anders W Jonsson (C) demand 1.
notis:
The Government has proposed that information about employees' absences shall be provided to the Swedish Tax Agency. This applies in cases where the absence could entitle the employee to parental benefit or temporary parental benefit, so-called care of children (vab). The Riksdag approved the proposal.
According to the proposal, the Swedish Tax Agency shall collect the information in connection with the employer declaration, which shall then be transferred to the Swedish Social Insurance Agency. The Swedish Social Insurance Agency uses the information in its monitoring of parental benefit entitlements.
The Government's proposal also contains a confidentiality provision that shall apply if information about an absence does not fall within this type of matter at the Swedish Social Insurance Agency.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 January 2025.
alternatives:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for
1. an act on information requirements regarding absence due to care of children,
2. an act amending the Act (2001:181) on the treatment of data in the Swedish Tax Agency's tax assessment activities,
3. an act amending the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (2009:400).
Thus the Riksdag approves proposition 2024/25:36 points 1-3 and rejects motion

2024/25:3249 by Anders W Jonsson (C) demand 1.

notis:
Asylum seekers shall as a main rule only be entitled to financial assistance if they exclusively reside in the asylum accommodation that they have been assigned. The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal.
The new rules mean that the Migration Board will have the opportunity to inspect spaces in asylum accommodations in order to control that asylum seekers reside at the assigned accommodation place. The purpose is to ensure that asylum seekers do not live in exclusion or economic and social hardship, and is a prerequisite for the asylum process and return work to function effectively.
Furthermore, an application for a residence permit shall be considered withdrawn for asylum seekers who do not reside in an asylum accommodation and have not notified the Migration Board of their residential address. In addition, a statutory obligation is introduced for asylum seekers to participate in community integration.
The new rules begin to apply on 1 March 2025.

2024/25:3075 by Jennie Nilsson et al. (S) request 8, and

2024/25:3274 by Katarina Luhr et al. (MP) request 3.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal that should create better conditions for municipalities' work with housing provision.
The legislative changes include, among other things, certain clarifications regarding municipal housing mediations. Such a housing mediation shall primarily mediate apartments in queue order according to waiting time in order to have the right to charge a queue fee. Through the legislative amendment, it shall become clearer that a municipal housing mediation has the right to charge a queue fee even if it reserves apartments for certain categories of applicants or distributes apartments according to a priority system.
The legislative changes also mean that current municipal guidelines for housing provision are replaced by an action plan. In the action plan, municipalities shall report on the need for new housing and take into account the need for coordination with other municipalities both in planning and in housing construction.
The Riksdag also directs a formal request (tillkännagivande) to the government to review how the use of reservations and priority in municipal housing mediation can be limited. The formal request came as a result of two proposals in follow-up motions.
The legislative changes begin to apply on 1 March 2025.

Parliament said yes to the government's proposal for reduced alcohol tax for beer from independent small breweries.

dok_titel: Swedish National Audit Office report on SIS special youth institutions
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion

2024/25:3265 by Martina Johansson et al. (C) demands 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has addressed a government statement concerning the Swedish National Audit Office's review of the State Institutions Agency's (SIS) special youth institutions and shortcomings in the state's compulsory care of children and young people.
The Swedish National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that SIS is not meeting the objectives of the activities at SIS institutions and that the children and young people placed at the institutions are not receiving effective care and treatment. Among other things, the Swedish National Audit Office states that SIS's mandate is unclear regarding which target groups SIS should receive, and that SIS should ensure that staff at youth institutions have the right expertise to provide care and treatment.
In its statement, the government agrees in part with what the Swedish National Audit Office has raised as shortcomings in the activities. Furthermore, the government points out that it has taken measures against, among other things, these shortcomings, and that measures are planned. With this, the government considers the report to be completed.
The Riksdag notes that the government has taken and plans measures and therefore decides to conclude the matter by filing the government's statement for the record.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motion

2024/25:3265 by Martina Johansson et al. (C) demands 1 and 2.

dok_titel: Swedish National Audit Office Report on Sis's Special Youth Facilities
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion

2024/25:3267 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) request 2.
notis:
Parliament has considered a communication from the government concerning the Swedish National Audit Office's review of the State Institutions Board's (Sis) special youth facilities and deficiencies in the state's compulsory care of children and young people.
The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that Sis does not meet the goals for operations at Sis facilities and that the children and young people placed at the facilities do not receive effective care and treatment. The National Audit Office notes, among other things, that Sis's mandate is unclear regarding which target groups Sis should receive, and that Sis should ensure that staff at the youth facilities have the right competence to provide care and treatment.
In its communication, the government partially agrees with what the National Audit Office has highlighted as deficiencies in the operations. Furthermore, the government points out that it has taken measures against, among other things, these deficiencies, and that measures are planned. With this, the government considers the report to be concluded.
Parliament notes that the government has taken and plans measures and therefore decides to conclude the matter by filing the government's communication with the records.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion

2024/25:3267 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) request 2.

dok_titel: Supplementary Provisions to the EU Regulation on the Use of Renewable and Low-Carbon Fuels for Maritime Transport
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for a law on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels for maritime transport.
Thereby, Parliament approves proposition 2024/25:76 and rejects motion

2024/25:3297 by Malin Östh et al. (V) request 1.
notis:
Parliament agreed to the government's proposal for a supplementary provision to the EU regulation on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels for maritime transport, which came into force on January 1, 2025. With this regulation, a limit was introduced for the amount of greenhouse gas that may be emitted on average per year from the fuels used by ships in commercial maritime transport.
The government's proposal contains, among other things, provisions on when and how Swedish authorities can decide on penalty charges for shipping companies that violate the EU regulation. The proposal also specifies what powers Swedish supervisory authorities shall have when monitoring compliance with the regulation.
The new law comes into force on March 1, 2025.
alternatives:

The Riksdag approved changes to, among other things, the Code of Judicial Procedure and the Police Crime Data Act which are to give crime-prevention authorities expanded opportunities to use biometrics. The purpose of the changes is for more crimes to be solved and for more perpetrators to be brought to justice.
The legislative changes entail, among other things, the following:

Biometric evidence shall be permitted to be collected, registered, and used in the investigation of crimes to a greater extent.
The police's current register of DNA profiles, fingerprints, and descriptions shall be replaced by new biometric registers.
In preliminary investigations into certain serious crimes, biometric comparisons of facial images and fingerprints of suspected perpetrators shall be permitted to be made against the Migration Agency's register of fingerprints and photographs.
DNA-based genealogical research shall, under certain conditions, be permitted in cases of murder and serious rape offences.

The legislative changes come into force on July 1, 2025.

notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for a new law which means that municipalities, regions, schools, and a number of state agencies, notwithstanding confidentiality provisions, shall provide certain information to the Police Authority and other crime-prevention authorities. This obligation means that information shall be provided upon request but also that information shall be provided on the authority's own initiative.
The Riksdag also approved the government's proposal which means that social services and health and medical care shall be given greater opportunities to provide information that is of significance for crime prevention.
The proposed rules give the crime-prevention authorities improved opportunities to access information held by other actors about, for example, crimes committed, suspected criminal schemes, and individuals with links to criminality. This gives them better conditions to prevent and combat crime as well as to prevent children and young people from becoming involved in criminality.
The new law and legislative changes come into force on April 1, 2025.

dok_titel: Secret data interception against serious crimes
forslag_text:
The Parliament adopts the Government's proposal for
1. law on amendment to the law (2000:562) on international legal assistance in criminal matters,
2. law on both continued validity of the law (2020:62) on secret data interception, and amendment to the same law,
3. law on amendment to the law (2020:62) on secret data interception,
4. law on amendment to the law (2024:326) on secret coercive measures for the purpose of implementing custodial penalties,
5. law on amendment to the law (2024:332) on amendment to the law (2024:326) on secret coercive measures for the purpose of implementing custodial penalties.
Thereby the Parliament approves proposition 2024/25:51 points 1-5 and rejects motion 

2024/25:3271 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) claims 4 and 5.
notis:
The Parliament said yes to the Government's proposal that secret data interception against serious crimes shall remain permitted. The proposal means that certain rules are clarified and in certain cases the possibility to use secret data interception is expanded.
The proposal means among other things:

The law shall apply without time limitation.
Secret data interception shall be permitted in more cases for the purpose of investigating who can reasonably be suspected of a crime.
The rules for which types of information may be collected shall be clarified.
The rules for the formulation of an authorization for secret data interception shall be clarified.
Surplus information that has emerged through secret data interception shall be permitted to be used for other purposes.
Legal security for the individual shall be strengthened. Among other things through improved opportunities for insight and supervision.

Current legislation ends on 31 March 2025. The law amendments are proposed to come into force on 1 April 2025.
The Parliament also said no to several motions, of which one proposal in a motion that was submitted during the general motion period 2024.

rubrik: Use of biometric registers for real-time camera surveillance with facial recognition
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2024/25:3246 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S).
notis:
The Riksdag approved changes to, among other things, the Code of Judicial Procedure and the police's crime data act which are to give law enforcement authorities expanded opportunities to use biometrics. The purpose of the changes is for more crimes to be solved and for more perpetrators to be brought to justice.
The legislative changes involve, among other things, the following:

Biometric material shall be permitted to be collected, registered and used in the investigation of crimes to a greater extent.
The police's current registers of DNA profiles, fingerprints and descriptions shall be replaced with new biometric registers.
During preliminary investigation of certain serious criminal activity, biometric comparisons of facial images and fingerprints of suspected perpetrators shall be permitted to be made against the Migration Agency's registers of fingerprints and photographs.
DNA-based genealogical investigation shall, under certain conditions, be permitted in cases of murder and serious rape offenses.

The legislative changes take effect on 1 July 2025.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2024/25:3246 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S).

rubrik: Calculation of the statute of limitations for young offenders
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2024/25:3287 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) claim 2.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for new criminal statutory limitations legislation. Among other things, the statutes of limitations for serious crimes shall be extended and all crimes that can result in life imprisonment shall be excluded from limitations.
The new rules also mean that the statute of limitations for gross violation of personal integrity and honor-based oppression of a child shall be calculated from the day the injured party reaches or would have reached 18 years of age, and that imposed prison sentences shall not be subject to limitations.
The legislative changes take effect from 1 April 2025. Most of the legislative changes also apply to crimes that have been committed but at that time had not been subject to limitations.

dok_titel: Increased information flow to crime prevention
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motion

2024/25:3284 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) motion 3.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for a new law which entails that municipalities, regions, schools and a number of government agencies, without hindrance of secrecy, shall provide certain information to the Police Authority and other law enforcement agencies. This obligation entails that information shall be provided on request but also that information shall be provided on own initiative.
Parliament also approved the government's proposal which entails that social services and health and medical care shall have greater opportunities to provide information that is of importance for crime prevention.
The proposed rules give the law enforcement agencies improved opportunities to access information that exists with other actors about, for example, committed crimes, suspected criminal arrangements and individuals with links to criminality. This gives them better conditions to prevent and combat crime and to prevent children and young people from becoming involved in criminality.
The new law and legislative amendments come into force on 1 April 2025.

rubrik: Increased supervision to prevent money laundering
dok_titel: National Audit Office report on government supervision to prevent money laundering
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2024/25:3280 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S) demands 1-4.
notis:
The Riksdag has dealt with a letter from the government which is based on the National Audit Office's audit report on government supervision to prevent money laundering.
The National Audit Office has examined the supervision that authorities conduct and concluded that the supervision needs to become better. The government's work to prevent money laundering is, according to the report, not sufficiently effective.
In the letter to the Riksdag, the government accounts for what measures have been taken to prevent money laundering. The government has submitted several bills and investigation directives to strengthen the work against money laundering.
On the Riksdag's table lies, for example, a bill that concerns measures against misuse of alternative payment systems. The bill contains proposals for measures to address the risks that alternative payment systems are used for money laundering and financing of terrorism.
Based on the measures that the government has carried out, the Riksdag sees no reason to propose any additional measures. The Riksdag rejects the motions and files the letter in the records, which means that the case is concluded.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2024/25:3280 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S) demands 1-4.

forslag_text:

2024/25:1004 by Rickard Nordin (C),

2024/25:3338 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) point 1 and

2024/25:3340 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) point 1.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal, which among other things means expanded opportunities for camera surveillance. The proposal includes, among other things, removing the requirement for a permit for camera surveillance for all actors in public activities.

dok_titel: Prescription of removal decisions, abolition of track-switching and certain questions about re-entry bans
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2024/25:3332 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) point 1.
notis:
The government proposes legislative amendments, among other things, to encourage more people to leave Sweden following a removal decision, that is, deportation or expulsion to the home country. The Riksdag approved the proposal.
The legislative amendments entail, among other things, the following:

A removal decision shall cease to apply (be prescribed) five years from when the foreign national has complied with the decision and left Sweden. According to current rules, the corresponding period is four years. If the decision is associated with a so-called re-entry ban that is in effect at that time, the decision shall cease to apply only when the re-entry ban expires.
Re-entry bans shall be determined for a maximum of five years, instead of one year as is currently the case. A re-entry ban means a prohibition from returning to Sweden. The re-entry ban may be longer, among other things, if the person poses a serious security threat.
The system of so-called track-switching is abolished. Track-switching means that a person who has received a rejection of their asylum application has the opportunity to instead seek a residence and work permit without leaving Sweden.

The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 April 2025.
The Riksdag also decided to reject proposals in motions within the field, of which two were submitted during the general motion period 2024.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2024/25:3332 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) point 1.

forslag_text:

b) the result target proposed by the government for research and innovation in the energy sector.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2024/25:3109 by Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al. (S) clause 66,

2024/25:3289 by Emma Nohrén et al. (MP) clauses 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a statement from the government based on the National Audit Office's audit report on the management of protected nature.
Fifteen percent of Sweden's area consists of protected nature, which includes the country's nature reserves and national parks. The Riksdag has decided that the protected areas shall be managed at a high ambition level. The National Audit Office points to several shortcomings in the management and makes recommendations to the government, the Environmental Protection Agency (Naturvårdsverket), and the county administrative boards in its report.
The Riksdag agrees with the National Audit Office's assessments that the state's efforts are lacking and welcomes the measures that the government has proposed to improve the management. The management of protected nature shall, according to the Riksdag, be efficient and appropriate while contributing to the fulfillment of Sweden's national goals and international commitments. The Riksdag laid the statement on file, which means the matter was concluded.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2024/25:2634 by Rebecka Le Moine and others (MP) request 1 and

2024/25:3285 by Anna-Caren Sätherberg and others (S) request 1.
notis:
Parliament has considered a letter from the government based on the Swedish National Audit Office's audit report on the management of protected nature.
Sweden's land area consists of 15 percent protected nature, which includes the country's nature reserves and national parks. Parliament has decided that the protected areas should be managed with high ambition levels. The National Audit Office points to several deficiencies in management and provides recommendations to the government, the Environmental Protection Agency and the county administrative boards in its report.
Parliament agrees with the National Audit Office's assessments that the state's efforts are deficient and welcomes the measures the government has proposed to improve management. According to parliament, the management of protected nature should be efficient and purposeful while contributing to fulfilling Sweden's national goals and international commitments. Parliament laid the letter to the records, which means the case was closed.

rubrik: Improved community care for children and young people
dok_titel: The National Audit Office's report on the state's efforts for children suspected of serious crimes
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2024/25:3283 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) demand 1.
notis:
The Riksdag has addressed a letter from the government concerning the state's efforts for children suspected of serious crimes. The letter is based on the National Audit Office's report in which the agency has examined how effective the state's efforts are to prevent children from committing serious crimes. The National Audit Office states that the state's efforts to stop children's serious criminality are not fully effective.
In the letter, the government describes the measures it has taken and plans to take in response to the National Audit Office's report. These include criminal law and social law measures, more resources to authorities, municipalities and regions, and measures concerning parents and guardians.
The Riksdag views positively the measures the government has taken and intends to take based on the National Audit Office's findings and recommendations. Extensive work is underway in the area within the Government Offices. Several inquiries have been appointed and are currently being prepared.
The Riksdag filed the letter with the records, which means the matter was closed.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2024/25:3283 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) demand 1.

dok_titel: Better Conditions for Animal Health Care and Animal Welfare
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2024/25:195 by Andreas Lennkvist Manriquez et al. (V) demand 21, 

2024/25:1397 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) demand 23 and 

2024/25:3108 by Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al. (S) demand 47.
notis:
Veterinary care should get better conditions to conduct its business. The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal, which involves changes for activities offering health and medical care for animals. The purpose is to ensure long-term well-functioning health and medical care for animals.
Supervision of animal health care will be expanded; today supervision only applies to the person performing animal treatment. The proposal means that supervision now also applies to the person conducting an activity where animal health personnel work.
Today, animal care workers do not form part of the animal health personnel. Given that demand for veterinary care has greatly increased, animal care workers will be able to be approved and thus join the animal health personnel.
Another regulatory change concerns making it easier for foreign veterinarians to work in Sweden.
The new regulations will come into effect on 1 September 2025, except for the changes concerning qualifications for animal care workers, which will instead come into effect on 1 September 2030.
The Riksdag also decided to direct a formal request to the government to protect and develop Swedish grazing rights.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2024/25:195 by Andreas Lennkvist Manriquez et al. (V) demand 21,

Supervision of animal health and veterinary services shall be expanded; currently supervision only applies to the person performing an animal treatment. The proposal means that supervision now also applies to those who conduct a business where animal health personnel work.

notis:
Animal veterinary services shall be given better conditions to conduct their operations. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal which means changes for businesses that offer health and veterinary services for animals. The aim is to ensure in the long term a well-functioning health and veterinary service for animals.
Supervision of animal health and veterinary services shall be expanded; currently supervision only applies to the person performing an animal treatment. The proposal means that supervision now also applies to those who conduct a business where animal health personnel work.
Today animal care assistants are not part of animal health personnel. Given that demand for animal veterinary services has increased greatly, animal care assistants will be able to become approved and thus be included in animal health personnel.
Another change in the regulations concerns making it easier for foreign veterinarians to work in Sweden.
The new regulations begin to apply on 1 September 2025 with the exception of changes relating to the qualifications for animal care assistants which instead begin to apply on 1 September 2030.
The Riksdag also decided to direct a formal request (tillkännagivande), an appeal, to the government to protect and develop Swedish pasture rights.

dok_titel: Better conditions for the tourism industry regarding small-scale production of alcoholic beverages
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2024/25:3319 by Leonid Yurkovskiy et al. (SD) demand 1 and 

2024/25:3330 by Christofer Bergenblock et al. (C) demands 2-4.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal which means that, for a limited period, a possibility shall be introduced to sell alcoholic beverages on a smaller scale at farm sales. The aim is to improve conditions for the local tourism industry. 
Certain restrictions are introduced to ensure that sales occur on a limited scale and that it is the visit rather than the sale that is in focus. Therefore, among other things, the following requirements are introduced:

The alcoholic beverages shall be self-produced by small-scale independent producers.
Farm sales may only take place to visitors who have participated in an educational event organized by the producer and paid for.
Sales to each individual visitor may not exceed 0.7 liters of spirits, 3 liters of wine, 3 liters of strong beer and 3 liters of other fermented alcoholic beverages at the same visit.

The legislative changes enter into force on 1 June 2025 and for six years onwards. Before the regulation is repealed, the reform should be evaluated.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2024/25:3319 by Leonid Yurkovskiy et al. (SD) demand 1 and 

2024/25:3330 by Christofer Bergenblock et al. (C) demands 2-4.

dok_titel: Better conditions for the tourism industry regarding small-scale production of alcoholic beverages
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposals for 
1. Act on amendment to the Alcohol Act (2010:1622),
2. Act on amendment to the Alcohol Act (2010:1622).
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2024/25:86 points 1 and 2 and rejects the motions 

2024/25:3322 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V), 

2024/25:3327 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S), 

2024/25:3330 by Christofer Bergenblock et al. (C) demand 1 and 

2024/25:3331 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal which entails that, for a limited time, a possibility shall be introduced to sell alcoholic beverages on a smaller scale through farm sales. The purpose is to improve conditions for the local tourism industry.
Certain restrictions are introduced to ensure that sales occur on a limited scale and that the visit rather than the sales is the focus. Therefore, among other things, the following requirements are introduced:

The alcoholic beverages shall be self-produced by small-scale independent producers.
Farm sales may only take place to visitors who have participated in an educational event arranged by the producer and paid for.
Sales to each individual visitor may not exceed 0.7 liters of spirits, 3 liters of wine, 3 liters of strong beer and 3 liters of other fermented alcoholic beverages at the same visit.

The law amendments come into effect on 1 June 2025 and for six years onwards. Before the regulation is repealed, the reform should be evaluated.
alternatives:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposals for 
1. Act on amendment to the Alcohol Act (2010:1622),
2. Act on amendment to the Alcohol Act (2010:1622).
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2024/25:86 points 1 and 2 and rejects the motions

notis:
Rules on international sanctions are to be tightened through a new law. Parliament approved the Government's proposal, which aims to implement the EU's sanctions directive into Swedish law.
International sanctions mean that one or more countries restrict the freedom of action for, for example, a person, an organization or another country's government. The purpose is to peacefully attempt to influence the subject of the restrictions through economic and political measures. This can be done, among other things, by introducing restrictions on exports and imports, imposing entry bans or freezing assets.
The purpose of the EU's sanctions directive – and of the new law – is to criminalize and establish penalties if the sanctions are not complied with.
The law entails that

penalties for violations of international sanctions are tightened
even violations of lesser severity (minor cases) are to be criminalized
new criminal offense designations in the form of sanctions violation, sanctions offense, gross sanctions offense and repeated sanctions offense are to be introduced
attempts and complicity in certain sanctions offenses are to be criminalized
certain government agencies are obligated to report if there is suspicion of a crime under the new law.

Parliament decided that the law enters into force on 10 June 2025 instead of 20 May 2025 as the Government proposed.

rubrik: Supplementary budget for 2025 – Temporarily increased subsidy rate for the rotavdrag
dok_titel: Supplementary budget for 2025 – Temporarily increased subsidy rate for the rotavdrag
forslag_text:
The Riksdag
a) adopts the Government's proposals for
1. Act amending the Income Tax Act (1999:1229),
2. Act amending the Income Tax Act (1999:1229),
3. Act amending the Act (2009:194) on the procedure for tax reduction for household work,
4. Act amending the Act (2009:194) on the procedure for tax reduction for household work,
5. Act amending the Tax Procedure Act (2011:1244),
6. Act amending the Tax Procedure Act (2011:1244),
b) approves amended calculation of revenues in the state budget for 2025 according to the Government's proposals.
Hereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2024/25:156 points 1-7 and rejects the motions

2024/25:3401 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V),

2024/25:3410 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) and

2024/25:3411 by Martin Ådahl and Anders Ådahl (both C).
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal to increase the subsidy rate for the rotavdrag (home improvement tax deduction) from 30 percent to 50 percent. The increase applies from May 12, 2025 to December 31, 2025.
Rotavdrag is the deduction a private person can receive when hiring a company for repair, maintenance, renovation or extension. The proposal aims to support the construction sector by, among other things, mitigating the effects of the economic situation.
The state budget for 2025 is affected by the proposal through reduced tax revenues of approximately 4.35 billion kronor (Swedish crowns). The rotavdrag is subsidized by the state, which means the state bears part of the cost of home improvement work. The deduction is financed through tax reduction and results in reduced tax revenues for the state.
The Government may submit ordinary supplementary budgets twice a year. However, it may also submit extraordinary supplementary budgets if it considers there are particular grounds for doing so. The Government believes that the construction sector's situation in the current economic climate constitutes such grounds, which the Riksdag agrees with.

2024/25:3107 by Morgan Johansson et al. (S) request 6 and

2024/25:3136 by Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S) request 36.
notis:
The rules on international sanctions will be strengthened through a new law. Parliament said yes to the Government's proposal, which aims to incorporate the EU's sanctions directive into Swedish law.
International sanctions mean that one or more countries restrict the freedom of action of, for example, a person, an organization or another country's government. The purpose is to peacefully, through economic and political measures, try to influence the one who the restrictions are imposed against. This can be done by, among other things, introducing restrictions on exports and imports, introducing entry bans or freezing assets.
The purpose of the EU's sanctions directive – and of the new law – is to criminalize and establish penalties if sanctions are not followed.
The law means that

penalties for violations of international sanctions are increased
even violations of lesser degree (minor cases) shall be criminalized
new crime designations in the form of sanctions violation, sanctions crime, gross sanctions crime and repeated sanctions crime shall be introduced
attempts and aiding and abetting certain sanctions crimes shall be criminalized
certain authorities shall be obliged to report if there is suspicion of a crime under the new law.

Parliament decided that the law comes into force on June 10, 2025 instead of May 20, 2025 as the Government proposed.

dok_titel: The National Audit Office's report on Industriklivet (Industrial Climate Initiative)
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2024/25:3317 by Kajsa Fredholm et al. (V) motions 3 and 4 as well as

2024/25:3320 by Katarina Luhr et al. (MP) motion 3.
notis:
Parliament has considered a communication from the government concerning the National Audit Office's audit of Industriklivet (Industrial Climate Initiative). In the audit, the National Audit Office examined whether the government and the Swedish Energy Agency have managed Industriklivet in such a way that it can effectively contribute to industry's climate transition and thereby Sweden's climate objectives.
The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that both the government's design of and the Swedish Energy Agency's work with Industriklivet has several shortcomings. The report contains a number of recommendations to the government and the Swedish Energy Agency, including on coordinating government support for climate transition.
The government agrees with certain conclusions, for example that Industriklivet can contribute more effectively to industry's transition. However, the government does not share the National Audit Office's assessment in certain other respects, for example that the target group for Industriklivet is unclear.
Parliament supports the government's assessment in several respects and decided to file the communication away, that is, to close the case.

dok_titel: A new rule on interest differential compensation – reduced barriers to early repayment of housing loans
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2024/25:3343 by Jennie Nilsson et al. (S) and

2024/25:3344 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) amendment 5.
notis:
The Riksdag approved a new model for calculating interest differential compensation for early repayment of fixed-rate mortgages. An interest differential compensation is the sum that a borrower needs to pay to their bank when a loan with a fixed interest rate is to be prepaid.
The purpose of the new model is to strengthen consumer protection by reducing the risk of unjustified differences between different borrowers who prepay their fixed-rate mortgage. Furthermore, the idea behind the new rules is that it should become easier for borrowers to plan their finances and to put their housing loans out to competitive tender.
The new rules enter into force on 1 July 2025.

2024/25:3157 by Helena Vilhelmsson et al. (C) requests 4, 15 and 21 and

2024/25:3307 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) requests 1 and 3.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered the government bill with an in-depth follow-up of work to prevent and combat male violence against women.
The bill is part of the government's action programme to prevent and combat male violence against women, domestic violence, and honour-related violence and oppression, as well as prostitution and human trafficking. According to the action programme, the government shall every other year submit a bill to the Riksdag with a report on work to achieve the gender equality policy objective that male violence against women shall cease. The present bill describes developments during the period of the national strategy to prevent and combat male violence against women 2017–2026, with a focus on 2022–2023.
The Riksdag notes, among other things, that extensive work is underway to prevent and stop male violence against women and domestic violence, and expresses confidence that the government will continue to pursue an active policy and carefully monitor developments in this area.
The Riksdag referred the government bill to the archives, that is to say concluded the matter.
The Riksdag also rejected the subsidiary motion that was raised in connection with the bill and approximately 30 proposals in motions from the ordinary motion period 2024, primarily on the grounds that work is already underway in the matters that the proposals address.
The proposals deal, among other things, with work against male violence against women and domestic violence, work against honour-related violence and oppression, and measures concerning support and protection for those subjected to violence.

dok_titel: A new rule on interest rate difference compensation – reduced obstacles to early repayment of housing loans
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2024/25:2950 by Alireza Akhondi et al. (C) motion 34 and

2024/25:3344 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) motions 1-4.
notis:
Parliament said yes to a new model for calculating interest rate difference compensation for early repayment of fixed-rate mortgages. Interest rate difference compensation is the sum that a borrower needs to pay to their bank when a fixed-rate loan is to be repaid early.
The purpose of the new model is to strengthen consumer protection by reducing the risk of unjustified differences between different borrowers who repay their fixed-rate mortgages early. Furthermore, the idea with the new rules is to make it easier for borrowers to plan their finances and to expose their mortgages to competition.
The new rules come into force on 1 July 2025.

Parliament rejects the motions

forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposed
1. act amending the Income Tax Act (1999:1229),
2. act amending the Tax Procedures Act (2011:1244),
3. act amending the Act (2020:1066) on procedures for tax reduction for installation of green technology.
Thereby parliament approves proposition 2024/25:109 points 1-3 and rejects the motions

2024/25:3357 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V),

2024/25:3374 by Anders Ådahl et al. (C), and

2024/25:3382 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP).
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal to reduce the subsidy rate for solar panel installation from 20 to 15 percent within the framework of green technology. The proposal also means that the tax reduction for microproduction of renewable electricity is abolished. Special tax rules have applied to those who produce renewable electricity by, for example, installing solar panels on their property and supplying electricity to the power grid.
The number of solar panel installations has increased significantly in recent years. Parliament shares the government's assessment that there is no longer a need to stimulate demand for solar panels to the same extent, and that the tax reduction for microproduction of renewable electricity should be removed.
The reduced subsidy rate for solar panel installation comes into effect on 1 July 2025. The proposal to abolish the tax reduction for microproduction of renewable electricity comes into effect on 1 January 2026.

notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal which entails several reductions in shoreline protection regulations.
According to the proposal, small bodies of water and bodies of water constructed in modern times shall no longer be covered by the general shoreline protection. The proposal also means that opportunities to build or take measures in shoreline-adjacent locations increase.
Shoreline protection shall, in individual cases, be able to be introduced for small bodies of water with special significance for the purposes of shoreline protection, which are to in the long term protect the public's access to shoreline areas and preserve good living conditions for animal and plant life on land and in water.
The exception for enterprises that use natural resources on land and in water, primary industries, becomes according to the Government's proposal more generous. The provisions for primary industries shall also be supplemented so that aquaculture, that is, activity that conducts cultivation in water, for example fish and shellfish farming, is also covered by the reductions.
Furthermore, municipalities shall more easily be able to decide that shoreline protection does not reapply when they adopt a new detailed plan, that is, the regulations that control construction within a certain area.
The proposals enter into force on 1 July 2025.
The Riksdag simultaneously rejected approximately 40 proposals in motions, among other things with reference to the Government's proposal and ongoing work. The proposals were submitted during the general motion period of 2024.

dok_titel: Reductions in shoreline protection – a first step
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for
1. a law on amendment to the Environmental Code,
2. a law on amendment to the law (1998:811) on implementation of the Environmental Code,
3. a law on amendment to the Planning and Building Act (2010:900) with the amendment that the preamble to the Government's proposal shall have the following wording: Hereby it is prescribed concerning the Planning and Building Act (2010:900) that partly sections 5, 10 and 16 of chapter 3, section 17 of chapter 4, section 3 of chapter 9 and section 10 of chapter 11 shall have the following wording, partly that a new section, section 17 a of chapter 4, shall be introduced with the following wording.
Thereby the Riksdag approves Government Bill 2024/25:102 points 1-3 and rejects the motions

2024/25:3348 by Andrea Andersson Tay et al. (V) demand 1 and

2024/25:3351 by Emma Nohrén et al. (MP) demand 1.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal which entails several reductions in shoreline protection regulations.
According to the proposal, small bodies of water and bodies of water constructed in modern times shall no longer be covered by the general shoreline protection. The proposal also means that opportunities to build or take measures in shoreline-adjacent locations increase.
Shoreline protection shall, in individual cases, be able to be introduced for small bodies of water with special significance for the purposes of shoreline protection, which are to in the long term protect the public's access to shoreline areas and preserve good living conditions for animal and plant life on land and in water.
The exception for enterprises that use natural resources on land and in water, primary industries, becomes according to the Government's proposal more generous. The provisions for primary industries shall also be supplemented so that aquaculture, that is, activity that conducts cultivation in water, for example fish and shellfish farming, is also covered by the reductions.
Furthermore, municipalities shall more easily be able to decide that shoreline protection does not reapply when they adopt a new detailed plan, that is, the regulations that control construction within a certain area.
The proposals enter into force on 1 July 2025.
The Riksdag simultaneously rejected approximately 40 proposals in motions, among other things with reference to the Government's proposal and ongoing work. The proposals were submitted during the general motion period of 2024.
alternatives:

dok_titel: Stricter Approach to Sexual Harassment, Fraud against the Elderly and Crimes with Gender as Hate Crime Motive
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2024/25:3390 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V),

2024/25:3391 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) demand 2,

2024/25:3393 by Henrik Vinge et al. (SD) demand 2 and

2024/25:3396 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) demand 1.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for amendments to the penal code. For example, criminal liability for rape of children is extended and purchase of sexual acts performed remotely is criminalized. Furthermore, gender is added to the provision on sentencing enhancement for crimes with hate crime motive.
A person who engages in sexual intercourse or another sexual act with a child under 18 years of age with reduced ability to protect their sexual integrity due to, for example, mental illness, disability or the perpetrator's authority, can be sentenced for rape of a child and sexual abuse of a child.
The criminal label of purchase of sexual service is changed to purchase of sexual act and the scope of criminal conduct for that crime and for pimping is expanded to include acts performed remotely, that is, without physical contact, for example via webcam.
The changes also mean that more cases of fraud against the elderly and other particularly vulnerable persons are to be assessed as serious crimes and result in harsher sentences.
The law changes enter into force on 1 July 2025.

The new rules are expected to work more crime-preventively than before and make it possible to issue more restraining orders. 
They include, among other things, the following:

Monitoring someone inappropriately is introduced as a new ground for issuing a restraining order.
A presumption rule is introduced that means the conditions for issuing a restraining order shall always be considered met following a judgment for serious crimes in close relationships.
Extended and specially extended restraining orders shall be given more easily and apply in larger areas.
Restraining orders may be issued when a person is expected to subject someone to pressure regarding an upcoming legal proceeding, for example testimony.

The legislative amendments come into effect on 1 July 2025.
The Riksdag simultaneously said no to proposals in motions, four of which are from the general motion period 2024.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the criminal code.
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2024/25:124 and rejects the motions 

2024/25:1903 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) clause 15, 

2024/25:2618 by Rasmus Ling et al. (MP) clause 40,

2024/25:3111 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) clause 71, 

2024/25:3157 by Helena Vilhelmsson et al. (C) clause 1, 

2024/25:3164 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) clause 45.1 and 

2024/25:3391 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) clause 1.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal for amendments to the criminal code. For example, criminal liability for rape of children is expanded and purchase of sexual acts performed remotely is criminalized. In addition, gender is added to the provision on sentence enhancement for crimes motivated by hate.
Anyone who engages in sexual intercourse or other sexual act with a child under 18 years of age with reduced ability to protect their sexual integrity due to, for example, mental illness, functional impairment or the perpetrator's authority may be convicted of rape of a child and sexual abuse of a child.
The crime designation "purchase of sexual service" is changed to "purchase of sexual act" and the criminal scope for that crime and for pimping is expanded to also include acts performed remotely, that is, without physical contact, for example via webcam.
The amendments also mean that more cases of fraud against elderly persons and other particularly vulnerable persons shall be treated as serious crimes and result in harsher punishment. 
The legislative amendments come into effect on 1 July 2025.
