dok_titel: Easements in building requirements for student housing
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for a law amending the Planning and Building Act (2010:900).
Thereby the Riksdag grants proposition 2024/25:132 and rejects motions

2024/25:3361 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (V) and

2024/25:3386 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) claim 1.
notis:
It shall become possible to make exceptions to the requirements for accessibility and usability in a building containing student housing. The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal for amendments to the Planning and Building Act.
Exceptions to the requirements apply to a maximum of 80 percent of either the total number of student apartments in a building or the number of student apartments that are added to a building when a measure is taken. The exception is intended to create conditions for increasing the construction of student housing with lower rent.
At least 20 percent of the student apartments shall still meet the current requirements for accessibility and usability. A student apartment covered by the exception may, however, be visited by a person with impaired mobility or orientation ability.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 July 2025.

forslag_text:

notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on state support for investments in new nuclear power. The new law regulates the fundamental conditions and forms of state support for companies investing in new nuclear reactors in Sweden.
The support shall be structured so that risks and profits are distributed in a well-balanced manner between the state and the company receiving support. The proposal means that state support may be provided in the form of

state loans
two-way difference contracts, a model for electricity price hedging that consists of an agreement between the operator of the reactor facility and the state that covers both minimum compensation protection and a limit on overcompensation.

State loans may be granted for construction and testing of new nuclear reactors as well as for design and other preparatory measures before construction. Two-way difference contracts may be entered into for routine operation of new nuclear reactors.
The law comes into force on 1 August 2025.

forslag_text:

2024/25:3312 by Anders Ådahl et al. (C) request 10 and

2024/25:3313 by Daniel Helldén et al. (MP) request 2.
notis:
The Government has presented its research policy for the years 2025–2028. In connection with this, the Government also presented a proposal which means that the Government shall be able to determine rules so that universities may decide that an employment with them may be combined with employment outside the university. Parliament approved the Government's proposal. Today, combined employment at universities applies only to certain positions, such as specially trained doctors and dentists, and the Government's proposal means that the restriction to certain sectors or positions can be removed.
The purpose of the legislative change is to increase the opportunity for exchange of knowledge and competence between individual researchers, higher education institutions and other sectors of society, and thereby strengthen competence supply and competitiveness. The legislative change enters into force on 1 July 2025.
Parliament also directed a directive, a so-called tillkännagivande (formal request), to the Government regarding the Government's announced investigation into how appropriate today's authority form is for state-run higher education institutions. According to Parliament, such an investigation into changed organizational form should not be carried out. The formal request came as a result of a proposal in a supplementary motion.
Parliament said no to other motions, of which approximately 140 proposals come from the general motion period 2024.

notis:
Parliament approved the Government's proposal on a new reduction obligation. The reduction obligation shall reduce carbon dioxide emissions, for example by fuel suppliers mixing biofuel into ordinary fuel.
Today, fuel suppliers shall mix in at least 6% biofuel, which the Government proposes to raise to 10%. The increase applies from 1 July 2025–31 December 2026. For the period 2027 to 2030, 10% shall apply.
The Government's proposal also means a new opportunity for fuel suppliers to partially fulfill the reduction obligation by delivering fossil-free electricity, through for example public charging stations.
Parliament also approved the Government's proposal on new rules for sustainable fuels and new rules for datacenters. The proposals mainly concern adapting Swedish law to EU law.
They include, among other things:

More fuels shall be covered by the sustainability criteria. In particular, recovered coal fuels and renewable fuels of non-biological origin shall be covered by the criteria.
Certain datacenters – or server halls, that is an installation used to store and manage large amounts of data and information – shall report, among other things, energy consumption to a European database.

dok_titel: Activities in the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) in 2024
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2024/25:3360 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V) demand 6.
notis:
Since March 7, 2024, Sweden participates fully in NATO's decision-making and thereby contributes to influencing the alliance's direction. The Riksdag has considered a memorandum in which the government reports on NATO activities in 2024. Furthermore, the Riksdag has considered a report from the Swedish delegation to NATO's parliamentary assembly on their activities in 2024.
The Riksdag emphasizes how important it is for the Riksdag to have insight into and influence over the government's actions on NATO matters. The Riksdag and the government believe that Sweden should be a credible, reliable, and solidary ally that contributes to strengthening security and stability in our neighborhood and in the Euro-Atlantic area. It is positive that the government in 2024 prioritized strengthening NATO's collective deterrence and defense capability, including by integrating Sweden into NATO's plans and structures and through concrete contributions to NATO activities. The Riksdag again emphasizes that support for Ukraine should continue to be a central part of Swedish security and defense policy and that Sweden should support Ukraine's struggle as long as it is needed.
All of NATO's 32 member states are part of the parliamentary assembly. The purpose of the assembly is to discuss and influence decisions on common security, create understanding for the security policy challenges that transatlantic cooperation faces, and support national parliaments' insight into defense and security matters. The Riksdag emphasizes the importance of the Swedish delegation for the Riksdag to gain insight into NATO's activities.
The Riksdag filed the memorandum and report, i.e., closed the case.

rubrik: Sweden's foreign and security policy as a NATO member
dok_titel: Activities of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) in 2024
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2024/25:3384 by Jacob Risberg et al. (MP) claim 1.
notis:
Since 7 March 2024, Sweden fully participates in NATO's decision-making and thereby contributes to influencing the alliance's direction. Parliament has addressed a statement in which the government reports on activities within NATO during 2024. Furthermore, Parliament has addressed a report from the Swedish delegation to NATO's parliamentary assembly on their activities during 2024.
Parliament emphasizes how important it is that Parliament gains insight and influence over the government's actions on NATO matters. Parliament and the government believe that Sweden should be a credible, reliable, and solidarity-minded ally that contributes to strengthening security and stability in our surrounding area and in the Euro-Atlantic area. It is positive that the government during 2024 prioritized strengthening NATO's collective deterrence and defense capability, including by integrating Sweden into NATO's plans and structures and through concrete contributions to NATO's activities. Parliament points out again that support for Ukraine should continue to be a central part of Swedish security and defense policy and that Sweden should support Ukraine's struggle as long as needed.
All of NATO's 32 member states participate in the parliamentary assembly. The purpose of the assembly is to discuss and influence decisions about common security, create understanding for the security policy challenges that transatlantic cooperation faces, and support national parliaments' insight into defense and security matters. Parliament emphasizes the importance of the Swedish delegation for Parliament to gain insight into NATO's activities.
Parliament laid the statement and report aside for further consideration, that is, closed the matter.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion 

2024/25:3384 by Jacob Risberg et al. (MP) claim 1.

dok_titel: Improved implementation of the EIA Directive
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts chapter 6, section 26 a of the government's proposal for a law amending the Environmental Code.
Thereby, the Riksdag accepts proposition 2024/25:153 point 1 in this respect and rejects motion

2024/25:3407 by Emma Nohrén et al. (MP).
notis:
The Swedish implementation of the so-called EIA Directive will become clearer. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.
The EIA Directive contains EU regulations on environmental impact assessments for certain public and private projects. The Directive has previously been implemented in Swedish law, but the EU Commission has provided comments on how Swedish legislation is designed. As a result, the government has proposed, among other things, the following changes:

Decisions on significant environmental impact shall be made publicly accessible.
The Government shall have the authority to determine rules on when a reportable activity may earliest begin.
It shall be clearer that environmental organizations are allowed to appeal certain decisions.

The legislative changes, which are implemented in the Environmental Code and in several other sectoral laws, take effect on August 1, 2025.

forslag_text:

notis:
The Riksdag has considered the government's letter regarding the National Audit Office's report on the state's efforts to reduce shipping emissions of harmful substances into the sea.
The National Audit Office finds that the environment in Swedish waters is heavily burdened and does not achieve good environmental status. If extensive measures are not taken, it is expected to have negative consequences for both the environment and society. The National Audit Office's recommendations to the government include, among other things, introducing a ban as soon as possible on discharges of so-called scrubber water, that is, wash water from ships' exhaust gas cleaning systems, in Sweden's entire territorial waters.
In its letter, the government essentially agrees with the National Audit Office's recommendations and has implemented or plans measures to address issues covered by the recommendations.

rubrik: Secret and preventive coercive measures when children under 15 years of age commit crimes
dok_titel: Secret and preventive coercive measures when children under 15 years of age commit crimes
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2024/25:3444 by Gudrun Nordborg et al. (V) points 2 and 3 and

2024/25:3447 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) point 2.
notis:
The law enforcement authorities shall be able to use secret and preventive coercive measures against children under 15 years of age. The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal. The proposals shall provide the authorities with better tools to combat serious crime committed by children and reduce the risk of children becoming involved in criminal activity. The proposals deal, among other things, with the following:

Secret coercive measures shall be able to be used to investigate certain serious crimes where the reasonably suspected person is under 15 years of age.
Preventive coercive measures shall in certain cases be able to be used against children under 15 years of age to prevent, avert and detect particularly serious crime.
Children shall be able to be held in more cases and for somewhat longer than currently for interrogation or for the purpose of being handed over to, for example, parents or social services.

The legislative changes come into force on 1 October 2025. Several of the legislative changes shall be time-limited to 30 September 2028 or 30 September 2030.

rubrik: Constitutional bill and changes to the Riksdag's main provisions
dok_titel: Strengthened protection for democracy and judicial independence
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts as pending the government's proposal for
1. Act on amendment to the Instrument of Government,
2. Act on amendment to the Rules of the Riksdag.
The Riksdag thereby approves proposition 2024/25:165 points 1 and 2 and rejects the motions

2024/25:1934 by Jessica Wetterling et al. (V) point 3 and

2024/25:3429 by Michael Rubbestad et al. (SD) point 1.
notis: The Riksdag said yes to adopting as pending the government's proposals for changes to the Instrument of Government and the Rules of the Riksdag, with the aim of strengthening the institutional protection of Sweden as a democratic state governed by the rule of law. The proposals essentially mean that it will become more difficult to amend the constitutional laws and that the protection of the independence of the courts and judges will be strengthened in the long term. Among other things, there will be requirements that at least half of the Riksdag's members say yes to a decision to adopt a constitutional bill as pending and that at least two-thirds of the Riksdag's members say yes to the second decision to adopt the proposal – after a Riksdag election has been held. Because the proposal concerns an amendment to constitutional law, the Riksdag must vote twice on the proposal in the same way and there must be a Riksdag election in between. The first decision means that the constitutional bill is adopted as pending. Through the second decision, the constitutional bill is adopted finally. Amendments to so-called main provisions in the Rules of the Riksdag are decided in the same way. The legislative changes are proposed to come into force on 1 April 2027.

The Riksdag rejects motion

notis: The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal for changes to the Electoral Act. The changes aim to protect general elections and strengthen the possibilities of exercising the right to vote. The changes mean that the Election Authority is given responsibility to support and coordinate work on the protection of elections. County administrative boards, municipalities and foreign authorities that have established polling stations shall promptly report incidents that may affect the conduct of elections. Furthermore, the requirements are clarified that voting shall be accessible to all voters and more voters shall have the opportunity to vote by mobile polling officers. The changes to the Electoral Act also include requirements that a polling officer shall always be present when voters use an assistant and that Swedes abroad who have fallen out of the voter roll shall be able to vote early in Sweden and through their vote be re-entered in the voter roll. The legislative changes come into force on 1 December 2025 in order to be applied in the general elections 2026.

dok_titel: Alignment of Swedish law with the revised VIS Regulation
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the Government's proposal for a law amending the Aliens Act (2005:716) in the parts concerning Chapter 9, Sections 8 d, 8 h and 8 j.
Thereby Parliament approves Government Bill 2024/25:176 point 1 in this respect and rejects motion

2024/25:3433 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) request 1.
notis:
Control of third-country nationals applying for national visa or residence permit in Sweden shall be strengthened. Parliament approved the proposal.
The purpose of the proposal is to align Swedish law with the EU's revised rules on the Central Information System for Visas, VIS. VIS is a system for exchange of information on visas between EU member states. According to the revised rules, information on national visas, that is to say visas for longer stays, and residence permits shall now also be included in the system. In addition, law enforcement authorities shall have improved access to it.
The proposal means among other things that

it becomes clearer in which situations a third-country national, that is to say a person who is not a citizen of an EU/EES country, is obliged to be photographed and provide fingerprints for a check in the system
it introduces an obligation to be photographed and provide fingerprints when applying for national visa.

The legislative changes shall enter into force on a date determined by the Government.

notis:
Parliament has considered a Government communication based on the National Audit Office's report on sectoral responsibility in disability policy. The National Audit Office notes that the sectoral responsible authorities partially work effectively to contribute to the implementation of disability policy. In its audit, the National Audit Office argues that the Government's direction of disability policy needs to become clearer.
The Government generally shares the National Audit Office's findings. The Government also considers the report an important contribution to the promotion of disability policy and the Government's work for Sweden to fulfill its commitments under the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
Parliament notes among other things that the National Audit Office recommends that the Government review whether authorities for more sectors should be assigned sectoral responsibility within disability policy. The Government shares this assessment, but argues that such consideration must be preceded by an analysis. Parliament agrees with the Government's assessment.
Parliament laid the communication aside, that is to say concluded the matter.

forslag_text:

2025/26:123 by Helena Vilhelmsson et al. (C) and

2025/26:2834 by Helena Vilhelmsson et al. (C) request 41.
notis:
Parliament approved the Government's proposal which means that virginity testing, certification of sexual virginity and virginity procedures are criminalized, both within and outside health and medical care. The changes aim to strengthen protection for girls and women living in an honour context.
The punishment for virginity testing or virginity procedure is imprisonment for at most one year. The punishment for certification of sexual virginity is a fine or imprisonment for at most six months.
Parliament also approved the Government's proposal that failure to disclose or prevent the crime of forced marriage and child marriage is criminalized, that is to say that it becomes punishable to not disclose or prevent ongoing crime.
The legislative changes shall enter into force on 1 December 2025.

forslag_text:

2024/25:3441 by Jennie Nilsson et al. (S) demands 1 and 2 as well as 

2024/25:3442 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) demands 6 and 7.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal for a simpler, more effective and more appropriate regulatory framework for building permits.
The purpose of the proposal is to create more housing and increase property owners' opportunities to determine how their own property should be developed.
The Government proposes among other things the following:

In areas not covered by a detailed plan it shall be possible to carry out more and larger measures without a building permit. However, a building permit shall still be required for construction near border, within areas of national interest for total defence and within particularly valuable areas.
Larger extensions shall be able to be built without a requirement for a building permit.
The requirement for a building permit for façade changes for single and two-family houses is abolished.
A building permit can be granted for attic conversion in residential buildings despite the fact that the detailed plan contains a prohibition on attic conversion.
The requirement for so-called plan-compliant starting point is abolished fifteen years after the detailed plan's implementation period has ended.

The legislative changes come into force on 1 December 2025.

Negligence in air traffic that is not gross may constitute grounds for liability, and the law clarifies when a crime is to be assessed as gross.

dok_titel: Sharper tools for the Inspectorate for Health and Social Care
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2025/26:1964 by Christofer Bergenblock et al. (C) proposition 3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to give the Inspectorate for Health and Social Care (IVO) more tools to intervene against unscrupulous and criminal actors in health and social care. This concerns private companies and other legal entities that operate group homes, home care services or work in personal assistance.
The government's proposal means among other things that

licenses for activities that have not been used for six months may be revoked
activities conducted unlawfully may be prohibited
persons who conduct activities despite a prohibition may be fined
it is clarified that the legal entity applying for a license must undergo a suitability assessment
municipalities may report such activities that require a license to IVO if there are suspicions of serious deficiencies.

The purpose of the government's proposal is to strengthen supervision and secure the right to good health and social care.
The legislative changes shall enter into force on 1 January 2026.

dok_titel: Adjustments to interest deduction rules to comply with EU law
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2025/26:3818 by Anders Ådahl et al. (C).
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to adapt the interest deduction rules to EU law.
The proposal means that interest expenses to a company in the same interest group that is domiciled in the European Economic Area (EEA) may not be deducted if the debt relationship is part of an artificial arrangement whose purpose is for the interest group to obtain a substantial tax advantage.
Companies are deemed to be in an interest group with each other if one of the companies owns shares in the other company or if it otherwise has a substantial influence in the other company, whether directly or indirectly.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 January 2026.

dok_titel: Stricter requirements in municipal adult education in Swedish for immigrants (sfi)
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motions

2025/26:319 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S) amendment 3,

2025/26:357 by Camilla Hansén et al. (MP) amendment 2, and

2025/26:3810 by Anders Ygeman et al. (S) amendment 75.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to strengthen requirements in municipal adult education in Swedish for immigrants (sfi).
The proposals entail essentially the following:

The right to participate in sfi shall apply for three years from the time the person was first admitted to the education, with certain possibilities for extension.
The municipality shall establish an action plan for its efforts to reach the persons in the municipality who have the right to sfi.
A person who has the right to sfi shall have the right to participate in the education in another municipality than their home municipality, if the person based on their personal circumstances has special grounds.
When a person is admitted to sfi, their knowledge shall be assessed, unless such an assessment is obviously unnecessary. The result of the assessment shall form the basis for the individual study plan.
The individual study plan for a student in sfi shall contain information about the time the student was first admitted to the education.

The purpose of the government's proposal is, among other things, to make sfi education more efficient and coherent so that more individuals acquire sufficient knowledge of Swedish for further studies or to establish themselves in the labor market.
The legislative changes come into force on January 1, 2026.

dok_titel: An improved model for presumption rent
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for
1. an act amending the Land Code,
2. an act amending the Act (1973:188) on Lease Committees and Rent Committees,
3. an act amending the Rent Negotiation Act (1978:304),
4. an act amending the Act (2022:1657) on dispute resolution within the framework of certain collective rent negotiations.
The Riksdag hereby approves proposition 2024/25:192 points 1-4 and rejects motions

2025/26:175 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (V) amendment 1 and

2025/26:210 by Amanda Palmstierna et al. (MP).
notis:
The rules for rent-setting for newly built apartments, so-called presumption rents, are to become more flexible. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for legislative changes concerning presumption rents.
Presumption rent is often applied in new construction and means that the rent is determined for the first 15 years. During this time, the rent is usually not increased as much as for apartments with use-value rents. This means that the move-in rent for new construction today is usually higher than on the rental market otherwise.
With the new rules, there are to be greater opportunities to adjust presumption rents continuously during the rental period. According to the proposal, this is to create both better conditions for building rental housing and enable lower move-in rents for tenants. Another part of the proposal is that tenants are to have greater opportunities to influence the design of the apartment themselves – and thus the rent – through requests for add-ons or opt-outs. To enable necessary modernizations of a property, the rent may also be changed taking into account a substantial interest.
Disputes concerning initial presumption rents and continuous adjustments of such rents are, according to the government's proposal, to be able to be resolved with the help of a so-called arbitrator appointed by the Rent Committee.
The legislative changes come into force on January 1, 2026.

forslag_text:

2025/26:3550 by Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S).
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal on regulatory changes in the electricity market. The changes are being made to adapt Swedish law to changed EU regulations.
Among other things, the following is proposed:

Electricity suppliers with more than 200,000 electricity users shall be able to offer contracts with fixed duration and price.
Electricity users shall receive a summary of the most important contract terms before a contract is concluded or extended.
Electricity suppliers shall have strategies to reduce the risk of not being able to deliver electricity.
Network companies shall choose so-called designated electricity suppliers in a fair, open and non-discriminatory manner.

These and other regulatory changes begin to apply on January 1, 2026.

Policy shall be directed at supporting hard-working people's economy so that the prolonged recession can be broken and recovery can resume. A benefit reform shall make it more profitable to work. Defense shall be strengthened as well as support to Ukraine. Fossil fuels shall be phased out and Sweden shall reach net-zero emissions by 2045.
Financial policy is expansive in 2026 to counteract the recession from having prolonged negative consequences on the Swedish economy. With stable public finances and low government debt, Sweden stands strong and therefore has the opportunity to implement measures that strengthen Sweden and Swedish households' economy and break the recession.

extended temporarily increased reduction of tax on agricultural diesel
eliminated vehicle tax and caravan tax for certain trailers
modernized taxation of gases.

All law changes begin to apply on January 1, 2026 except those concerning modernized taxation of gases, which begin to apply on July 1, 2026 and eliminated vehicle tax and caravan tax for certain trailers which begin to apply on February 1, 2026.
Parliament also approved the government's direction for economic policy and budget policy.
Policy shall be directed at supporting hard-working people's economy so that the prolonged recession can be broken and recovery can resume. A benefit reform shall make it more profitable to work. Companies' conditions shall be improved. Resources for schools shall increase, crime shall continue to be combated and waiting times for healthcare shall be shortened. Defense shall be strengthened as well as support to Ukraine. Fossil fuels shall be phased out and Sweden shall reach net-zero emissions by 2045.
Financial policy is expansive in 2026 to counteract the recession from having prolonged negative consequences on the Swedish economy. With stable public finances and low government debt, Sweden stands strong and therefore has the opportunity to implement measures that strengthen Sweden and Swedish households' economy and break the recession.
Parliament's decision on expenditure frameworks for the state budget is guiding when Parliament in the next step decides on appropriations for the 27 expenditure areas in the budget.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2025/26:211 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) demands 1-3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to tighten requirements for public counsels. A public counsel is engaged to provide legal support and represent individuals in, for example, expulsion and deportation cases or cases concerning forced removal into care. The competence requirements for interpreters in migration cases shall also be tightened.
The purpose of the legal changes is, among other things, to strengthen legal certainty in cases concerning individuals' integrity and freedom.
The legal changes involve the following:

The qualification requirements for public counsels are tightened. Currently, for example, there is no absolute requirement for a law degree, which shall be required according to the bill.
Special permission shall be required for a public counsel to delegate their assignment to another qualified person.
A person deemed unsuitable may be declared unqualified to act as an agent or counsel at the Migration Agency, the Police Authority and the Security Police.
Competence requirements for interpreters and translators in migration cases are introduced. This means, among other things, that the authority, if possible, shall engage an interpreter or translator who is authorized.

The legal changes enter into force on 1 January 2026.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2025/26:3831 by Lotta Johnsson Fornarve et al. (V) demand 2.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to tighten the rules for conditional release.
The proposals include, among other things:

the portion of the sentence that must be served before conditional release can occur is raised from two-thirds to three-quarters, and this increase is implemented gradually starting with the longest prison sentences
the threshold for postponing conditional release if the sentenced person misbehaves during incarceration is lowered
it shall be possible to postpone conditional release if there is a risk that the sentenced person reoffends in serious crime
the general prison minimum, the shortest prison sentence, shall be raised to one month, and all prison sentences shall be covered by the conditional release system
the probation period after conditional release shall be at least two years, instead of today's one year, and the conditionally released person shall, as a main rule, be placed under supervision
the entire conditionally granted freedom shall be forfeited upon reoffence during probation, and no new conditional release shall be granted from the forfeited portion.

One purpose of the government's proposal is to shift focus from offender to victim and public protection.
The legal changes enter into force on 1 January 2026, except for certain legal changes regarding the increase in the portion of the sentence that must be served before conditional release can occur. Those legal changes enter into force on a day determined by the government.

The Riksdag rejects motion

2025/26:3831 by Lotta Johnsson Fornarve et al. (V) demand 2.

The government's proposal includes the following, among other things:

The Riksdag's ability to convene is strengthened.
The Riksdag's war delegation is retained for war and war threat, and the rules regarding the delegation are adjusted. Among other things, the Speaker gets a role corresponding to that in the Riksdag. Furthermore, a member who becomes a minister shall no longer be able to serve in the delegation.

notis:
To achieve a high level of cybersecurity in society, the government proposes a new cybersecurity law aimed at implementing the so-called NIS 2 directive. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.
The proposal means that public and private operators within certain designated sectors shall, among other things, take measures to protect their networks and information systems and report significant incidents. The NIS 2 directive was adopted by the EU in 2022 and aims to achieve a high level of cybersecurity throughout the union.

dok_titel: Strong protection for networks and information systems – a new cybersecurity law
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2025/26:3834 by Ulf Holm et al. (MP).
notis:
To achieve a high cybersecurity level in society, the government proposes a new cybersecurity law aimed at implementing the so-called NIS 2 directive. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.
The proposal means that public and private operators in certain designated sectors are to take measures to protect their networks and information systems and report significant incidents. The proposal also means that a supervisory authority is to intervene if an operator breaches provisions in the law.
The NIS 2 directive was decided by the EU in 2022 and aims to achieve a high common cybersecurity level throughout the union.
The Riksdag also approved the government's proposal to amend other laws concerning electronic communications, top-level domains, and confidentiality.
The new rules enter into force on 15 January 2026.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2025/26:3834 by Ulf Holm et al. (MP).

dok_titel: The National Audit Office's report on the state's efforts against economic abuse in close relationships
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:1826 by Aylin Nouri (S), 

2025/26:3827 by Ardalan Shekarabi et al. (S), 

2025/26:3828 by Maj Karlsson et al. (V) proposals 1 and 2 and 

2025/26:3833 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) proposals 1 and 3.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a statement from the government based on the National Audit Office's report on the state's efforts against economic abuse in close relationships. Economic abuse means, for example, taking control over and controlling another person's finances.
The Riksdag welcomes the National Audit Office's examination and believes that it shows that the work against economic abuse must continue and be intensified and that economic abuse must be made more visible.
The report contains four recommendations to the government and two to relevant agencies. The Riksdag notes that the government has implemented some measures based on the recommendations. Among other things, the government has initiated a review of the rules on property division and consideration time in the Marriage Code. The Riksdag also notes that the government is working on developing a new long-term strategy on, among other things, men's violence against women and that the government, as part of that work, will continue the work to prevent and combat economic abuse.
The Riksdag filed the statement, that is, closed the matter. At the same time, the Riksdag said no to a number of motions on the subject, two of which were submitted during the general motion period in 2025.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions 

2025/26:1171 by Anne-Li Sjölund and Christofer Bergenblock (both C), 

2025/26:1375 by Sanne Lennström and Inga-Lill Sjöblom (both S), 

2025/26:2175 by Johanna Rantsi (M), 

2025/26:2185 by Johanna Rantsi (M) items 2 and 3,

2025/26:3581 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) item 16, 

2025/26:3702 by Elin Nilsson et al. (L) and 

2025/26:3865 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) items 1 and 2.
notis:
Parliament approved allowing municipalities greater opportunity to conduct register checks in hiring.
According to the decision, municipalities may conduct register checks on persons who will work in the homes of elderly persons or adults with disabilities. Register checks may also be conducted on persons who will be hired for senior positions in municipalities. Additionally, the opportunity for register checks of persons who will work with children is expanded.
This means that municipalities in more cases than today will be able to access information from the criminal record register – and in some cases also the suspicion register – before they hire someone.
The purpose of the new rules is to prevent persons with criminal or harmful intentions from taking employment in municipal activities.
The new laws and amendments to laws enter into force on 1 March 2026.

rubrik: The trial period for work testing
dok_titel: Work testing with retained sick pay
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts Chapter 27, Section 8 b of the Government's proposed amendment to the Social Insurance Code. 
Thereby Parliament approves proposition 2025/26:53 in this respect and rejects motion 

2025/26:3852 by Malte Tängmark Roos et al. (MP).
notis:
Parliament said yes to the Government's proposed amendments to the Social Insurance Code to lower the thresholds for return to work. 
The proposals mean that an insured person who has the right to full sick pay can, in agreement with their employer, have the opportunity to test their work ability with the employer while retaining sick pay for a limited time.
The legislative changes take effect on 1 March 2026.

dok_titel: A new ban on credit gambling
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2025/26:3820 by Mats Berglund et al. (MP).
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for an expanded ban on credit gambling.
The purpose of the proposal is to counteract debt among those who gamble. The ban means that gambling merchants and those licensed to provide online gambling (license holders) may neither permit nor participate in gambling being financed with credit. License holders and gambling merchants must also take appropriate measures to prevent gambling from being financed with credit.
The law comes into force on May 1, 2026.

rubrik: Construction of the Travel Guarantee Fund
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:3181 by Alireza Akhondi et al. (C) claim 21, 

2025/26:3849 by Joakim Järrebring et al. (S) and 

2025/26:3854 by Alireza Akhondi et al. (C) claim 2.
notis:
The Riksdag agreed to the government's proposal for an improved travel guarantee system. The purpose of the proposal is for travelers to receive stronger financial protection while costs and administration are reduced for travel companies.
The travel guarantee system is changed by establishing a collective fund into which travel organizers pay a fee. As the fund grows, the individual guarantees that travel companies have towards travelers shall be reduced in size.
Another legislative change means that more reimbursement claims shall be covered by the travel guarantee system. For example, travelers shall in certain cases be able to receive compensation even if they have been compensated in the form of a voucher, which previously would have become worthless if a travel organizer has gone bankrupt or cannot pay its debts.
The government also proposes that it shall be possible for legal entities, such as payment card companies, to apply for compensation from the travel guarantee. Payment card companies can according to the Consumer Credit Act or contract be obligated to pay out compensation to travelers. These companies shall thus in turn be given the right to apply for compensation from the travel guarantee (so-called right of recourse).
The legislative changes which mean that a collective fund is established begin to apply on 1 April 2026. Other changes shall begin to apply on the day the government determines.

2025/26:3181 by Alireza Akhondi et al. (C) claim 21,

The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for a law on special calculation of employer contributions and general payroll tax for persons who have reached 18 but not 23 years of age at the beginning of the year.
Thereby, the Riksdag approves proposition 2025/26:66 and rejects the motions 

2025/26:3867 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) and 

2025/26:3870 by Malte Tängmark Roos et al. (MP) motion 1.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for a temporary reduction in employer contributions for persons who have reached 18 but not 23 years of age at the beginning of the year.
The government's proposal means that only the old-age pension contribution and half of the other contributions and the general payroll tax are to be paid on compensation up to 25,000 kronor per calendar month.
The purpose of the proposal is to facilitate young people entering the labour market and at the same time create better conditions for companies to retain and hire young people.
The new law is to come into force on 1 April 2026 and apply to compensation paid during the period 1 April 2026–30 September 2027.

dok_titel: Next steps for good and accessible care
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:3815 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V) demands 1-3.
notis:
The Government proposes that primary care's mandate and responsibilities become clearer and that it is clarified that a medical assessment by a doctor and nurse when needed should be available at any time, 24 hours a day, in municipal healthcare. The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal.
Primary care refers to, for example, health centers and other healthcare activities that handle common healthcare needs that do not require special medical or technical resources or any other special expertise.
The legislative changes include the following:

It becomes clearer that regions and municipalities should collaborate in the planning and development of healthcare.
It also becomes clearer that primary care should meet both physical and mental healthcare needs.
A requirement is introduced that there must be a medically responsible person for rehabilitation in the municipality.
The term home healthcare (hemsjukvård) is replaced with healthcare in the home.
The requirement for information to patients is strengthened. A patient should receive information about who is their fixed care contact and fixed doctor contact. It should also be clear how the patient contacts them and their care units.

The legislative changes come into force on July 1, 2026.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:3815 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V) demands 1-3.

rubrik: The level of employer contributions and young people's establishment on the labour market
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:3862 by Martina Johansson and Anders W Jonsson (both C) and 

2025/26:3870 by Malte Tängmark Roos et al. (MP) request 2.
notis:
The Riksdag accepted the government's proposal on temporary reduction of employer contributions for persons who at the beginning of the year have reached 18 but not 23 years of age.
The government's proposal means that only the old-age pension contribution and half of the other contributions and the general salary levy shall be paid on compensation up to 25,000 kronor per calendar month.
The purpose of the proposal is to facilitate young people entering the labour market and at the same time create better conditions for enterprises to retain and employ young people.
The new law shall come into force on 1 April 2026 and shall apply to compensation paid during the period 1 April 2026–30 September 2027.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:2046 by Ann-Sofie Lifvenhage (M) and 

2025/26:3556 by Peter Hultqvist et al. (S) demand 89.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a statement from the government. It concerns the Riksdag Audit Office's report on state management of civil defence establishment.
The Riksdag Audit Office's overall assessment is that the government's management of civil defence establishment has not been sufficiently effective during the period reviewed, the years 2015–2024. The Riksdag has during the past two years deepened its focus specifically on the area of civil defence with regard to results monitoring. The observations that the Riksdag has made during this time are consistent with the Riksdag Audit Office's assessment.
However, the Riksdag agrees that management and monitoring have substantially improved and welcomes the government's intention to continue working to strengthen both management and monitoring within the area.
The Riksdag files the statement, which means that the matter is closed.
The Riksdag also said no to 14 proposals in motions from the general motion period in 2025. The proposals concern, among other things, civil defence, what tasks the Agency for Societal Protection and Preparedness (now the Agency for Civil Defence) should have, and state responsibility for rescue services.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:2046 by Ann-Sofie Lifvenhage (M) and

dok_titel: Development of the macroprudential oversight area
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:3911 by Mikael Damberg and others (S) claims 1 and 2.
notis: The Riksdag agreed with the government's proposals concerning changes to amortization requirements and mortgage ceiling. The proposals include, among other things, that the mortgage ceiling is raised from 85 to 90 percent of the residential property's market value when purchasing a new residence, while the possibility to increase one's mortgage with a so-called supplementary loan is limited to 80 percent of the residential property's market value. Supplementary loans can, for example, be used to renovate the residence. According to the proposals, the so-called heightened amortization requirement shall also be removed, that is the requirement for additional amortization of at least 1 percent if the borrower's total residential loans exceed 4.5 times gross annual income. The original amortization requirement governed by the loan-to-value ratio remains. The proposals also mean that a new law on the limitation of residential credit replaces the Financial Supervisory Authority's regulations and general advice on amortization requirements and mortgage ceiling. The purpose of the proposals is, among other things, to reduce thresholds on the housing market and for more people to be able to own their residence. The new law and legislative amendments enter into force on April 1, 2026.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:3911 by Mikael Damberg and others (S) claims 1 and 2.

dok_titel: National Audit Office report on government management of civil defence construction
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion

2025/26:2822 by Mikael Larsson et al. (C) motion 43.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a communication from the government. It concerns the National Audit Office's report on government management of civil defence construction.
The National Audit Office's overall assessment is that the government's management of civil defence construction was not sufficiently effective during the period reviewed, 2015–2024. Over the past two years, the Riksdag has studied the civil defence area in depth with regard to performance monitoring. The observations that the Riksdag has made during this time are consistent with the National Audit Office's assessment.
However, the Riksdag agrees that management and monitoring have improved significantly and welcomes the government's intention to continue working to strengthen both management and monitoring in the field.
The Riksdag places the communication on file, which means the matter is closed.
The Riksdag also rejected 14 proposals in motions from the general motion session of 2025. The proposals concern, among other things, civil defence, what tasks the Agency for Civil Defence and Readiness (formerly the Agency for Societal Security and Preparedness) should have, and state responsibility for rescue services.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motion

2025/26:2822 by Mikael Larsson et al. (C) motion 43.

dok_titel: Report on the Use of Secret Coercive Measures in 2024
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2025/26:3886 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) proposal 2.
notis:
Every year the government reports to parliament how the law enforcement authorities use secret wiretapping and other secret coercive measures. Parliament has addressed the report on the use during 2024. It concerns how the Public Prosecution Authority, the Economic Crimes Authority, the Police Authority, the Customs Agency and the Security Police have used secret wiretapping of electronic communications, secret monitoring of electronic communications, secret camera surveillance, secret room surveillance and secret data reading.
Parliament agrees with the government that the secret coercive measures serve an important function for investigating crimes and that the report shows that the secret coercive measures have been of real value. Parliament filed the report with the records, that is, concluded the matter.
Parliament also said no to proposals in motions regarding the design of the annual report and on strengthening the Security and Privacy Protection Committee.

dok_titel: The National Audit Office's report on the state's work on Agenda 2030
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:1809 by Aida Birinxhiku (S), 

2025/26:3876 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S), 

2025/26:3882 by Martin Ådahl et al. (C) and 

2025/26:3883 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) motions 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a letter from the government concerning the National Audit Office's report on the state's work on Agenda 2030. The National Audit Office has examined whether the state's work on Agenda 2030 has been effective. The agency has focused on the implementation by the government and central agencies between 2015–2025. 
The overall conclusion in the report is that the state's work on the agenda has not been effective. The National Audit Office points out that Sweden ranked very high in the world ranking of achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals when the work began in 2016, but that Sweden's achievement has not increased significantly since then. The National Audit Office assesses, among other things, that the monitoring of achievement of the goals in Sweden is incomplete, which makes it difficult to determine which areas would need to be prioritized. The National Audit Office also assesses that the government has not created conditions for more coherent sustainable development policy.  
In its letter, the government welcomes the National Audit Office's review and states that Agenda 2030 is implemented on the basis of national conditions. Following the National Audit Office's observation of unclear allocation of responsibility for coherent policy, the government intends to clarify responsibility allocation within the Government Offices. The Riksdag shares the government's assessment that several social problems have grown or not improved, which complicates implementation nationally and internationally.
The Riksdag filed the letter with the records, which means that the matter was closed.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:1809 by Aida Birinxhiku (S), 

2025/26:3876 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S), 

2025/26:3882 by Martin Ådahl et al. (C) and 

2025/26:3883 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) motions 1 and 2.

Parliament views positively that the Government has taken measures to increase quality and equality in preschool. Parliament laid the statement to the records, that is, concluded the matter.

rubrik: Certain questions regarding the future design of legislation
dok_titel: Secure custody – a new indeterminate deprivation of liberty sanction
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:3902 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) demands 2, 4 and 5.
notis:
Persons who have committed serious crimes against other persons and who also have a high risk of reoffending should be able to be sentenced to secure custody for an indeterminate period. The Riksdag voted yes to the government's proposal. 
Secure custody means that the court first determines a minimum period to be served in prison, which corresponds to the prison sentence that would otherwise have been imposed. In addition to this, a maximum period of an additional four to six years is to be determined. The maximum period may be extended by at most three years at a time if it is absolutely necessary to deter the convicted person from reoffending in serious crime.  
At the end of the minimum period, the court may decide on so-called conditional release. This means that the Swedish Prison and Probation Service may decide that the convicted person shall serve the sanction outside the institution with special support and under supervision. If the person misbehaves or commits new crimes, the release may be interrupted.
The purpose of the government's proposal is to strengthen society's protection against persons who have committed serious crimes against other persons and who also have a high risk of reoffending in such crime, but who are not eligible for forensic psychiatric care or life imprisonment.
The new rules enter into force on 15 April 2026.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:3902 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) demands 2, 4 and 5.

rubrik: A new salary requirement for work permits
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the Aliens Act (2005:716) in the parts concerning chapter 6, section 2, first paragraph 1.
Thereby the Riksdag approves bill 2025/26:87 in this part and rejects the motions 

2025/26:3880 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) in this part, 

2025/26:3881 by Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C) demand 1, 

2025/26:3885 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) demand 1 and 

2025/26:3890 by Lorena Delgado Varas and Daniel Riazat (both -) demand 1.
notis:
The Riksdag voted yes to the government's law proposal where the conditions for labour migration are tightened, while immigration of highly qualified labour is promoted.
Among other things, a requirement for comprehensive health insurance and a salary requirement are introduced as conditions for labour migration. Certain occupational groups should be able to be exempted from the salary requirement while other occupational groups should be able to be excluded from the possibility of being granted work permits. Work permits may be refused if the employer has been convicted or is suspected of certain crimes or has been subjected to certain sanctions.
The legislative amendments also introduce two new crimes: exploitation of foreign labour and trafficking in work permits. At the same time, the special fee for those who have a foreigner employed who does not have the right to reside or work in Sweden is increased.
Furthermore, the permit period for so-called EU Blue Cards and for seasonal work is extended. In addition, the possibilities for certain highly qualified foreigners to apply for residence permits from within Sweden are expanded.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 June 2026 with certain transitional provisions.
alternatives:

dok_titel: Preventive detention — a new indefinite deprivation of liberty sanction
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposals for
1. law on the enforcement of preventive detention,
2. law on amendments to the Penal Code,
3. law on amendments to the Passport Act (1978:302),
4. law on amendments to the Act (1998:620) on criminal records,
5. law on amendments to the Act (1998:714) on compensation for deprivation of liberty and other coercive measures,
6. law on amendments to the Act (2000:562) on international legal assistance in criminal matters,
7. law on amendments to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (2009:400),
8. law on amendments to the Act (2015:96) on recognition and enforcement of deprivation of liberty sanctions within the European Union,
9. law on amendments to the Act (2018:1250) on credit for time in detention,
10. law on amendments to the Sentencing Act (2018:1251),
11. law on amendments to the Act (2018:1693) on police processing of personal data within the scope of the crime data law,
12. law on amendments to the Act (2018:1694) on the Customs Board's processing of personal data within the scope of the crime data law,
13. law on amendments to the Act (2025:520) on international enforcement in criminal matters,
14. law on amendments to the Act (2025:798) on amendments to the Passport Act (1978:302).

Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2025/26:95 points 1-14 and rejects the motions

2025/26:3027 by Noria Manouchi (M) amendment 8,

2025/26:3234 by Marléne Lund Kopparklint (M) amendment 1,

2025/26:3477 by Marléne Lund Kopparklint (M),

2025/26:3586 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) amendment 58,

2025/26:3591 by Ardalan Shekarabi et al. (S) amendment 20,

2025/26:3901 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) amendments 1 and 2 and

2025/26:3902 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) amendments 1 and 3.
notis:
People who have committed serious crimes against other people and who also have a high risk of reoffending can be sentenced to preventive detention for an indefinite period. The Riksdag voted in favour of the government's proposal.

Preventive detention means that the court first determines a minimum term to be served in prison and which corresponds to the prison sentence that would otherwise have been imposed. In addition to this, a range period shall be determined of an additional four to six years. The range period may be extended by no more than three years at a time if it is absolutely necessary to prevent the sentenced person from reoffending in serious crime.

At the end of the minimum term, the court may decide on so-called conditional release. This means that the Prison Service may decide that the sentenced person shall serve the sentence outside the prison facility with special support and under supervision. If the person misbehaves or commits new crimes, the conditional release can be revoked.

The purpose of the government's proposal is to strengthen society's protection against people who have committed serious crimes against other people and who also have a high risk of reoffending in such crimes, but who are not currently eligible for forensic psychiatric care or life imprisonment.

The new rules come into force on April 15, 2026.

notis:
Parliament approved the government's bill to tighten the conditions for labour immigration while promoting immigration of highly qualified workers.
Among other things, comprehensive health insurance and a wage requirement are introduced as conditions for labour immigration. Certain occupational groups may be exempted from the wage requirement while other occupational groups may be excluded from the possibility of being granted work permits. Work permits may be refused if the employer has been convicted or is suspected of certain crimes or has been subject to certain sanctions.
The legislative changes also mean that two new crimes, exploitation of foreign workers and trafficking in work permits, are introduced. At the same time, the special fee for those who have a foreigner employed who does not have the right to reside or work in Sweden is increased.
Furthermore, the permit period for so-called EU blue cards and for seasonal work is extended. The possibilities for certain highly qualified foreigners to apply for residence permits from within Sweden are also expanded.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 June 2026 with certain transitional provisions.

rubrik: The design of the wage requirement and exceptions from the requirement
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:781 by Helén Pettersson and Åsa Karlsson (both S),

2025/26:3874 by Ida Karkiainen et al. (S) amendment 2 and

2025/26:3885 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) amendment 8.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's bill where conditions for labour immigration are tightened, while immigration of highly qualified labour is promoted. Among other things, a requirement for comprehensive sick leave insurance and a wage requirement are introduced as conditions for labour immigration. Certain occupational groups may be exempted from the wage requirement while other occupational groups may be excluded from the possibility of being granted work permits. Work permits may be denied if the employer has been sentenced or is suspected of certain crimes or has been subject to certain sanctions.
The legislative changes also mean that two new crimes, exploitation of foreign labour and trafficking in work permits, are introduced. At the same time, the special fee for those who have a foreigner employed who does not have the right to stay or work in Sweden is increased.
Furthermore, the permit period for so-called EU Blue Cards and for seasonal work is extended. In addition, the possibilities for certain highly qualified foreigners to apply for residence permits from within Sweden are expanded.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 June 2026 with certain transitional provisions.

notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to tighten regulations for invasive alien species.
The bill means, among other things, that those who intentionally or with gross negligence introduce an invasive alien species into Sweden from another EU country may be sentenced to fines or imprisonment for at most two years.
The proposal also means that those who introduce invasive alien species from another EU country shall be obliged to report the species to the Customs Authority. The Customs Authority shall also receive authority to check the import of alien species at the internal land border and, if necessary, seize such species.
By invasive alien species is meant species of animals, plants, fungi or microorganisms that are introduced and spread in the environment and cause problems for, for example, native plants and animals, human health and society.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 May 2026.
The Riksdag also said no to approximately 200 proposals in motions from the general motion period 2025, primarily by referring to already taken measures. The proposals deal, among other things, with invasive alien species, area protection, species protection, remediation and beach protection.

rubrik: Review of the regulation on special measures for persons with functional disability that impairs work capacity
dok_titel: The National Audit Office's report on the Public Employment Agency's support to persons with functional disability, etc.
forslag_text:
The Riksdag supports what the committee states regarding a review of Regulation (2017:462) on special measures for persons with functional disability that impairs work capacity and informs the government of this.
Thereby, the Riksdag partly approves the motions 

2025/26:3872 by Ardalan Shekarabi et al. (S), 

2025/26:3878 by Ciczie Weidby et al. (V) motion 2, and 

2025/26:3887 by Leila Ali Elmi et al. (MP) motion 2, and 

rejects the motions 

2025/26:3543 by Nils Seye Larsen et al. (MP) motion 15, and 

2025/26:3877 by Magnus Persson et al. (SD) motion 2.
notis:
The Riksdag submits a formal notification—an instruction—to the government to review the regulation on special measures for persons with functional disability that impairs work capacity. Examples of special measures are wage subsidies, contributions toward workplace aids, and interpreter services for persons with visual or hearing impairment. The reason for the review is to ensure that the conditions for the measures contribute to fulfilling the purpose of the labor market policy program.
The formal notification is based on proposals in motions in response to the government's letter regarding the National Audit Office's audit report on the Public Employment Agency's support to persons with functional disability. The National Audit Office concludes in the report that there are deficiencies in how effectively the Public Employment Agency works with the target group. Furthermore, the National Audit Office assesses that the government's direction has not been sufficiently effective.
The Labor Market Committee considers the National Audit Office's audit to be an important contribution to the work of providing appropriate measures to persons with functional disability that affects work capacity. The committee also notes that the government has already taken several measures to improve support and that additional measures may be needed.
The Riksdag rejected the other proposals in the motions and filed the letter with the records.

rubrik: Measures against the spread of invasive alien species
dok_titel: Tightening of regulations for invasive alien species and nature conservation
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:1856 by Johan Büser and Dzenan Cisija (both S) motion 3,

2025/26:2824 by Stina Larsson et al. (C) motion 14,

2025/26:3428 by Emma Nohrén et al. (MP) motion 55,

2025/26:3774 by Emma Nohrén et al. (MP) motion 37 and

2025/26:3845 by Stina Larsson et al. (C) motions 1-3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal to tighten the regulations for invasive alien species.
The bill means, among other things, that a person who intentionally or through gross negligence introduces an invasive alien species to Sweden from another EU country can be sentenced to fines or imprisonment for up to two years.
The proposal also means that a person who introduces invasive alien species from another EU country must be obliged to report the species to the Swedish Customs Agency. The Customs Agency must also be granted authority to check the importation of foreign species at the internal land border and, if necessary, seize such species.
Invasive alien species means species of animals, plants, fungi or microorganisms that are introduced and spread in the environment and cause problems for, for example, native plants and animals, human health and society.
The law changes enter into force on 1 May 2026.
The Riksdag also rejected approximately 200 proposals in motions from the ordinary motion period 2025, primarily citing measures already taken. The proposals concern, among other things, invasive alien species, area protection, species protection, remediation and shore protection.

dok_titel: National Audit Office report on the Public Employment Service's support for persons with disabilities, etc.
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:949 by Daniel Persson (SD),

2025/26:1951 by Mattias Vepsä and Alexandra Völker (both S) motion 2,

2025/26:3543 by Nils Seye Larsen et al. (MP) motion 14,

2025/26:3887 by Leila Ali Elmi et al. (MP) motions 1 and 3-5 as well as

files government communication 2025/26:72.
notis:
The Riksdag directs a formal statement (tillkännagivande) to the government to review the regulation on special measures for persons with disabilities resulting in reduced work capacity. Examples of special measures are wage subsidies, subsidies for workplace aids and interpreters for persons with visual or hearing impairments. The reason for the review is to ensure that the conditions for the measures contribute to achieving the purpose of the labor market policy program.
The formal statement is based on proposals in motions in response to the government's communication regarding the National Audit Office's audit report Employment Service Support for Persons with Disabilities. In the report, the National Audit Office concludes that there are shortcomings in how effectively the Employment Service works with the target group. Furthermore, the National Audit Office assesses that the government's steering has not been sufficiently effective.
The Labor Market Committee believes that the National Audit Office's audit is an important contribution to the work of providing appropriate measures to persons with disabilities affecting work capacity. The Committee also notes that the government has already taken several measures to improve the support and that further measures may be needed.
The Riksdag rejected the other proposals in the motions and filed the government communication.

dok_titel: National Audit Office's report on labour law conditions in public procurement
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions 

2025/26:3896 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S) claim 3 and 

2025/26:3898 by Andrea Andersson Tay et al. (V) claims 1 and 2.
notis:
Parliament laid the government's statement concerning the National Audit Office's report on labour law conditions in public procurement on the record, which means that the matter was concluded.
The National Audit Office's overall conclusion in the report is that the work of setting labour law requirements in public procurement does not function effectively. The consequence could be that the authorities contribute to wage dumping and otherwise poor working conditions among their suppliers. The National Audit Office submits several recommendations in its report to the government as well as to the Public Procurement Agency and the Competition Authority. Parliament agrees with the National Audit Office's assessment that there are opportunities to make the authorities' procurement more efficient.
In the statement, the government reports the measures that have been taken and that the government intends to implement following the National Audit Office's observations. Parliament notes the measures that the government is considering within the areas covered by the National Audit Office's recommendations and welcomes them.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the motions 

2025/26:3896 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S) claim 3 and 

2025/26:3898 by Andrea Andersson Tay et al. (V) claims 1 and 2.

dok_titel: Privacy protection in signal intelligence operations in defense intelligence activities
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:3556 by Peter Hultqvist et al. (S) item 94.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a government communication regarding privacy protection in signal intelligence operations in defense intelligence activities. Signal intelligence is closely regulated through laws and regulations, among other things to protect individuals' personal privacy. It is the State Inspection of Defense Intelligence Activities, Siun, that supervises that signal intelligence operations are conducted in accordance with the regulatory framework.
The government assesses that Siun's review of the signal intelligence operations conducted in 2024 has functioned well and that Siun has had access to the information needed to fulfill its assignment.
The Riksdag filed the communication with its records, which means the matter was concluded. Furthermore, the Riksdag rejected three proposals in motions concerning signal intelligence and intelligence operations. The Riksdag refers to the very significant appropriations that FRA, the Swedish Defence Radio Establishment, receives to strengthen signal intelligence operations. Furthermore, the Riksdag believes there is no reason to anticipate proposals on intelligence operations that the government intends to submit in 2026.

rubrik: Other matters concerning the state's promotion of national minority languages
dok_titel: The National Audit Office report on the state's promotion of national minority languages
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:3884 by Jan Riise et al. (MP) item 3 and 

2025/26:3892 by Lorena Delgado Varas and Daniel Riazat (both -) items 1 and 5-7.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a government communication regarding the National Audit Office's review of the state's efforts to protect national minority languages. The public authorities have by law a special responsibility to protect and promote the national minority languages—Yiddish, Romani Chib, Sámi, Finnish and Meänkieli.
The National Audit Office has reviewed whether the state's efforts to keep the national minority languages alive are effective. According to the National Audit Office, the state's efforts are not sufficient to reach the goal and resources could be used more effectively.
The government agrees in principle with the National Audit Office's findings. The government takes seriously that the state's efforts are insufficient and is committed to long-term work to keep minority languages alive.
The Riksdag emphasizes the importance of preserving, strengthening and increasing access to minority languages and agrees with the government's assessment that long-term work is required. Furthermore, the Riksdag considers the National Audit Office's report to be an important knowledge base for the continued work to keep minority languages alive.

2025/26:3435 by Jan Riise et al. (MP) amendment 3,

2025/26:3775 by Amanda Lind et al. (MP) amendment 46,

2025/26:3884 by Jan Riise et al. (MP) amendment 1 and

2025/26:3892 by Lorena Delgado Varas and Daniel Riazat (both -) amendment 4.
notis:
The Riksdag has discussed a communication from the Government concerning the National Audit Office's examination of the State's efforts to protect the national minority languages. According to law, the public sector has a special responsibility to protect and promote the national minority languages: Yiddish, Romani Chib, Sámi, Finnish, and Meänkieli.
The National Audit Office has examined whether the State's efforts to keep the national minority languages alive are effective. According to the National Audit Office, the State's efforts are insufficient to achieve the goal, and resources could be used more effectively.
The Government largely agrees with the National Audit Office's findings. The Government takes seriously the fact that the State's efforts are insufficient and is committed to long-term work to keep minority languages alive.
The Riksdag emphasizes the importance of preserving, strengthening, and increasing access to minority languages and shares the Government's assessment that long-term work is required. Furthermore, the Riksdag believes that the National Audit Office's report is important knowledge material for ongoing work to keep minority languages alive.
The Riksdag filed the Government's communication with the documents, which means the matter was closed.

The Riksdag rejects the motions

dok_titel: Identity requirements for registration and measures against circumvention of the housing cooperative law
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2025/26:3910 by Amanda Palmstierna et al. (MP).
notis: The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on stricter requirements for providing an identity designation in applications for registration. The Riksdag also supported the government's proposal intended to prevent the regulations from being circumvented when rental apartments are converted to housing cooperative apartments. The decision means that an application for registration concerning a natural person shall contain information about the acquirer's personal or coordination number. For legal entities, the application shall contain information about the acquirer's organizational number. The purpose of the decision is to create better control over who owns a property. Stricter identity requirements can contribute to the police and other authorities' ability to prevent and combat crime. If a housing cooperative wishes to acquire a rental building to convert rental apartments to housing cooperative apartments, this shall be decided at a general meeting. The conversion decision is only valid if the tenants in at least two-thirds of the apartments covered by the acquisition consent to the decision. The Riksdag decision means that a requirement is introduced that a residential tenant must have been registered at a property for at least six months immediately before the general meeting to be counted in the qualified majority required. The new rules enter into force on 1 July 2026.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2025/26:3910 by Amanda Palmstierna et al. (MP).

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2025/26:3897 by Joakim Järrebring et al. (S) proposal 3.
notis:
The government wants support for people who need a legal representative — that is, a guardian or administrator — to become more reliable. Parliament approved the government's proposal.
The proposal includes, among other things, clearer terms of reference for the guardian or administrator's assignment with increased consideration for the individual's wishes and increased focus on the individual's well-being. The government also proposes that a central state authority should be responsible for the legal representative sector and that a national register of legal representatives be introduced.
The purpose of the proposal is to strengthen the individual's position, raise the quality of activities, create better opportunities to recruit and retain competent guardians and administrators, and improve the work of the supervisory authorities.
Most of the legislative changes enter into force on 1 July 2026. The proposal on a register of legal representatives enters into force on 1 January 2028.
alternatives:

dok_titel: Suspension of Execution – A New Procedure for Certain Foreigners in Case of Temporary Obstacles to Execution
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion

2025/26:3925 by Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal on a new procedure in case of temporary obstacles to execution.
A foreigner residing in Sweden who for various reasons does not have the right to remain in the country may be issued a decision on refusal of entry or expulsion. There may, however, be obstacles to execution, which means that a decision on refusal of entry or expulsion cannot be carried out. The obstacle may be that the person risks being punished with death, subjected to torture, or other inhumane or degrading treatment.
Today, temporary residence permits are often granted in case of temporary obstacles to refusal of entry or expulsion. The decision means that the expulsion or refusal of entry is postponed instead of the person being granted a time-limited residence permit. The foreigner may also be required to report to the Migration Agency or the Police Authority and at the same time be prohibited from leaving a residential area.
The purpose of the new rules is to create conditions for more efficient work on returning people. Furthermore, the rules are to strengthen the state's ability to handle people who pose a threat to Sweden and who for a certain time cannot leave the country.
The new rules enter into force on 1 June 2026.
