dok_titel: Identity requirements at land registration and measures against circumvention of the cooperative housing law
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2025/26:3905 by Joakim Järrebring et al. (S).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal on stricter requirements to provide an identity number when applying for land registration. The Riksdag also supported the government's proposal aimed at preventing circumvention of the regulations when rental apartments are converted to cooperative housing.
The decision means that an application for land registration concerning a natural person shall contain information about the acquirer's personal or coordination number. Regarding legal entities, the application shall contain information about the acquirer's organizational number. The purpose of the decision is to create better control over who owns a property. Stricter identity requirements can contribute to the police and other authorities' ability to prevent and combat crime.
If a cooperative housing association wishes to acquire a rental building to convert rental apartments to cooperative housing, this shall be decided at a member meeting. The conversion decision is only valid if tenants in at least two-thirds of the apartments covered by the acquisition agree to the decision. The Riksdag decision means that a requirement is introduced that a residential tenant must have been registered at a property for at least six months immediately before the member meeting to be counted in the qualified majority required.
The new regulations will enter into force on 1 July 2026.

dok_titel: Supplementary budget for 2026 – Reduced tax on fuel and electricity and gas price support
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2025/26:4082 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S) request 1.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal for a supplementary budget in order to reduce the tax on fuel and introduce a temporary new electricity and gas price support.
The proposal means that the energy tax on petrol and diesel is temporarily reduced by 82 öre per litre respectively 319 kronor per cubic meter during the period 1 May–30 September 2026.
For petrol and diesel in environmental class 1, this means a reduction to the minimum level of the energy tax directive. The energy tax on alkylate petrol is reduced as much as possible without falling below the minimum tax level. The reduction in energy tax will entail changes in the law on energy tax.
The government also proposes that funds be allocated for a new temporary electricity and gas price support to households for January and February 2026.
The proposal means that the state's income decreases by approximately 1.56 billion kronor and that the state's expenditure is estimated to increase by approximately 2.4 billion kronor in 2026. This weakens the administration's financial savings and the state's budget balance by approximately 4.1 billion kronor in 2026.
The government may submit ordinary supplementary budgets twice a year. However, it may also submit extraordinary supplementary budgets if it considers that there are special reasons for it. The conflict in the Middle East, which is assessed to affect fuel prices, as well as the high electricity prices and the severe cold that has meant that households' costs for heating have been high at the beginning of 2026 are, according to the government, such reasons and the Riksdag makes no other assessment.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2025/26:4082 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S) request 1.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2025/26:3873 by Jessica Wetterling et al. (V).
notis:
The government proposes that a digital recording that has been seized or copied in a house search should not be considered a public document. Parliament agreed to adopt as pending the government's proposal for amendment to the Freedom of the Press Act.
The government's proposal means that a recording for automated processing that has been seized or copied in a house search, among other things in a criminal investigation, should not be considered a public document. The same applies to such a recording that has been received by a public authority as a result of the authority taking over responsibility for the seized information carrier or copy from the house search.
If a recording is added to an investigation of a crime or criminal activity or other activity at the authority, it shall, however, continue to be a public document.
Since the proposal concerns amendments to the Constitution, it is required that Parliament votes the same way twice on the proposal and that a general election is held between the votes. This is the first decision on the proposal. Parliament agreed to adopt the proposal as pending.
The legislative changes enter into force on 1 January 2027.

rubrik: Working with a residence permit for studies
dok_titel: Improved migration law rules for researchers and doctoral students and measures to prevent abuse of residence permits for studies
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2025/26:3945 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) claims 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on changed rules for foreign researchers, doctoral students and students. The changes include the following:

Doctoral students may be granted a residence permit for research.
Researchers and doctoral students may be granted permanent residence permits more quickly, and they may also be granted longer residence permits to seek employment after completed research or completed studies.
Researchers and doctoral students and their family members have expanded opportunities to apply for a residence permit from within Sweden.
Opportunities to work with a residence permit for studies are restricted.
Requirements to make satisfactory progress in studies are tightened.
Requirements to switch from a residence permit for studies to a residence permit for work are tightened.
New rules are introduced for when residence permits for family members of students can be revoked.

The Riksdag also approved a new law with special provisions on granting residence permits for so-called mass refugees from Ukraine.
The new rules enter into force on 11 June 2026.

forslag_text:

2025/26:3906 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S) claims 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on changes to several environmental laws that will reduce the amount of waste and increase recycling. The aim is for Sweden to achieve the targets that the EU has decided on in this area.
The changes include, among other things, that the rules for responsibility for waste become clearer. It should be clear what the responsibility covers and when it ends. At the same time, the rules for supervision of waste management are changed.
The changes should also contribute to a more circular economy and lead to more sustainable management of excavation waste. Additionally, the state, municipalities, regions and municipal associations will no longer need to provide financial security for the disposal of waste or for the management of waste arising from the extraction of minerals and other natural resources.
The new rules enter into force on 1 July 2026.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2025/26:3931 by Hanna Gunnarsson et al. (V),

2025/26:3938 by Mikael Larsson and Kerstin Lundgren (both C) demands 2 and 4, and

2025/26:3944 by Ulf Holm et al. (MP) demands 1 and 2.
notis:
The Government wishes to strengthen protection for the civilian population during heightened alert. Parliament approved the Government's proposal for a new law on shelters and protected spaces.
Today there are approximately 64,000 shelters with capacity for 7 million individuals in Sweden. However, this is not sufficient to provide the population with adequate protection. Now the Government wishes to ensure that Sweden has modern protection for the civilian population during heightened alert or armed attack.
The Government has therefore proposed a new law on shelters and protected spaces. The new law provides, among other things, regulations for a new protection option beyond shelters, the so-called protected spaces. A protected space is a space for protecting the population that provides limited protection compared to shelters.
The law amendments enter into force on 1 June 2026.

notis:
Parliament approved the Government's proposal to tighten the requirements for obtaining Swedish citizenship.
The proposal means, among other things, that

the requirement that one must have lived in Sweden for a certain period, that is to say, had one's residence here, is raised from five to eight years as a starting point
higher requirements are placed on the lifestyle of the person who wishes to obtain Swedish citizenship
a requirement for financial support is introduced when applying for citizenship
a requirement for sufficient knowledge of Swedish and about Swedish society is introduced to obtain Swedish citizenship
the notification procedure, that is to say, the possibility of becoming a Swedish citizen through notification, is to be limited as far as possible
children are to be able to acquire Swedish citizenship independently after the child's guardian has made an application.

The purpose of the proposal is to strengthen the status of citizenship and increase the individual's opportunity to actively participate in society.
The law amendments enter into force on 6 June 2026. The law amendments concerning the citizenship test in reading and listening comprehension in Swedish at functional level enter into force on 1 October 2027 or an earlier day as determined by the Government. The law amendments concerning the citizenship test in Swedish otherwise enter into force on the day determined by the Government.

rubrik: Government's work with documentation and evaluation within the climate policy framework

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motion

2025/26:3924 by Katarina Luhr et al. (MP) demands 1-3.
notis:
Parliament has considered a letter from the Government. It concerns the National Audit Office's examination of whether the Government and public agencies have conducted effective work with documentation and evaluations within the climate policy framework.
The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the handling has several shortcomings, particularly concerning the Environmental Protection Agency's work in preparing comprehensive documentation for the Government's climate reports and climate action plans. The National Audit Office also provided a number of recommendations to the Government, the Environmental Protection Agency, the Energy Agency, and the Climate Policy Council.
In its letter, the Government welcomes the National Audit Office's examination and largely agrees with the National Audit Office's problem description but makes partly a different assessment of what measures should be taken. In its letter, the Government emphasizes that it is conducting ongoing work to evaluate and develop the documentation within the climate policy framework in order to improve the quality and clarity of the climate report and climate action plan. The Government also notes that in recent years, measures have also been taken to improve the public agencies' work with documentation within the climate policy framework.
Parliament, like the Government, welcomes the National Audit Office's examination and views positively the Government's work to improve the quality and clarity of the climate reports and climate action plans and assumes that this work continues.
Parliament referred the letter to the records, that is to say, closed the matter.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects the motion

2025/26:3924 by Katarina Luhr et al. (MP) demands 1-3.

For anyone who has committed a crime and is between 15–17 years of age, if a deprivation of liberty penalty cannot be avoided, the penalty shall be determined as imprisonment instead of closed youth care. The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal on this.
According to current rules, a person aged 15–17 who commits such a serious crime that it leads to a deprivation of liberty penalty shall, as a general rule, be sentenced to closed youth care instead of imprisonment. Closed youth care is implemented by the Swedish Prison and Probation Service and the sentenced person is placed at a special youth facility (SiS facility).
The decision means that children and young people in these cases shall instead be sentenced to imprisonment. The Swedish Prison and Probation Service becomes responsible for implementing the penalty and closed youth care is removed from the penalty system. This further means, among other things, the following:

Children sentenced to imprisonment shall, as a general rule, be placed in special children's and youth units, which shall be specially adapted based on children's needs and rights.
By the penalty becoming imprisonment, children and young people are covered by the system of conditional release and when transitioning from detention to freedom they shall, as a starting point, be placed under supervision in order to provide them with the support and control they need (which differs from the penalty of closed youth care).
The imposed sentence becomes in itself longer, since four years of closed youth care corresponds to six years of imprisonment. However, the deprivation of liberty part is not always longer since part of the sentence can be served outside detention after conditional release. 

The legislative changes enter into force, in all material respects, on 1 July 2026.

The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal for a new act on public commercial activities. The new act shall improve competition in public and private activities. The Government emphasizes that the new act will better protect private companies from the unequal conditions that can arise when public and private actors operate on the same market.
The Riksdag shares the Government's view that it is important to address problems caused by so-called undue influence. The Riksdag also approved the Government's proposal which means that the Swedish Competition Authority gets greater opportunities to investigate and take measures to remove obstacles to effective competition.

For a person who has committed a crime and is 15–17 years old, if a custodial sentence cannot be avoided, the sentence shall be determined as imprisonment instead of closed youth custody (ungdomsvård). The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on this.
According to current law, a person aged 15–17 who commits such a serious crime that it leads to a custodial sentence shall, as a general rule, be sentenced to closed youth custody instead of imprisonment. Closed youth custody is enforced by the National Board for Institutional Care and the convicted person is placed at a special youth home (SiS home).
The decision means that children and young people in these cases shall instead be sentenced to imprisonment. The Prison and Probation Service thus becomes responsible for enforcing the sentence and closed youth custody is removed from the sentencing system. This means, among other things, the following:

Children sentenced to imprisonment shall, as a general rule, be placed in special children's and youth units, which shall be specially adapted based on children's needs and rights.

The legislative changes begin, in all material respects, to apply on 1 July 2026.

notis:
The Riksdag has considered a communication from the government concerning the National Audit Office's review of the State Property Board's property management. The purpose of the review was to examine whether the State Property Board's (SFV) management of market rent and subsidized properties leased as premises is efficient.
The National Audit Office's overarching conclusion is that the management is conducted efficiently in large part, but that there are certain shortcomings in both the SFV's management and the government's control. The National Audit Office provides, among other things, the following recommendations to the government:

Review the calculation model for the rate of return requirement and monitor the development of the SFV's growing government capital.
Ensure a long-term solution for the financing of subsidized properties in line with the ambitions that exist for these properties.
Clarify responsibility and principles for the process of additions to the state property portfolio.

In its communication, the government agrees with the National Audit Office's overarching observations and at the same time points to measures that have already been taken and measures that the government will continue to follow up. 
The Riksdag notes that the government has implemented a number of measures in response to the National Audit Office's observations and recommendations, and that the government also intends to continue monitoring developments regarding the SFV's property management.
The Riksdag thus files the communication, that is, concludes the matter.

forslag_text:

notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal to criminalize psychological violence. Through the bill, the harmful patterns of conduct that are carried out to control or break down a person and that today fall outside the criminal law can be captured.
The regulation means that it becomes punishable to repeatedly subject another person to insults in the form of accusations, derogatory statements, humiliating behavior, improper threats, improper coercion or improper surveillance, if the insults taken together have been capable of seriously damaging the person's self-esteem.
The regulation also means that it becomes punishable to subject someone to improper surveillance that is persistent, if the act has been capable of seriously damaging the person's self-esteem.
The punishment is imprisonment for a maximum of four years and the legal amendments come into force on 1 July 2026.

rubrik: Expanded opportunities for condominium owners to sublease their apartments
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the condominium act (1991:614) to the extent it concerns chapter 7, section 11.
Thus parliament approves proposition 2025/26:187 point 5 in this regard and rejects the motions

2025/26:3995 by Andreas Lennkvist Manriquez et al. (V) point 2,

2025/26:4011 by Joakim Järrebring et al. (S) point 1 and

2025/26:4065 by Amanda Palmstierna et al. (MP) point 1.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for a private rental act and amendments to, among other things, the land code and the condominium act. The amendments are intended to create a more flexible rental market and increase access to housing. A new private rental act is to be introduced with the aim of simplifying and clarifying the rules for private individuals who rent out their homes. The possibilities to rent out one's condominium to third parties are also expanded. The fact that the apartment was previously rented out is only to be taken into account in this context when the apartment is rented out again if the previous rental occurred to a significant extent.
New rules are also being introduced to meet companies' needs for housing for their staff and to facilitate the increasingly common living arrangement where tenants rent individual rooms and share common areas. The new rules mean that the conditions for accommodating these forms of housing through so-called block rental are improved. Block rental means that a landlord rents out several apartments in a "block" to a single tenant, instead of renting out each apartment directly to private individuals.
Furthermore, compensation for rental brokers is increased and rules are introduced regarding, among other things, leave to appeal in cases concerning the return of rent in order to streamline the process.
The new law and legal amendments come into force on 1 July 2026.

rubrik: A new model for block rental
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for a law amending the Land Code to the extent it concerns chapter 7, section 31 and chapter 12, sections 1 e, 45 a, 55, 55 b and 55 f.
Thus parliament approves proposition 2025/26:187 point 2 in this regard and rejects the motions

2025/26:3995 by Andreas Lennkvist Manriquez et al. (V) point 3,

2025/26:4011 by Joakim Järrebring et al. (S) point 2 and

2025/26:4065 by Amanda Palmstierna et al. (MP) points 2 and 3.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for a private rental act and amendments to, among other things, the land code and the condominium act. The amendments are intended to create a more flexible rental market and increase access to housing. A new private rental act is to be introduced with the aim of simplifying and clarifying the rules for private individuals who rent out their homes. The possibilities to rent out one's condominium to third parties are also expanded. The fact that the apartment was previously rented out is only to be taken into account in this context when the apartment is rented out again if the previous rental occurred to a significant extent.
New rules are also being introduced to meet companies' needs for housing for their staff and to facilitate the increasingly common living arrangement where tenants rent individual rooms and share common areas. The new rules mean that the conditions for accommodating these forms of housing through so-called block rental are improved. Block rental means that a landlord rents out several apartments in a "block" to a single tenant, instead of renting out each apartment directly to private individuals.
Furthermore, compensation for rental brokers is increased and rules are introduced regarding, among other things, leave to appeal in cases concerning the return of rent in order to streamline the process.
The new law and legal amendments come into force on 1 July 2026.

dok_titel: A specific criminal provision for psychological violence
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:1576 by Jonathan Svensson (S),

2025/26:3586 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) proposal 56,

2025/26:3591 by Ardalan Shekarabi et al. (S) proposal 19 in this part and

2025/26:3933 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) proposal 1.
notis:
The Riksdag agreed to the government's proposal to criminalize psychological violence. Through the bill, insulting patterns of behavior carried out to control or undermine a person that currently fall outside the criminal scope can be captured.
The regulation means it becomes criminal to repeatedly subject another person to insults in the form of accusations, derogatory statements, humiliating behavior, improper threats, improper coercion or improper surveillance, if the insults collectively were likely to seriously damage the person's self-esteem.
The regulation also means it becomes criminal to subject someone to improper surveillance that is persistent, if the action was likely to seriously damage the person's self-esteem.
The penalty is imprisonment for a maximum of four years and the legislative changes enter into force on July 1, 2026.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for
1. Act on amendment to the Enforcement Code,
2. Act on amendment to the Act (1981:775) on the introduction of the Enforcement Code,
3. Act on amendment to the Tax Procedure Act (2011:1244),
4. Act on amendment to the Coast Guard Act (2019:32),
5. Act on amendment to the Customs Authority Act (2024:710),
6. Act on amendment to the Act (2026:000) on amendment to the Act (1981:775) on the introduction of the Enforcement Code.
The Riksdag thereby approves Government Bill 2025/26:224 items 1-6 and rejects motion

2025/26:4008 by Joakim Järrebring et al. (S).
notis:
The Riksdag agreed to the government's proposal to streamline and modernize the Kronofogde Authority's ability to collect a debt.
The legislative changes mean that the Kronofogde Authority with the help of several law enforcement agencies to a greater extent will be able to seize property without being on site. This applies when the agencies encounter movable property in their activities.
Furthermore, it is proposed that an explicit provision be introduced that the Kronofogde Authority shall take into account the proportionality principle in debt collection. This means, among other things, that a distraint shall not be more intrusive for a person than necessary. It also introduces a rule that the child's best interests shall always be considered.
The government's proposal also means that immovable property and cooperative apartments shall be treated equally to as great an extent as possible in debt collection.
The purpose of the legislative changes is that higher selling prices for distrained property can be achieved, that more debts will be paid faster, and that confidence in the enforcement system will increase.
The legislative changes shall enter into force on July 1, 2026.

dok_titel: Strengthened efforts for elderly and for those who care for or support close relatives
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2025/26:3860 by Nadja Awad et al. (V) proposal 1.
notis:
The Riksdag agreed to the government's proposal which means that those living in special accommodation for the elderly shall be offered a fixed care contact. The person designated as fixed care contact shall be a nursing assistant.
Through the elderly care initiative over 7,000 employees have been further trained as nursing assistants and specialist nurses in 2023. The committee shares the government's assessment that more nursing assistants are necessary to provide the elderly with coherent, continuous and individually adapted care.
The government's proposal also means that the social board shall offer a support contact to those who care for or support a close relative. This means the individual can receive guidance to, or information about, healthcare, or about diagnoses. The committee shares the government's view that cooperation between the individual, the social board and other actors thereby becomes clearer.
Furthermore, the responsibility of the social board, healthcare provider and healthcare personnel to support children when a parent or other adult in the household becomes seriously ill or unexpectedly dies is clarified. The same responsibility shall apply if a child's sibling becomes seriously ill.
The legislative changes enter into force on July 1, 2026.

dok_titel: The principle of public access with relief rules for private small operators in the education sector
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:4024 by Anders Ygeman et al. (S) demands 3 and 4.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal to introduce the principle of public access for private preschools, private schools, and private after-school centers.
The proposal aims to ensure that the possibility of transparency is the same for all operators within the education sector and essentially entails the following:

The right to access public records shall apply to legal entities that are private operators within the education sector.
Such operators shall be equated with authorities when applying the Act on Public Access to Information and Secrecy, and certain secrecy provisions that apply to such operators shall be adapted so that secrecy does not hinder access to information about the education sector.
Smaller operators shall be permitted to apply rules that provide certain relief in handling public records. This shall apply to operators that have at most 450 children and pupils, or, if they only have private preschools, at most 100 children, or are part of a group where the group companies collectively have that many children or pupils.
What according to the Archives Act applies to archives of municipal authorities shall apply to the affected private operators, with the exception of smaller operators that shall preserve public records as a principal rule for at least seven years.
During the first two years after implementation, all legal entities that are private operators within the education sector shall be permitted to apply relief rules.

The new regulations enter into force on 1 January 2027.

The activity requirement aims, among other things, to counteract exclusion and to utilize labor. Persons who have received social assistance for at least three consecutive months shall be subject to the requirement.
The government's proposal includes a number of exceptions for when the activity requirement shall not apply, for example for persons under 18 years of age, those who have sickness benefit, or those who are on parental leave with a child under one year.

2025/26:4069 by Emma Nohrén et al. (MP).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal for a law on emergency stockpiles of goods in the food chain, that is, the entire process from farm to table. The purpose of the stockpiling is to ensure access to food if Sweden is at war or in imminent danger of war, or if, as a result of an extraordinary event, there is or risks becoming a shortage of food in the country.
Among other things, the following shall apply to Sweden's emergency stockpiles:

The government shall decide which goods in the food chain shall be emergency stockpiled and in what quantity, and where in the country there shall be emergency stockpiles.
The emergency stockpiles shall be held by the authority determined by the government. An emergency stockpile may also be held by a private actor with which the responsible authority enters into an agreement.
The goods that shall be emergency stockpiled shall be procured by the responsible authority and owned by the state.
Confidentiality shall apply to those who have participated in an individual's activities to hold an emergency stockpile at the request of an authority and who thereby become aware of sensitive information.

The government considers that emergency stockpiles should be built up gradually over a longer period.
The legal changes enter into force on 1 July 2026.

This shall apply to principals who have at most 450 children and pupils or, if they only have private preschools, at most 100 children, or are part of a group where the group companies together have so many children or pupils.
What applies according to the Archives Act for municipal authorities' archives shall apply to affected private principals, with the exception for smaller principals who shall preserve public records for at least seven years as a main rule.
During the first two years after implementation, all legal entities that are private principals within the education system shall be permitted to apply exemption rules. 

The new rules enter into force on 1 January 2027.

forslag_text:

notis:
A benefit ceiling shall be introduced to break benefit dependency and reduce social exclusion. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for reformed subsistence assistance.
The benefit ceiling consists of several sub-proposals:

a modernization of the so-called national norm
a limitation of subsistence assistance for larger households
a limited scope for the social committee to provide subsistence assistance at a higher level than the national norm. 

The proposal also means, among other things, that

those who have reduced working capacity due to illness shall submit a medical certificate in order to receive subsistence assistance
those who rent housing as a second-hand tenant shall only receive subsistence assistance for housing costs if the second-hand lease is approved
subsistence assistance shall only be given to persons who are legally resident in Sweden.

The purpose of the proposal is for more people to move from subsistence assistance to work.
The legislative changes that introduce a requirement to submit a medical certificate enter into force on 1 July 2026. Other legislative changes enter into force on 1 January 2027.

forslag_text:

2025/26:3953 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) amendments 4 and 5.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal to give the Police Authority the opportunity to use AI technology for real-time facial recognition.
The proposal means that the Police Authority shall be able to use AI technology if it is absolutely necessary to locate or identify a certain person

who is suspected of being subjected to abduction, human trafficking or human exploitation or who is missing and suspected of being a victim of a crime
if there is an imminent risk that the person will commit a serious crime that poses a danger to another person's life or physical safety
who can reasonably be suspected of having committed a certain serious crime for which the penalty scale includes imprisonment for four years or more or such a penalty may follow for attempt, preparation or complicity in such crimes, in order to investigate or prosecute the crime
who has been convicted of such a serious crime, in order to enforce the criminal sentence.

The use of the technology shall be proportionate and require authorization from a prosecutor or court. In urgent cases, the use may commence without authorization and an application for authorization must be made within 24 hours.
The new law and other legislative amendments come into force on July 1, 2026.

2025/26:3966 by Andreas Lennkvist Manriquez et al. (V),

The purpose of the proposal is for students, teachers, principals and other school staff to have a safe and secure educational and working environment and for students at risk to receive well-founded and correct support measures.
The proposal also means that more schools are obligated to inform that they have received a student at risk, since the proposal applies both between different external schools, as well as within the school between, for example, primary school, intermediate school and secondary school.

notis:
The Riksdag has addressed the Government's memorandum Deepened results reporting of international aid – Ukraine. In the memorandum, the Government provides a deepened account of Swedish aid's activities and results in Ukraine during the period 2022–2025.
Sweden's support for Ukraine's state budget has contributed to maintaining basic government functions and economic stability. This has contributed to strengthening the country's resilience, saving lives and reducing human suffering. At the same time, war-affected people, including many refugees, have received humanitarian aid in the form of, among other things, food, emergency housing, health care and livelihood support. Sweden also contributes to strengthening Ukraine's ability to resist continued Russian aggression as well as building up a stable and democratic society. The efforts have also aimed to deepen bilateral relations between Sweden and Ukraine.
The Riksdag shares the Government's assessment of the importance of continued strong and long-term Swedish and European support for Ukraine. With this, the Riksdag filed the Government's memorandum as documents, that is, closed the matter.

Grocery stores and pharmacies shall, with certain exceptions, be required to accept cash at physical points of sale with staffed checkouts.
Banks shall be required to provide places for cash deposits for consumers to a satisfactory extent throughout the country.
There shall be demand-adapted services for companies to handle change and deposit daily cash tills.

The Riksdag also decided to direct a formal request (tillkännagivande) to the government to investigate whether certain public-law services can also be covered by the obligation to accept cash payment proposed for grocery stores and pharmacies.

The Riksdag approved the government's proposal which addresses strengthening consumer protection on the credit market. The decision includes, among other things, a new consumer credit act.
The new consumer credit act is to strengthen consumer protection and adapt it to developments on the consumer credit market in recent years. The law regulates many different aspects of credit provision to consumers. It concerns, among other things, information, right of withdrawal, marketing, and interest rate and cost ceilings. To combat over-indebtedness, the rules for credit assessment are strengthened. Furthermore, a new licensing requirement is introduced which means that more business operators who provide or broker credit, among other things, are to be subject to supervision and meet requirements for sufficient knowledge and competence.
Through the proposals, an EU directive on consumer credit is implemented.
The new consumer credit act and the legislative changes enter into force on 20 November 2026.

The government wants to expand the registry check that is performed when someone is to be employed or otherwise accepted within the school system and other educational activities. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on expanded registry checks in the school system.
The proposal mainly means the following:

The registry check shall also include certain information in the suspicion registry and not only the criminal record registry, as it does today.
The registry extract shall not be older than six months when it is presented, as opposed to today's one year.
The time limit for when the person who is to be employed or otherwise accepted by the same employer can do so without presenting a registry extract again shall be lowered from one year to six months.
A registry check shall also be conducted on the person who is to be employed or otherwise accepted within municipal adult education.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2025/26:4018 by Anders Ygeman et al. (S) claim 1 and

2025/26:4041 by Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C) claim 2.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal aimed at creating better conditions for safety and study environment in schools through several coordinated measures.
The proposal entails, among other things, that the responsibility of the school board and principal for safety and study environment at the school unit shall be clarified. In addition to preventive work, the school board and principal shall work to maintain safety and study environment.
According to the proposal, schools shall be made mobile phone-free by collecting students' mobile phones at the beginning of the school day and returning them at the end of the school day. The proposal also entails that today's conduct rules shall be renamed to school rules, become school-wide and contain a plan for consequences for breaching the rules. The opportunities shall also be strengthened to use the disciplinary measures removal from the classroom, temporary relocation within the school unit and temporary placement outside the school unit as well as suspension.
The government also proposes that it shall be possible in certain cases to deny a student access to the school unit if the student threatens the safety of other students and staff. The school's expectations on students and their guardians shall be clarified through an expectations document.
In addition, it shall be possible to operate crisis schools on contract, that is an activity where students are temporarily provided teaching outside their own school unit.
The legislative changes take effect on 1 August 2026.

In the communication, the government also describes how the military support is coordinated in an international context, how the support is monitored and how lessons learned from the war in Ukraine are addressed, as well as the government's assessment of the effects of Swedish support.

dok_titel: New curricula – for a strong knowledge-based school
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2025/26:3998 by Isabell Mixter et al. (V) claim 1,

2025/26:4022 by Anders Ygeman et al. (S) claim 4 and

2025/26:4054 by Camilla Hansén et al. (MP) claim 5.
notis:
There should be stronger focus on knowledge in schools. Parliament approved the government's proposal which jointly aims at a school where the knowledge mission is in focus. New curricula shall be drawn up for primary level, intermediate level and upper secondary level.
Parliament shares the government's view that Sweden needs a strong knowledge-based school where teachers have good conditions to carry out their mission and where all students are given the conditions to reach the goals of education. A new knowledge perspective is needed along with new curricula that focus on teaching and learning.
Parliament's decision entails among other things the following:

It should be clear that the school's most important task is to convey and anchor knowledge and values.
The role of teachers shall be strengthened. It shall be the teachers who, on the basis of the curriculum, determine and lead the teaching.
The new curricula for the compulsory school forms shall be clearly knowledge-oriented and the level shall be adapted to children's cognitive development.
There should be strong focus on basic knowledge and skills, such as reading, writing and arithmetic.
The curricula shall also receive a more purposeful structure and the content shall be based on principles that promote high and equitable quality.
New courses in basic Swedish shall be introduced for students who are beginners in Swedish.
The principle of aggregate assessment shall apply for all grade levels, that is also for grade E.

Most of the legislative changes take effect on 1 July 2028. New curricula for primary school, adapted primary school, special school and Sami school shall start being used from autumn term 2028.

The changes also entail that the regulation of the guarantee for early support measures and extra adjustments shall be abolished. Instead, standardized tests shall be conducted at the beginning of autumn term in certain year groups to be able to identify students with support needs.
Students shall be given support teaching at an early stage in the compulsory school forms, upper secondary school and adapted upper secondary school in the subjects Swedish, Swedish as a second language and mathematics. The changes also entail that teachers within municipal adult education shall have access to or possibility for consultation with personnel with special education expertise.
The changes to the Schools Act take effect on 1 July 2028.

forslag_text:

The Riksdag has considered a statement from the government regarding the Swedish National Audit Office's examination of the state's work to acquire emission credits.

The Swedish National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the state's work with international climate efforts partially achieves its purposes.
The Swedish National Audit Office recommends that the government clarify objectives and expectations in the management of the Energy Agency and consider setting quantitative targets for acquiring emission credits in relation to the climate target 2045 and the milestone targets 2030 and 2040. The government is also recommended to monitor cost-effectiveness based on total cost, so that both the price per emission credit and administrative costs are taken into account and can be compared with other complementary measures.
Like the government, the Riksdag welcomes the Swedish National Audit Office's examination and considers it to constitute valuable material for the continued work to implement cost-effective international climate efforts. In its statement, the government partially agrees with the Swedish National Audit Office's recommendations.
The Riksdag placed the statement on file, which means the matter was closed.

forslag_text:

notis:
The Riksdag voted yes to the Government's proposal aimed at creating better conditions for safety and study peace in schools through several coordinated measures.
The proposal includes, among other things, that the principal's and rector's responsibility for safety and study peace at the school unit shall be clarified. In addition to preventive work, the principal and rector shall work to maintain safety and study peace.
According to the proposal, schools shall be made mobile-free by collecting students' mobile phones at the beginning of the school day and returning them at the end of the school day. The proposal also means that today's rules of conduct shall change their name to school rules, become school-wide and contain a plan for consequences for violations of the rules. The possibilities shall also be strengthened to use the disciplinary measures removal from the classroom, temporary relocation within the same school unit and temporary placement outside the same school unit as well as suspension.
The Government also proposes that in certain cases it should become possible to deny a student access to the school unit if the student threatens the safety of other students and staff. The school's expectations of students and their guardians shall be clarified through an expectations document.
In addition, it should be possible to conduct emergency school on contract, that is, an activity where students temporarily receive teaching outside their own school unit.
The legislative changes come into force on 1 August 2026.

dok_titel: New Curricula – for a Strong Knowledge-Based School
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:4036 by Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C) request 3 and

2025/26:4054 by Camilla Hansén et al. (MP) requests 3, 7 and 8.
notis:
There should be a stronger focus on knowledge in schools. The Riksdag approved the government's proposal which, taken together, aims for a school with the knowledge mission in focus. New curricula should be developed for lower grades, middle grades and upper grades.
The Riksdag shares the government's view that Sweden needs a strong knowledge-based school where teachers have good conditions to carry out their mission and where all students are given the conditions to achieve the goals of education. A new knowledge perspective and new curricula are needed that focus on teaching and learning.
The Riksdag's decision includes, among other things, the following:

- It should be clear that the school's most important task is to convey and anchor knowledge and values.
- Teachers' roles should be strengthened. It should be the teachers who, based on the curriculum, determine and lead the instruction.
- The new curricula for the compulsory school forms should be clearly knowledge-oriented and the level should be adapted to children's cognitive development.
- There should be a strong focus on basic knowledge and skills, such as reading, writing and arithmetic.
- The curricula should also have a more appropriate structure and the content should be based on principles that promote high and equal quality.
- New course curricula should be introduced in basic Swedish for students who are beginners in the Swedish language.
- The principle of overall assessment shall apply to all grade levels, that is, also for grade E.

Most of the legislative changes enter into force on July 1, 2028. New curricula for primary school, adapted primary school, special school and Sami school shall be used starting from the autumn term of 2028.

forslag_text:

b) the government's proposal for a law amending the Act (1994:1811) on Disciplinary Liability within Total Defense, etc.
Thereby the Riksdag approves proposition 2025/26:181 points 1 in this part and 3 and rejects motion

2025/26:4062 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP).
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for strengthened public protection and clearer consequences for repeat offenses. The proposal aims to strengthen public protection in cases of serious and repeated crime, reduce the risk of repeat offenses, increase security for crime victims and tighten consequences for misconduct or repeat offenses.
The legislative changes include, among other things, the following:

- Escape from certain forms of detention, such as remand detention, prison and custody, is criminalized
- Repeat offenses become more significant in sentencing
- Opportunities to combine supervisory sentences with imprisonment are expanded
- A person sentenced to supervisory sentencing or conditionally released shall be notified of restrictions on freedom of movement (residence restrictions) if he or she is involved in, or has a connection to a group that engages in serious crime and risks committing or otherwise participating in serious crime at a certain location or within a certain area
- Residence restrictions can be imposed for the purpose of protecting the complainant
- It is stated in law that involvement in, or connection to, a group that engages in serious crime shall be considered when deciding on furlough.

The legislative changes enter into force on July 2, 2026.

dok_titel: The National Audit Office report on international climate efforts
forslag_text:

2025/26:3949 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S) motions 2 and 3.
notis:
The Riksdag has addressed a letter from the government regarding the National Audit Office's review of the state's work on purchasing emission credits.
The National Audit Office has reviewed whether the state's work on purchasing emission credits achieves the intentions of international climate efforts: to reduce global greenhouse gas emissions, to promote climate transition and sustainable development in the countries where they are implemented, and to be able to contribute to achieving Sweden's climate policy goals in a cost-effective manner. The National Audit Office's overall conclusion is that the state's work on international climate efforts partially achieves its purposes.
The National Audit Office recommends the government to clarify objectives and expectations in the management of the Energy Agency and to consider setting quantitative targets for purchasing emission credits in relation to the 2045 climate target and the interim targets for 2030 and 2040. The government is also recommended to follow up cost-effectiveness based on total cost, so that both the price per emission credit and administrative costs are considered and can be compared with other complementary measures.
Like the government, the Riksdag welcomes the National Audit Office's review and considers it to be valuable material for continued work on implementing cost-effective international climate efforts. In its letter, the government partially agrees with the National Audit Office's recommendations.
The Riksdag referred the letter to the records, which means the matter was closed.

The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on strengthened medical expertise in municipal health and medical care. The proposal means that municipalities shall be able to engage physicians in their own care.
The Riksdag considers that the government's proposal entails increased flexibility regarding the municipalities' opportunities to ensure access to physicians and thus ultimately to provide care according to needs and of good quality.

rubrik: Report by the Swedish National Audit Office on the application of the fiscal framework 2025
dok_titel: Guidelines for economic policy and budget policy
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2025/26:4109 by Martin Ådahl (C) and 

files document 2025/26:241.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for guidelines on economic policy and budget policy in the spring budget bill.
Uncertainty and unpredictability regarding geopolitical and trade policy developments have led the government to revise forecasts for, among other things, GDP and unemployment compared to the spring budget bill. As a result, recovery in the Swedish economy is expected to continue at a slower pace than what was assessed in the spring budget bill.
Parliament agrees with the government that sustainable economic recovery must be ensured and that Sweden should continue to be built stronger to become more competitive and resilient. Parliament also shares the government's assessment that economic policy should focus on three areas: continuing to safeguard public finances, enabling more jobs in Sweden, and ensuring that effort is rewarded.
Parliament also decided to file the government's document in response to the Swedish National Audit Office's review report on the application of the fiscal framework 2025, that is, to close the matter. Parliament also rejected proposals in motions, of which twelve proposals are from the general motion period 2025/2026.
alternatives:

2025/26:4109 by Martin Ådahl (C) and 

files document 2025/26:241.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions 

2025/26:4044 by Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C) and 

2025/26:4058 by Camilla Hansén et al. (MP) demands 2 and 4.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal which, among other things, means that a new grading system and a new model for calculating students' merit scores will be introduced.
The government's proposal entails the following, among other things:

A new model for calculating students' merit scores shall be developed, where the merit score shall consist partly of the applicant's grade value, partly of the results from national final exams.
A grading scale with ten grade levels from 1 to 10, without a sharp pass/fail boundary, shall be introduced in compulsory school forms and voluntary school forms at upper secondary level. In the final grading of a subject, teachers shall have assessment consultations. School authorities shall submit grade information to an authority.
National final exams shall be introduced in primary school, special schools, upper secondary school, and municipal adult education at upper secondary level. The exams should be graded centrally.

The purpose is to more fairly reflect students' subject knowledge and counteract grade inflation.
Changes to the Education Act will mainly take effect on 1 July 2028. For municipal adult education, however, the changes will take effect on 1 January 2031.

dok_titel: Activities in the European Union during 2025
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions 

2025/26:2369 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V) demand 1, 

2025/26:3570 by Anna Lasses et al. (C) demand 2, 

2025/26:3623 by Morgan Johansson et al. (S) demands 30 and 33, 

2025/26:3729 by Kerstin Lundgren et al. (C) demand 18 and 

2025/26:3988 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V) demands 2, 5 and 15.
notis:
The government has submitted a document on EU activities during 2025. The document addresses decisions and events in the Union and presents the breadth of Union issues based on the work in the various Council configurations.
In the document, the government describes how European security has been challenged by an unstable neighborhood, hybrid threats, and a global context in which the rules-based international order is being questioned. Parliament believes, as it has before, that it is central to Sweden's security and world stability that the rules-based international order is maintained.
During the year, Sweden has been a driving force behind the EU imposing additional sanctions against Russia and Belarus due to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Parliament welcomes that the government is working to increase pressure on Russia.
The enlargement process in the Union has also made progress during 2025. Parliament believes an enlargement is important for peace, stability, and prosperity in Europe. But enlargement is only possible if the process is perceived as legitimate and has broad support in the member states.
Furthermore, Parliament believes that respect for the EU's common fundamental values – democracy, the rule of law, human rights, and international law – is one of the Union's greatest assets that must be guaranteed.
Parliament filed the document, that is, closed the matter.

The government proposes a new law which means that people living near wind power facilities shall have the right to compensation corresponding to a portion of the annual revenues from a facility, so-called wind power compensation. Parliament approved the government's proposal.
According to the government's proposal, wind power compensation shall be paid by the operator of a wind power facility to owners of residential buildings that are located within nine wind turbine heights from a wind turbine in a wind power facility. The wind power compensation is proposed to be higher the closer the facility is to the residence.
The government also proposes amendments to the Income Tax Act, which means that wind power compensation shall be tax-free to the extent it concerns a private residence.
The new law and the amendment to the law will take effect on 1 July 2026.

Some of the proposals are expected to affect the state's budget in coming years as well.

This includes entering into agreements with Videberg Kraft AB on fixed costs for a new nuclear waste program as well as capital contributions and acquisition of shares in the company.
The Riksdag also approved the government's proposal for a legislative amendment meaning that the Swedish Social Insurance Agency shall not charge any fee for connection to the electronic system for state dental care support. The proposal means that the provision on fees shall cease to apply at the end of July 2026.

notis:
The Government proposes a new law that means that residents near wind power facilities shall have the right to compensation equivalent to a share of the annual revenues from a facility, so-called wind power compensation. Parliament approved the Government's proposal.
According to the Government's proposal, wind power compensation shall be paid by the operator of a wind power facility to owners of residential buildings located within nine wind turbine heights from a wind turbine in a wind power facility. The wind power compensation is proposed to be higher the closer the residence is to the facility.
The Government also proposes amendments to the income tax law, which means that the wind power compensation shall be tax-free to the extent it concerns a private residence.
The new law and the amendment come into effect on July 1, 2026.

rubrik: Agreement on enhanced partnership and cooperation between the European Union and its Member States, on the one hand, and the Republic of Kyrgyzstan, on the other hand
dok_titel: Agreement on enhanced partnership and cooperation between the European Union and its Member States, on the one hand, and the Republic of Kyrgyzstan, on the other hand
forslag_text:
Parliament approves the agreement on enhanced partnership and cooperation between the European Union and its Member States, on the one hand, and the Republic of Kyrgyzstan, on the other hand.
Thereby Parliament concurs with proposition 2025/26:248 and rejects motion

2025/26:4190 by Jacob Risberg et al. (MP) claim 1.
notis:
Parliament approved the Government's proposal for an agreement on enhanced partnership and cooperation between the European Union and its Member States, on the one hand, and the Republic of Kyrgyzstan, on the other hand.
The agreement aims to deepen the political and economic relations between the EU and Kyrgyzstan and is based on the common values that the EU is built on: democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms and the principles of the rule of law. The agreement covers several areas of cooperation such as trade, sustainable development and connectivity, intellectual property, research and innovation, education, environment and climate change, the principles of the rule of law, human rights and civil society.
The European Union (EU) has since 1999 had a partnership and cooperation agreement with the Republic of Kyrgyzstan. With the enhanced agreement, today's political and economic conditions are better reflected, as well as the EU's ambition to further develop its relation with the country.

dok_titel: Improved rules for Swedish tonnage taxation
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion

2025/26:4128 by Niklas Karlsson et al. (S).
notis:
The Government wants to improve the tonnage taxation system. The system means that income from qualified shipping operations is calculated standardly based on vessels' net tonnage. The purpose of the improvements is to strengthen Sweden's competitiveness in the shipping industry. Parliament voted for the Government's proposal.
The Government's proposal means

that the tonnage taxation system is expanded to include certain activities within specialized shipping
greater opportunities to rent out qualified vessels without crew within the framework of tonnage-taxed operations
changed conditions for a vessel to be qualified
more generous terms for companies to use a so-called accelerated depreciation fund.

The proposals also mean that certain clarifications and adjustments are made to the regulations to achieve better compliance with the Commission's guidelines for state aid and decision-making practice. The proposals mean amendments to the income tax law and the tax procedure law.
The amendments come into effect on July 20, 2026 and are applied for the first time for tax years beginning after December 31, 2026.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion

2025/26:4128 by Niklas Karlsson et al. (S).

dok_titel: New law on municipal harbor operations
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for a law on municipal harbor operations.
Thereby Parliament approves proposition 2025/26:234 and rejects the motions

2025/26:4103 by Malin Östh et al. (V) motion 1,

2025/26:4125 by Aylin Nouri et al. (S) and

2025/26:4135 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (-).
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for new rules on municipal harbor operations. The rules are changed to be compatible with EU law. The decision entails that a new regulation for municipal harbors in Sweden is created.
Currently, harbors operated by municipalities are tax-exempt while other harbors pay tax according to general rules. The EU Commission has drawn Sweden's attention to the fact that this may contradict EU state aid rules. State aid that distorts competition by favoring certain actors is, according to EU competition rules, not permitted.
The decision entails that municipalities or regions that have harbor operations shall conduct them in a municipal corporation and on a commercial basis.
The new rules for municipal harbor operations come into force on 1 August 2026.

dok_titel: Time-limited housing for certain newly arrived immigrants – a new law on settlement
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for
1. law on settlement for certain newly arrived immigrants,
2. law amending the Land Code (jordabalken),
3. law amending the Act (2002:546) on the processing of personal data in labor market policy activities,
4. law amending the Reception Act (2026:000).
Thereby Parliament approves proposition 2025/26:215 points 1-4 and rejects the motions

2025/26:4077 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) motions 3 and 4,

2025/26:4079 by Ardalan Shekarabi et al. (S) motion 3 and

2025/26:4086 by Leila Ali Elmi et al. (MP) motions 2 and 3.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for a new law on settlement for certain newly arrived immigrants.
The decision entails, among other things, that municipalities shall continue to be required to receive newly arrived immigrants by assignment and that the distribution of assignments between municipalities shall be based on the conditions for integration in the municipalities. A municipality's request regarding the reception shall, however, under certain conditions be taken into account in the distribution. This means that municipalities will have greater influence over the reception of newly arrived immigrants than is currently the case.
In addition to the distribution criteria that apply today, including labor market and population size, consideration shall also be given to conditions in the housing market and areas where social exclusion is large.
Furthermore, the right to housing shall be time-limited to 36 months and it is the municipality that shall arrange housing during that time. The right to housing may be terminated early, among other things, if the newly arrived immigrant is not assigned to a labor market policy program and lacks acceptable reasons for it.
The new law and related amendments to other laws come into force on 1 January 2027.
alternatives:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for
1. law on settlement for certain newly arrived immigrants,
2. law amending the Land Code (jordabalken),
3. law amending the Act (2002:546) on the processing of personal data in labor market policy activities,
4. law amending the Reception Act (2026:000).
Thereby Parliament approves proposition 2025/26:215 points 1-4 and rejects the motions

dok_titel: An extended criminal liability for public officials
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts
a) the government's proposal for a law amending the Penal Code in the parts concerning Chapter 20, Section 2,
b) the government's proposal for a law amending the Act (1994:260) on public employment.
Thereby Parliament approves proposition 2025/26:217 points 1 in this part and 2 and rejects the motions

2025/26:4099 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) motion 1 and

2025/26:4112 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) motion 1.
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal which entails a new crime in the Penal Code designated as abuse of public office and that the minimum penalty for aggravated misconduct in office is increased to imprisonment for one year and six months.
Through the new crime, it is punishable to intentionally, in breach of law or other regulation, take or fail to take an action in order to gain an improper benefit or for someone else to gain such a benefit, or in order to wrongfully disadvantage someone else. The new crime applies to someone who holds a public office, exercises a public assignment or other public activity.
If the crime is aggravated, it shall be convicted for aggravated abuse of public office. The penalty for abuse of public office is proposed to be a fine or imprisonment for a maximum of two years. For aggravated abuse of public office, imprisonment for a minimum of one year and six months and a maximum of six years.
The legislative amendments come into force on 1 August 2026.

b) the government's proposal for a law amending the Act (1994:260) on public employment.

forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for
1) law amending the Act (1984:3) on nuclear technology activities,
2) law amending the Act (2006:647) on financing of nuclear waste products,
3) law amending the Act (2010:950) on liability and compensation for radiological accidents.
Thereby Parliament approves proposition 2025/26:168 points 1-3 and rejects the motions

2025/26:3959 by Birger Lahti et al. (V) and

2025/26:3982 by Katarina Luhr et al. (MP) motion 1.
notis:
The government wants mining and processing of nuclear materials to be treated in the same way as other metals and minerals within the framework of the comprehensive licensing process. Parliament approved the government's proposal.
The purpose of the government's proposal is for the assessment process for activities concerning both mining and processing of nuclear materials to a greater extent resemble the assessment process for other mining activities. This means that the process for initiating such activities becomes more transparent and efficient.
The changes are made with the purpose of creating appropriate regulation for mining and processing of nuclear materials, where radiation protection and safety requirements are adapted to the risks of the activity. The proposals entail that mining and processing of uranium at a comprehensive level will be treated in the same way as other metals and minerals within the framework of the comprehensive licensing process. This has the consequence, among other things, that the government's permissibility review under the Environmental Code will no longer cover facilities for mining and processing of nuclear materials. This simultaneously means that the approval of the municipal council will no longer be required for such activity to be permitted.
The Business Committee agrees with the government's assessment that this adaptation of the regulation entails that it becomes more logical and predictable. Overall, this creates better conditions for activities of strategic importance for the country's energy supply, as well as for Sweden to be able to contribute to both a higher degree of self-sufficiency in critical metals and minerals within the EU and the green transition.
The legislative amendments come into force on 15 July 2026.

The government wants to create better conditions for new establishment of nuclear technology facilities and presents proposals for amendments to the Environmental Code. Parliament approved the government's proposal.

the prohibition against nuclear technology facilities within coastal areas and archipelagos in Bohuslän, from the border with Norway to Brofjorden, in Småland and Östergötland, from Simpevarp to Arkö Sound, and in Ångermanland, from Storfjärden at the mouth of the Ångermanälven to Skagsudde, and on Öland is removed.

The legislative amendments come into force on 15 July 2026.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:4150 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) request 3 and

2025/26:4173 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) request 4.
notis:
The Government wants to streamline return work and make several amendments to the Aliens Act and other legislation. The Riksdag voted yes to the Government's proposal.
To streamline return work, the Government proposes that the Police Authority and the Migration Agency are to be given better tools to enforce departure and expulsion decisions. The Government proposes a new obligation for the Public Employment Service, the Swedish Social Insurance Agency, the Prison Service, the Enforcement Service, the Pensions Agency and the Tax Agency to take the initiative to provide information about a foreign national to the Police Authority if there is reason to believe that he or she does not have the right to stay in Sweden.
The proposal also includes that the authorities are given additional tools to clarify a foreign national's identity. It introduces a possibility to seize and search a foreign national's mobile telephone if it can be assumed to contain information about the foreign national's identity. In addition, fingerprints and photographs are to be used in alien affairs more extensively and more efficiently than today.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 13 July 2026.

dok_titel: Double penalties for crimes in criminal networks and enhanced criminal penalties
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposals for
1. Act amending the Penal Code,
2. Act amending the Code of Judicial Procedure,
3. Act amending the Tax Offences Act (1971:69),
4. Act amending the Act (2000:1225) on penalties for smuggling,
5. Act amending the Bribery Offences Act (2007:612),
6. Act amending the Act (2014:307) on penalties for money laundering offences,
7. Act amending the Act (2016:1307) on penalties for market abuse on the securities market,
8. Act amending the Subsidy Offences Act (2025:1267).
Thereby, the Riksdag approves Government Bill 2025/26:218 points 1-8 and rejects the motions

2025/26:3027 by Noria Manouchi (M) requests 3, 5 and 6,

2025/26:3229 by Marléne Lund Kopparklint (M),

2025/26:3586 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) request 16,

2025/26:4111 by Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) requests 3 and 4,

2025/26:4114 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) request 1 and

2025/26:4121 by Lorena Delgado Varas et al. (-).
notis:
The Government wants penalties in a better way to reflect the seriousness of the crime, for the victims' perspective to have greater influence and for public safety to be improved. The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal.
The proposal means that

the ten-year limit for time-limited sentences is removed
nearly 50 criminal penalty scales are enhanced
a new regulation of the combined penalty scale in cases of multiple offences is introduced which means that the highest sentence that can be imposed is the highest maximum sentence doubled
life imprisonment can be imposed as a joint sentence for certain serious cases of repeated violent and sexual crimes
a new sentence enhancement provision is introduced which aims at all crimes that are connected to criminal networks
the conditions for detention are expanded to include the crimes of gross violation of a woman's integrity, gross violation of integrity and honor-based oppression.

The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 August 2026.

dok_titel: Sharpened and clearer requirements for good conduct for residence permits
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:4154 by Ida Karkiainen et al. (S) request 1 and

2025/26:4161 by Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C) request 2.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal that a foreign national's good conduct, that is to say way of life, to a greater extent should be taken into account when examining the right to residence permits, both when it comes to granting and revoking such permits.
The purpose of the change is primarily to increase the possibilities of removing persons from the country because of their way of life. Furthermore, residence permits should among other things be able to be revoked in more situations than today.
The decision means among other things that the requirements are sharpened for obtaining and retaining a residence permit by having a person's way of life, so called good conduct, have greater significance when examining the right to residence permits. It becomes possible to deny or revoke a residence permit for misconduct such as not complying with laws, regulations and administrative decisions, having large debts or making a living in a dishonest way.
The legislative amendments begin to enter into force on 13 July 2026.

forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motion

2025/26:4099 by Teresa Carvalho et al. (S) demand 2.
notis:
Parliament voted yes on the government's proposal which introduces a new crime in the Penal Code called misuse of public position and sharpens the minimum penalty for serious dereliction of duty to imprisonment for one year and six months.
Through the new crime it is punishable to intentionally contrary to law or other regulation take or fail to take an action in order to gain an improper advantage or so that someone else obtains such an advantage, or to improperly harm someone else. The new crime applies to anyone who holds a public office, exercises a public assignment or other public activity.
If the crime is serious it shall be convicted of serious misuse of public position. The penalty for misuse of public position is proposed to be fines or imprisonment for no more than two years. For serious misuse of public position imprisonment for no less than one year and six months and no more than six years.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 August 2026.

forslag_text:

notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal regarding coordinated care and support operations, among other things.
The proposal aims to achieve more uniform and coordinated care for persons with harmful use or dependency and other psychiatric conditions. The care shall be directed at persons who have special needs for healthcare and social services over a longer period due to a mental disability.
The Government's proposal entails an expanded requirement for cooperation between municipalities and regions. The regions shall, among other things, organize care for persons with harmful use or dependency so that it can be provided in coordination with other psychiatric care.
Another change is that the word "missbruk" (misuse) is removed and replaced with "bruk" (use) or "skadligt bruk och beroende" (harmful use and dependency) in several statutes concerning healthcare and social services.
The legislative changes shall enter into force on 1 January 2028.

notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal that Statistics Sweden's microsimulation model (Fasit) should be expanded to collect data on the household sector's debt and debt payments.

dok_titel: Compensation for limitations on disposal due to species protection
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2025/26:4113 by Helena Lindahl et al. (C) request 1.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on amendments to the Environmental Code. The amendments essentially mean that forest and land owners shall have the right to compensation when regulations on the protection of animals and plants lead to restrictions on their land use. The legislative amendments aim to strengthen ownership rights to forest and land, while at the same time increasing incentives for the protection of species.
The amendments also mean that it shall be possible for the state to demand repayment of paid compensation if the restriction due to species protection no longer exists. Such a decision on repayment must, however, be reasonable in relation to the individual property owner and be assessed based on the circumstances in the individual case.
The legislative amendments enter into force on the day the government determines.

2025/26:4113 by Helena Lindahl et al. (C) request 1.

dok_titel: A clear regulatory framework for active forestry
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:4143 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) and 

2025/26:4145 by Helena Lindahl et al. (C) request 1.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal on several regulatory simplifications in forestry.
The legislative amendments include the following:

A notification for consultation for forestry measures under the Environmental Code shall be required only if it is specified in regulations that the government determines.
The land owner's cost to obtain the knowledge needed before a forestry measure is taken, for example regarding protected species in a forest area, shall be reasonable in relation to the property's value.
The confidentiality for the protection of animal and plant species shall be changed so that landowners can access the information needed to determine if consultation is required.
The Forest Board's decisions under the Forestry Act shall be appealed to a Land and Environmental Court instead of to an Administrative Court.
The deadline for non-profit environmental organizations to appeal decisions about forestry or forestry measures shall be counted from the day the decision was made. Additionally, the Forest Board shall be given standing as a party when environmental organizations appeal the agency's decision.

The proposal aims, among other things, to strengthen ownership rights and increase predictability for forest owners.
The legislative amendments shall mainly enter into force on 1 January 2027. However, the provision that consultation requirements under the Environmental Code shall apply only if specified in an ordinance shall first enter into force on the day the government determines.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:4143 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) and 

2025/26:4145 by Helena Lindahl et al. (C) request 1.
