rubrik: Foreigners who arrived in Sweden before reaching age 15
dok_titel: Tightened rules on expulsion due to crime
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects the motions

2025/26:4095 by Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C) demand 4 and

2025/26:4097 by Annika Hirvonen et al. (MP) demand 5.
notis:
Parliament said yes to the Government's proposal to tighten the rules on expulsion due to crime so that more foreigners who commit crimes are expelled. As a main rule, crimes that carry stricter punishment than fines can lead to expulsion. Furthermore, the balancing of reasons for and against expulsion in more cases shall lead to expulsion.
The rules are also changed so that persons who came to Sweden before reaching the age of 15 no longer receive the same protection against expulsion. Furthermore, courts should no longer take into account implementation obstacles, that is, practical obstacles to carrying out the expulsion.
Furthermore, re-entry bans will become longer and in certain cases apply without time limit. Prosecutors should also in certain cases be obliged to request expulsion in criminal proceedings. Finally, stricter penalties for certain crimes under the Aliens Act are introduced.
The legislative changes begin to apply on 1 September 2026.

rubrik: Sample collection of information on household debt
dok_titel: Sample collection of information on household debt
forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the Government's proposal for a law amending the Act (2019:508) on treatment of personal data in the distribution-analytical statistics system for income and transfers.
Thereby Parliament approves Government bill 2025/26:255 and rejects motion

2025/26:4185 by Mikael Damberg et al. (S) demand 1.
notis:
Parliament said yes to the Government's proposal that Statistics Sweden's microsimulation model (Fasit) should be expanded to be able to collect information on the household sector's debts and debt payments.
The proposal means that it will become possible in Fasit to analyze individuals' and households' resilience and sensitivity to economic disturbances, such as for example an income loss or unexpected interest rate changes. The purpose of the Government's proposal is to improve the decision-making basis for economic policy and make it easier to develop appropriate measures.
The Government means that a collection to Fasit limited to only include information on debts is sufficient to achieve the purposes intended. Such a limitation provides the basis needed to better shape policy within financial stability and distribution policy. At the same time, unnecessary mapping of individuals' and households' economy is avoided.
The legislative changes begin to apply on 1 August.
alternatives:

dok_titel: A clear regulatory framework for active forestry
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion

2025/26:4147 by Rebecka Le Moine et al. (MP).
notis:
Parliament said yes to the Government's proposal on several regulatory simplifications in forestry.
The legislative changes include, among other things, the following:

Notification for consultation for forestry measures under the Environmental Code is needed only if it follows from regulations that the Government determines.
The landowner's cost to acquire the knowledge needed before a forestry measure is taken, for example regarding protected species in a forest area, shall be reasonable in relation to the property's value.
The secrecy to protect animal and plant species is changed so that landowners can access the information needed to determine whether consultation is required.
The Forest Board's decisions under the Forest Management Act shall be appealed to a land and environmental court instead of to an administrative court.
The deadline for environmental organizations to appeal decisions on forestry or forestry measures shall be counted from the day the decision was announced. Furthermore, the Forest Board should be given party status when environmental organizations appeal the authority's decision.

The proposal aims, among other things, to strengthen property rights and increase predictability for forest owners.
The legislative changes shall primarily begin to apply on 1 January 2027. The provision that consultation requirement under the Environmental Code shall apply only if it follows from a regulation shall, however, apply first on a day that the Government determines.
alternatives:
Parliament rejects motion

2025/26:4147 by Rebecka Le Moine et al. (MP).

In the law on transparency in party financing, among other things, a prohibition against receiving anonymous and foreign contributions is introduced, regardless of amount. The parties' duty to disclose information shall also be expanded and the oversight of compliance with the rules shall be tightened.
A new law shall regulate the influence of decision-makers, among other things through advocacy actors (lobbyists) registering with Kammarkollegiet (the Government Offices), as well as disclosing information about their communication with political decision-makers.
The decision also includes a new law regulating partisan political contributions from labor market organizations, such as trade unions and employer organizations. The law includes among other things that a member of a labor market organization shall be able to submit a statement that his or her membership fee shall not be used as a contribution for partisan political purposes.
The new legislation enters into force on 1 July 2027.

rubrik: Extra Amendment Budget for 2026 - Support to Ukraine and Support to Households and Other Measures Regarding the War in the Middle East
dok_titel: Extra Amendment Budget for 2026 – Support to Ukraine and Support to Households and Other Measures Regarding the War in the Middle East
forslag_text:
Amendments to the State Budget for 2026
The Riksdag
a) approves changed appropriation frames for expenditure areas and allocates changed and new appropriations in accordance with the Committee's proposal in Appendix 4,
b) authorizes the Government to undertake financial commitments during 2026 which, including previous commitments, require future appropriations of at most the amounts and within the time periods that the Committee proposes in Appendix 7,
c) approves amended calculation of revenues in the State Budget for 2026 according to the Government's proposal,
d) authorizes the Government during 2026 and 2027 for appropriation 1:3 Acquisition of Materiel and Facilities within expenditure area 6 Defense and Civil Protection to decide to donate defense materiel to Ukraine in the form of naval command materiel and, as part of the Gripen E/F sales, up to 16 Jas 39 Gripen C/D including qualified ammunition that can be dispensed by the Swedish Armed Forces during a limited period, to a value of at most 19,571,000,000 kronor,
e) authorizes the Government to conclude an agreement with Ukraine on the sale of up to 20 Gripen E/F including associated air defense systems,
f) approves the proposed use of appropriation 1:12 Swedish Transport Agency within expenditure area 22 Communications,
g) approves the proposed use of appropriation 1:17 Measures for Rural Environment and Structure within expenditure area 23 Rural Industries, Countryside and Food.
Thereby the Riksdag approves Government Bill 2025/26:275 points 5-11 and rejects the motions

2025/26:4199 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) requests 2 and 4 as well as

2025/26:4201 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) request 2.

The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposals for
1. an Act amending the Act (2026:372) amending the Act (2025:1358) amending the Act (1994:1776) on Energy Tax,
2. an Act amending the Act (1994:1776) on Energy Tax,
3. an Act amending the Act (2026:373) amending the Act (1994:1776) on Energy Tax,
4. an Act amending the Act (1994:1776) on Energy Tax.

2025/26:4199 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) request 1 and

2025/26:4201 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) request 1.

Duty Exemption for Jet Fuel
The Riksdag adopts the Committee's proposal in Appendix 9 to an Act amending the Act (1994:1776) on Energy Tax.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal for an extra amendment budget to provide support to Ukraine and support to households and other measures regarding the war in the Middle East.
The proposal means, among other things, that the Government, through so-called authorizations, shall have the right to decide to donate 16 Jas 39 Gripen C/D including qualified ammunition to Ukraine, as well as to conclude an agreement with Ukraine on the sale of Gripen E/F with associated air defense systems.
The Government also proposes further temporary reduced tax on petrol and diesel during the period July 1 – November 30, 2026, temporary support for reduced prices in public transport during the period July 1 – December 31, 2026, and measures to support the aviation and agricultural sectors.
In addition to the Government's proposal, the Finance Committee on its own initiative submitted a bill on duty exemption for jet fuel. The proposal means that jet fuel is given the same conditions regarding energy tax as aviation fuel. The legislative change enters into force on July 1, 2026. A committee initiative means that the Committee has taken the initiative for the proposal. It is not based on a Government Bill or a parliamentary motion.
Overall, the Government's proposal means that the financial savings of the public administration and the State budget balance are expected to improve by 5.3 billion kronor in 2026. Proposals for changes to order authorizations for 2026 mean that the Government estimates that appropriations need to increase by a total of 22.6 billion kronor for 2027–2034.
The Government can submit ordinary amendment budgets twice a year. But it can also submit extra amendment budgets if it considers there are special grounds for it. According to the Government, the situation in Ukraine and fuel and aviation fuel prices due to the war in the Middle East are such grounds, and the Riksdag makes no other assessment.

notis:
On June 15, the Riksdag approved certain parts of the Government's proposal for stricter rules on supervision and detention in the migration process. The new rules that the Riksdag approved mean that more forms of supervision as an alternative to detention are introduced. Supervision can mean that a person is required to reside at a specific place or stay within a specific area.
The residence requirement can be combined with conditions on electronic monitoring if it is necessary to control that the residence requirement is followed. It will become clearer what conditions apply for placing a person under supervision and for detaining a person. Moreover, it will become clearer which authority is responsible at each stage of the migration process for deciding on supervision and detention.
These rules enter into force in large part on July 21, 2026.
During the debate in the chamber on June 14, a request for suspension of consideration was submitted regarding certain proposals. The request concerned certain grounds for detaining children, time limits for detention of certain children, and separation of children from their guardians.

On June 17, the Riksdag decided to suspend consideration of the bills concerning certain grounds for detaining children, time limits for detention of certain children, and separation of children from their guardians.
The suspension decision means that the Government's bills are returned to the Social Insurance Committee and become suspended there for at least twelve months.

dok_titel: New opportunities to combat online recruitment
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion

2025/26:4195 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP).
notis:
Parliament approved the government's proposal for a new law on removal of recruitment content online and an amendment to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act.
The new regulation means that recruitment content online, which is used to recruit in particular children and young people to commit crimes, can be removed or made inaccessible on digital platforms following a decision by an authority.
The new regulatory framework aims to prevent online recruitment in particular of children and young people, and to combat 'crime as a service', which means that serious crimes, such as explosions and shootings, are advertised and coordinated by criminals through various digital services.
The decision means that a competent authority can decide on injunctions for recruitment content to be removed or made inaccessible. An injunction shall be directed at the hosting service provider, that is, the one who provides the platform where the content is located. The recruitment content shall be removed as soon as possible and no later than one hour from when the hosting service provider received the injunction. A penalty fee can be imposed on the hosting service provider who violates its obligations under the new law.
The new rules enter into force on 15 July 2026.

2025/26:4195 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP).

forslag_text:
Parliament adopts the government's proposal for
1. law on amendment to the Population Registration Act (1991:481),
2. law on amendment to the Aliens Act (2005:716),
3. law on amendment to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (2009:400),
4. law on amendment to the Alien Data Act (2016:27),
5. law on amendment to the Act (2018:1693) on the police treatment of personal data within the scope of the crime data act,
6. law on amendment to the Act (2022:1697) on coordination numbers,
7. law on amendment to the Population Registration Data Act (2026:126),
8. law on amendment to the Act (2026:000) on amendment to the Act (2026:000) on amendment to the Act (2025:945) on amendment to the Alien Data Act (2016:27).
Thus parliament approves proposition 2025/26:261 points 1-8 and rejects motion

2025/26:4187 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V).
notis:
The government wants to see expanded powers for the Swedish Tax Agency within civil registration activities and therefore proposes, among other things, that a new crime be introduced: promotion of incorrect population registration. Parliament approved the government's proposal.
The government considers it important that Sweden has correct population registration in order, among other things, to prevent identity fraud and to establish the identity of the persons who are present and resident in the country.
It is the Swedish Tax Agency that is responsible for questions about population registration and coordination numbers. The government therefore wants the Swedish Tax Agency to have expanded powers within civil registration activities through amendments to several laws.
The proposals mean, among other things, the following:

The crime-free area for minor population registration crimes is expanded.
A new criminal provision is introduced – promotion of incorrect population registration.
Opportunities for the Swedish Tax Agency to use and store biometric data are expanded.
Exchange of information regarding fingerprints, facial image, and biometric data between the Migration Agency and the Swedish Tax Agency.
The Police Authority can request biometric data from the Swedish Tax Agency for crime prevention.

The law amendments enter into force on 1 December 2026.

dok_titel: Supplementary Budget for 2026 – Support for Ukraine and support for households and other measures in connection with the war in the Middle East
forslag_text:
Parliament rejects motion 

2025/26:4199 by Janine Alm Ericson et al. (MP) claim 3.
notis:
Parliament agreed to the Government's proposal for a supplementary budget to provide support to Ukraine and support for households and other measures in connection with the war in the Middle East.
The proposal entails, among other things, that the Government, through so-called authorizations, shall obtain the right to decide to donate to Ukraine 16 Jas 39 Gripen C/D including qualified ammunition, as well as to enter into an agreement with Ukraine regarding the sale of Gripen E/F with associated air defense systems.
The Government also proposes further temporary reduced taxation on petrol and diesel during the period July 1–November 30, 2026, temporary support for reduced prices in public transport during the period July 1–December 31, 2026 and measures to support the aviation and agricultural sectors.
In addition to the Government's proposal, the Finance Committee on its own initiative presented a legislative proposal on tax exemption for jet fuel. The proposal entails that jet fuel is given the same energy tax conditions as aviation fuel. The legislative change takes effect on July 1, 2026. A committee initiative means that the committee has taken the initiative for the proposal. It is not based on a Government proposal or a parliamentary motion.
In total, the Government's proposal means that the general government's financial savings and the State's budget balance is estimated to improve by SEK 5.3 billion in 2026. Proposals for changes to procurement authorizations for 2026 entail that the Government estimates that appropriations need to increase by a total of SEK 22.6 billion for 2027–2034.
The Government may submit regular supplementary budgets twice a year. However, it may also submit supplementary budgets if it considers that there are special grounds for it. The situation in Ukraine and fuel and aviation fuel prices in connection with the war in the Middle East are, according to the Government, such grounds, and Parliament makes no other assessment.

rubrik: Terrorist listing of the Wagner group
dok_titel: Activities in the European Union in 2022
forslag_text: Parliament supports what the committee states regarding a terrorist listing of the Wagner group and formally requests this to the government.
notis:
Parliament directed a formal request (tillkännagivande) to the government to actively work to achieve consensus within the EU to list the state-sponsored Russian so-called Wagner group as a terrorist group under EU terrorist sanctions.
In connection with the formal request, Parliament also points out that there is likely a need to upgrade EU's rules for terrorist listing so that it can better address threats from actors with state connections. According to current rules, a terrorist listing requires that a group is subject to legal proceedings for terrorism offenses. There must therefore be an ongoing or concluded legal process.
The formal request came in connection with Parliament handling a statement from the government regarding activities in the European Union in 2022 with accompanying motions, including on sanctions against Russia. Parliament rejected the motions and filed the statement with the records, that is, concluded the matter.
alternatives: Parliament supports what the committee states regarding a terrorist listing of the Wagner group and formally requests this to the government.

dok_titel: Prescription of Removal Decisions, Abolition of Track Change, and Certain Questions on Return Bans
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposals for
1. an Act amending the Aliens Act (2005:716),
2. an Act amending the Act (2013:156) on civic orientation for certain newly arrived immigrants,
3. an Act amending the Act (2024:1225) amending the Act (2022:894) amending the Act (2013:156) on civic orientation for certain newly arrived immigrants,
4. an Act amending the Act (2022:894) amending the Act (2013:156) on civic orientation for certain newly arrived immigrants.
With this, the Riksdag approves Government Bill 2024/25:92 points 1-4 and rejects motion 

2024/25:3324 by Tony Haddou et al. (V) points 1-3.
notis:
The Government proposes legislative amendments, among other things, with the aim of getting more people to leave Sweden after a removal decision, that is deportation or expulsion to their home country. The Riksdag said yes to the proposal.
The legislative amendments involve, among other things, the following:

A removal decision shall cease to apply (become prescribed) five years from when the alien has complied with the decision and left Sweden. According to current rules, the corresponding period is four years. If the decision is accompanied by a so-called return ban that is in effect at that time, the decision shall cease to apply only when the time for the return ban expires.
A return ban shall be determined for a maximum of five years, instead of one year as applies today. A return ban means a prohibition to return to Sweden. The return ban can be longer, among other things, if the person poses a serious security threat.
The system with so-called track change is abolished. Track change means that a person who has received a rejection of their asylum application has the possibility to instead apply for residence and work permit without leaving Sweden.

The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 April 2025.
The Riksdag also decided to say no to proposals in motions in the area, of which two were submitted during the general motion period in 2024.
alternatives:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposals for

The Government has presented its research policy for the years 2025–2028. In connection with this, the Government also presented a proposal which means that the Government shall be able to determine rules so that universities can decide that an appointment with them can be combined with an appointment outside the university. Parliament agreed to the Government's proposal. Today, combined appointments at universities only apply to certain positions such as specialist-trained doctors and dentists and the Government's proposal means that the limitation to certain sectors or positions can be removed.
The purpose of the legislative change is to increase the opportunity for knowledge and expertise exchange between individual researchers, educational institutions and other sectors of society and thereby strengthen competence supply and competitiveness. The legislative change enters into force on 1 July 2025.
Parliament also directed an urging, a so-called formal request (tillkännagivande), to the Government regarding the Government's announced investigation into how appropriate today's administrative form is for state educational institutions. According to Parliament, such an investigation into changed organizational form should not be carried out. The formal request (tillkännagivande) came in connection with a proposal in a follow-up motion.
Parliament rejected the other motions, approximately 140 proposals of which come from the general motion period 2024.

notis:
Parliament agreed to the Government's proposal on new rules for aquaculture.
The term aquaculture is used for activities that cultivate aquatic animals and plants such as fish, mussels, crustaceans and algae. To conduct aquaculture, several approvals are required today according to various legislation and by different authorities, among other things from an environmental perspective.
According to the proposal, the possible environmental impact of aquaculture should only be assessed according to the Environmental Code's rules on environmentally hazardous activities. This means that

the person conducting aquaculture does not need to apply for a cultivation permit for the activity
the possible impact the activity has on surrounding environments should be taken into account according to environmental legislation instead of according to the fisheries legislation
the Government, or the authority determined by the Government, should have the right to determine rules for, for example, which organisms may be cultivated in different water areas
the rule that aquaculture must seek permission for water activities according to the Environmental Code, that is, for example, have its water facility approved, is repealed.

The legislative changes enter into force 1 July 2026.
Parliament rejected a number of proposals in motions on aquaculture, of which 13 were submitted during the general motion period 2024.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for
1. an act amending the Planning and Building Act (2010:900) in the parts not covered by the committee's proposal above,
2. an act amending the Act (2006:985) on Energy Performance Certification of Buildings,
3. an act amending the Act (2022:333) on Energy Metering in Buildings.
Thereby the Riksdag approves government proposition 2025/26:180 points 1 in this part, 2 and 3 and rejects motion

2025/26:4059 by Amanda Palmstierna et al. (MP) requests 3 in this part and 4.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal to make rules clearer and simpler when building, modifying, or altering a building.
When making a major alteration to a building, the requirements that exist for design and technical characteristics are proposed to be met primarily for the part of the building that is being altered. The possibility of simultaneously imposing requirements on the entire building is limited. Such consequential requirements may only be imposed if needed to address serious risks to health and safety, or to meet requirements for broadband connection, energy efficiency, thermal insulation, and sustainable mobility.
The changes also mean that the word "reconstruction" should be replaced with "major building modification".
The changes also include certain easings in the requirements for accessibility for people with impaired mobility or orientation. For example, these requirements do not apply when a new dwelling is fitted out in an attic or basement.
The new rules come into force on 1 January 2027.
alternatives:

1. an act amending the Planning and Building Act (2010:900) in the parts not covered by the committee's proposal above,
2. an act amending the Act (2006:985) on Energy Performance Certification of Buildings,
3. an act amending the Act (2022:333) on Energy Metering in Buildings.

2025/26:3953 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) requests 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal to give the Police Authority the opportunity to use AI technology for real-time facial recognition.
The proposal means that the Police Authority shall be able to use AI technology if it is absolutely necessary in order to locate or identify a particular person

who is suspected of being a victim of human trafficking, human smuggling, or human exploitation or who is missing and suspected of being a victim of a crime
where there is an imminent risk that the person will commit a serious crime that poses a danger to another person's life or physical safety
who can reasonably be suspected of having committed a particular serious crime for which the penal code provides imprisonment for four years or more or such a sentence can follow for attempt, preparation, or complicity in such crimes, in order to investigate or prosecute the crime
who has been sentenced for such a serious crime, in order to enforce the criminal penalty.

The use of the technology must be proportionate and must require authorization from a prosecutor or court. In urgent cases, use may be initiated without authorization and then an application for authorization must be made within 24 hours.
The new law and other amendments come into force on 1 July 2026.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for
1. an act on temporary enforcement of Swedish prison sentences abroad,
2. an act on the applicability of the Work Environment Act for employees of the Swedish Prison and Probation Service when serving at a correctional institution abroad,
3. an act amending the Social Insurance Code,

5. an act amending the Income Tax Act (1999:1229),

7. an act amending the Election Act (2005:837),

10. an act amending the Prison Time Act (2018:1251),
11. an act amending the Social Services Act (2025:400),
12. an act amending the Act (2025:1053) on Enforcement of Prison Sentences with Electronic Monitoring.
Thereby the Riksdag approves government proposition 2025/26:185 points 3-14 and rejects the motions

2025/26:3997 by Samuel Gonzalez Westling et al. (V) in this part and

2025/26:4063 by Ulrika Westerlund et al. (MP) request 1 in this part.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposal to approve the agreement between Sweden and Estonia that makes it possible to temporarily enforce Swedish prison sentences in Estonia.
On 18 June 2025, an agreement was signed between Sweden and Estonia that makes it possible for persons sentenced to imprisonment in Sweden to temporarily serve their sentence in an Estonian institution, where the Estonian correctional authority shall be responsible for enforcement. The purpose of the agreement is to help address the serious shortage of places within the Swedish Prison and Probation Service.
The Riksdag has now approved the agreement and adopted the proposals for legislative amendments needed as a result of the agreement.
The new legal provisions come into force on 3 July 2026.
alternatives:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposal for
1. an act on temporary enforcement of Swedish prison sentences abroad,

rubrik: Adaptation of the grading system to Comvux
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:4001 by Isabell Mixter et al. (V) proposal 1 and

2025/26:4025 by Anders Ygeman et al. (S) proposal 5.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal, which among other things entails the introduction of a new grading system and a new model for calculating students' merit values.
The government's proposal includes, among other things, the following:

A new model for calculating students' merit values shall be developed, where the merit value shall consist partly of the applicant's grade value and partly of the results from national final exams.
A grading scale with ten grade levels from 1 to 10, without a clear threshold for passing, shall be introduced in compulsory school forms and voluntary school forms at upper secondary level. When assigning final grades in a subject, teachers shall have an assessment consultation. School principals shall submit grade information to a public authority.
National final exams shall be introduced in primary school, special school, upper secondary school, and municipal adult education at upper secondary level. The exams should be marked centrally.

The purpose is to more fairly reflect students' subject knowledge and counteract grade inflation.
The changes to the School Act shall enter into force on 1 July 2028 for the most part. For municipal adult education, however, the changes shall enter into force on 1 January 2031.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2025/26:4001 by Isabell Mixter et al. (V) proposal 1 and

2025/26:4025 by Anders Ygeman et al. (S) proposal 5.

dok_titel: Activities in the European Union during 2025
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2025/26:2369 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V) item 7, 

2025/26:2831 by Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al. (C) item 40, 

2025/26:3411 by Jacob Risberg et al. (MP) items 14 and 34, 

2025/26:3593 by Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S) item 35, 

2025/26:3623 by Morgan Johansson et al. (S) items 5 and 6, 

2025/26:3729 by Kerstin Lundgren et al. (C) item 39 and 

2025/26:3988 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V) items 25, 26 and 28.
notis:
The Government has submitted a communication on EU activities during 2025. The communication addresses decisions and events in the union and reports on the breadth of union issues based on the work in the various Council formations.
In the communication, the Government describes how European security has been challenged by an unstable neighbourhood, hybrid threats and a global context in which the rules-based international order is being questioned. The Riksdag believes, as before, that it is central to Sweden's security and stability in the world that the rules-based international order is maintained.
During the year, Sweden has been a driving force behind the EU imposing additional sanctions against Russia and Belarus due to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The Riksdag welcomes the Government's efforts to increase pressure on Russia.
The enlargement process in the union has also made progress during 2025. The Riksdag believes an enlargement is important for peace, stability and prosperity in Europe. But an enlargement is only possible if the process is perceived as legitimate and has broad support among the member states.
Furthermore, the Riksdag believes that respect for the EU's common fundamental values – democracy, the rule of law, human rights and international law – is one of the union's foremost assets that must be guaranteed.
The Riksdag placed the communication on file, that is, closed the matter.

rubrik: Subsidiarity review of the proposal for a regulation on the 28th order corporate law framework
dok_titel: Subsidiarity review of the Commission's proposal for a regulation on the 28th order corporate law framework 'EU Inc.'
forslag_text: The Riksdag decides not to submit a reasoned opinion and places the opinion on file.
notis:
The Riksdag has reviewed the EU Commission's proposal for a regulation on the 28th order corporate law framework based on the so-called subsidiarity principle, that is, the principle that decisions on new EU laws should be made as close to citizens as possible. The EU should only take action if it is more effective than if individual countries act on their own. The principle protects member states' right to make their own decisions at national level.
The Riksdag notes that the lack of an EU-wide corporate law framework is a structural problem that makes it difficult for companies to expand their operations across borders. New EU rules on companies are a step in the work of strengthening the EU's competitiveness and creating a better business climate. It can also reduce costs and simplify compliance with member states' corporate law rules.
The Riksdag assesses that member states themselves cannot achieve measures to solve this on their own. A new EU corporate form can only be implemented at EU level.
The Riksdag believes that the proposal does not violate the subsidiarity principle and placed the opinion on file.
alternatives: The Riksdag decides not to submit a reasoned opinion and places the opinion on file.
